### AW18. Thesis-Ready Literature Review Paragraph

The literature shows that routing is a mature computational problem but that auditable freight-route recommendation is a different problem. Classical shortest-path algorithms, alternative-path enumeration, and road-network speedups make route computation feasible at scale. Open-source engines and commercial route APIs demonstrate that route delivery, directions, matrices, and fleet optimisation are operationally mature. However, these systems usually present a route or plan as the output. This thesis instead treats the route as a conditional claim. The project asks whether the route remains justified under sampled evidence worlds, whether a hidden challenger could overturn it, whether user preference uncertainty changes the winner, whether more evidence is worth collecting, and whether abstention is the scientifically correct answer. That is the gap the codebase fills.

The project's main methodological contribution is the fusion of route generation, multiobjective evidence, bounded certification, VOI action control, preference ambiguity, typed abstention, and artifact provenance. Each element has a literature base, but the repository combines them into one source-readable applied system. DCCS adapts alternative-path and metareasoning ideas to choose challengers by expected decision impact. REFC adapts robust and stochastic motivation into bounded sampled-world certificates with explicit support limits. VOI-AD2R adapts value-of-information theory into deterministic value-per-cost action scoring over route-specific actions. Typed abstention adapts reject-option thinking into actionable route failure reasons. The run store and docs checks adapt reproducibility principles into the engineering workflow. The system is therefore not a new shortest-path engine; it is a new route-evidence architecture.

The strongest defensible comparison is that WhatIf Freight Router is more inspectable for academic evidence than ordinary route wrappers, scalar route scorers, and black-box commercial optimisers. It fixes the tendency of route systems to return an answer without exposing why that answer is adequately supported. It also fixes the tendency of research prototypes to report a result without preserving enough artifact evidence to audit the claim later. The thesis should make this precise: the project is not globally better than industrial logistics platforms, but it is better aligned with the research aim of producing auditable, conditional, and reproducible freight-route recommendations.

### AW19. Multiobjective Path Literature In More Detail

The multiobjective shortest-path literature is a direct predecessor for the route-frontier part of the project. Martins' multicriteria shortest-path paper established algorithms for nondominated path sets and made the practical point that one scalar criterion is often not enough for road-network decisions [Martins 1984](https://doi.org/10.1016/0377-2217(84)90077-8). More recent multiobjective shortest-path algorithms refine this line of work by improving label-setting, dominance checks, and efficient-path enumeration [Maristany de las Casas, Sedeño-Noda, and Borndörfer 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cor.2021.105424). Approximate Pareto-set research also matters because exact efficient frontiers can be too large for interactive decision support [Papadimitriou and Yannakakis 2000](https://doi.org/10.1145/335305.335335).

The project's deviation is not that it rejects Pareto theory. It uses Pareto filtering as a necessary sanity layer, then adds evidence and preference certification. The standard multiobjective path question is:

```text
Return all efficient paths p where no p' has c(p') <= c(p) componentwise.
```

The project changes that to:

```text
Return the subset of candidates whose decision status is certified, uncertain, or abstained,
and explain which evidence or preference blocker controls that status.
```

That is a real algorithmic change in the output contract. A normal Pareto-frontier algorithm can tell the thesis that route A is not dominated by route B. It cannot, by itself, tell the thesis that route A's nondominance depends on stale toll evidence, that route B is a possible winner under unresolved CO2 preference, or that a third route should be refined because it has high hidden-challenger risk. The project fixes this by treating the Pareto set as an intermediate evidence structure rather than the final decision.

### AW20. Robust Optimisation And Why The Project Uses Bounded Evidence Worlds

Robust optimisation normally protects decisions against uncertain data by optimising under an uncertainty set. Bertsimas and Sim's "price of robustness" is a useful reference because it frames robustness as a tradeoff: more protection usually costs more nominal performance [Bertsimas and Sim 2004](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.1030.0065). Robust combinatorial optimisation surveys also show that min-max and min-max-regret variants are often computationally hard, including shortest-path variants [Aissi, Bazgan, and Vanderpooten 2009](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2008.09.012). Exact robust shortest-path work with interval data reinforces that robust path problems quickly become specialised optimisation problems [Montemanni and Gambardella 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0305-0548(03)00114-X).

The project's design chooses bounded evidence certification instead of pretending to solve a universal robust shortest-path problem. In robust optimisation notation, a common form is:

```text
p_robust = argmin_p max_{c in U} cost(p, c)
```

The project uses a different object:

```text
support(p) = observed stability of p over sampled worlds Omega_hat
certified(p) = support(p) >= threshold and blockers(p) is empty
```

This choice is justified by thesis evidence requirements. A full robust-optimisation claim would require proving that the uncertainty set \(U\) is correct and that the optimisation solved the robust problem. The repository instead records the actual evidence worlds it used, the support state, the confidence calculation, the blockers, and the abstention reason. That makes the claim smaller but more defensible. It also prevents the common overclaim that a route is "robust" when the implementation actually tested only a finite set of scenarios.

### AW21. Sample Average Approximation And Stochastic Routing

Sample average approximation (SAA) is the closest academic analogue for the project's sampled-world evidence logic. SAA approximates an expected stochastic objective using a finite sample and then reasons about the sample solution [Kleywegt, Shapiro, and Homem-de-Mello 2002](https://doi.org/10.1137/S1052623499363220). SAA has also been applied directly to stochastic routing problems [Verweij et al. 2003](https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1021814225969).

The normal SAA objective is:

```text
x_hat_N = argmin_x (1/N) * sum_{i=1..N} F(x, xi_i)
```

WhatIf Freight Router borrows the finite-world idea but changes the goal from "choose the minimum sampled-average route" to "decide whether the current route decision is sufficiently certified". That is why the certificate contains winner support, pairwise gaps, possible/necessary winners, unresolved frontier mass, and abstention blockers rather than only a sampled mean. The project is more suitable for an applied thesis because it exposes the sample boundary:

```text
The claim is about the worlds in the manifest and the support assumptions in the run,
not about every possible future traffic, fuel, toll, carbon, weather, or incident state.
```

This is especially important because freight evidence is not stationary. A route that is certified under a recorded fuel-price snapshot and traffic regime may need a refresh when those evidence families move. The project fixes that by making evidence refresh an action in the VOI controller instead of treating stale evidence as invisible noise.

### AW22. DCCS Candidate-Criticality Equations

DCCS is where the project most clearly changes the academic alternative-route norm. Instead of returning the top \(k\) shortest alternatives, it estimates which unrefined or partially refined candidate can affect the certified decision. The candidate-criticality model includes search-deficiency risk:

```python
search_deficiency_risk = (
    0.45 * (1.0 - objective_gap)
    + 0.25 * overlap
    + 0.30 * near_duplicate
)
```

This looks unusual if read as pure route optimisation, because overlap and near-duplicate status would normally be penalties. In this project they are evidence signals. A near-duplicate with a small objective gap can expose whether the apparent winner is fragile under minor route changes. A high-overlap challenger can also identify whether the decision depends on a small number of uncertain shared segments. The model is therefore not "rewarding duplicates" in the user-facing candidate set; it is deciding whether a candidate has diagnostic value for certification.

The DCCS search-completeness score also adapts routing literature into a certification diagnostic:

```python
search_completeness_gap = (
    unresolved_possible_frontier_mass
    + unresolved_possible_winner_mass
    + unresolved_certificate_critical_mass
) / 3.0
search_completeness_score = 1.0 - search_completeness_gap
```

A normal route engine rarely exposes this because it is not trying to certify a decision boundary. The thesis needs it because an unsearched or weakly refined frontier can invalidate any winner claim. This makes DCCS better aligned with the research target than a static route-alternative list: it measures what remains unknown about the decision, not only what is currently known about route costs.

### AW23. REFC As A Certification Layer Rather Than A New Robust Optimiser

REFC is a route-evidence certification layer. It receives candidate routes, stress/evidence worlds, preference state, and support thresholds, then decides whether the system can certify a singleton, certify a set, continue evidence work, or abstain. This is different from robust optimisation and different from conformal prediction.

The closest equation is:

```text
certificate(r) = {
  winner_lcb(r),
  pairwise_gap_lower_bound_or_support_gap(r, r'),
  possible_winner_mass(r),
  necessary_winner_status(r),
  support_state(r),
  abstention_blockers
}
```

The project uses a winner-support lower confidence bound plus conservative pairwise lower/support gaps because a route should not be certified on the optimistic centre estimate alone. This matches the thesis stance: an auditable route recommendation should require support strong enough to survive reasonable uncertainty, and if that support is absent the system should say why. The difference from conformal prediction is also important. Conformal prediction gives calibrated prediction sets under exchangeability-style assumptions. REFC does not claim that. REFC gives a source-readable support certificate over the evidence worlds, route candidates, and assumptions in the repository.

### AW24. VOI-AD2R Compared With Active Learning And Knowledge Gradient

Active learning often selects the next label or experiment by uncertainty sampling, expected model change, expected error reduction, or query-by-committee disagreement. Knowledge-gradient policies choose measurements by expected value of the post-measurement decision. VOI-AD2R is closer to knowledge-gradient metareasoning than to generic uncertainty sampling, but it is intentionally more engineering-bounded.

The normal expected value of sample information can be written:

```text
EVSI(a) = E_y[max_d E[U(d) | y, a]] - max_d E[U(d)]
```

The project approximates this with route-specific predicted gains:

```text
Q(a) = (
  0.60 * predicted_winner_lcb_gain(a)
  + 0.25 * predicted_gap_lcb_gain(a)
  + 0.15 * predicted_boundary_contraction(a)
  + 0.02 * predicted_radius_or_flip_budget_gain(a)
  + 0.02 * predicted_unresolved_mass_reduction(a)
  + 0.02 * predicted_preference_ambiguity_reduction(a)
) / (action_cost(a) + epsilon)
```

The approximation is justified because the backend does not have an oracle over all future evidence observations. It has concrete actions with known costs and observable effects: refine a candidate, refresh an evidence family, resample worlds, ask a preference question, or stop. This is the right engineering compromise for the thesis. It keeps the action policy explainable and reproducible while retaining the central VOI idea that information should be collected only when it is expected to change the decision enough to justify its cost.

### AW25. Commercial APIs, Academic Algorithms, And The Better-For-This-Thesis Claim

The strongest wording for the thesis is not "my system beats commercial routing". The defensible wording is: this system is better for auditable applied research because it exposes decision evidence that route APIs and commercial planners do not expose, in their public API/documentation, as the same repo-local proof objects and replayable artifacts. Google Routes provides routing, Google Route Optimization supports fleet/job optimisation, HERE Tour Planning supports tour-planning workflows, ArcGIS and PTV support mature network-analysis or tour-planning workflows, and OSRM, openrouteservice, and GraphHopper provide strong open or API-accessible routing infrastructure. The thesis project fixes a different issue: after a route is returned, the code can explain whether that route should be trusted under the exact evidence state.

The comparison can be written as a precise claim:

```text
Existing route systems optimise or serve routes.
WhatIf Freight Router audits the route decision boundary.
```

That sentence is important because it avoids a false product race. The project is publishable-style work if framed as a decision-evidence architecture, not if framed as a global route-engine replacement. Its novelty is the integration of candidate-critical search, sampled evidence certification, action-valued refresh control, preference ambiguity, typed abstention, and reproducibility ledgers into one local freight-routing system.

### AW26. Literature Review Paragraphs For The Final Paper

A final paper can say that classical routing algorithms provide the computational base but not the evidence contract required for auditable freight decision support. Dijkstra, A*, Yen, Eppstein, contraction hierarchies, customizable route planning, OSRM, openrouteservice, and GraphHopper show how route candidates can be generated efficiently. Multiobjective shortest-path literature explains why a single travel-time objective is insufficient. Robust and stochastic optimisation explain why uncertain costs cannot be ignored. Eco-routing, pollution-routing, and freight-emissions standards explain why route choice should account for fuel, load, grade, carbon, and model scope rather than treating emissions as a cosmetic add-on. VOI, metareasoning, active learning, and preference elicitation explain why evidence and preference questions should be selected by decision value. Selective-decision literature explains why refusal can be rational. Reproducibility literature explains why every thesis claim needs traceable artifacts.

The project contributes by changing the endpoint of routing. Instead of returning a route as if it were self-justifying, the system returns a decision package. The package contains alternatives, objective evidence, support state, confidence summaries, preference ambiguity, VOI actions, abstention reasons, and artifact references. This fixes the main weakness of simple route wrappers and scalar scorers: they often give an answer without preserving the reasons why that answer is safe, unsafe, incomplete, or unsupported. It also fixes a weakness of many research prototypes: they report conclusions without enough operational machinery to rerun, inspect, and maintain the evidence chain.

The contribution should be described as grounded but ambitious. It is grounded because it uses known route-search and decision-analysis foundations, names its assumptions, and records negative results. It is ambitious because it combines these foundations into a system that treats route recommendation as a certified, conditional, evidence-bearing decision. That combination is the strongest thesis story.

## Appendix AX: Deep Literature Crosswalk, Code Evidence, And Equation-Level Novelty

This appendix extends Appendix AW with more external sources and more code-level evidence. It is written for a thesis examiner who wants to know exactly which standard algorithms are being used, which parts are inherited from the literature, which parts are project-specific adaptations, and why the adaptation is better for the specific thesis problem. The claim remains bounded: the project is not a universal replacement for industrial routing, full VRP optimisation, conformal prediction, regulatory emissions modelling, or theorem-complete robust optimisation. It is a more inspectable and better targeted architecture for auditable freight-route recommendation under incomplete search, uncertain evidence, and incomplete preferences.

### AX1. Shortest Path, Constrained Path, And Why The Route Is Not The Final Answer

The classical route-search baseline is still the shortest-path problem. Dijkstra solves a nonnegative scalar edge-cost problem [Dijkstra 1959](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01386390), A* adds heuristic guidance [Hart, Nilsson, and Raphael 1968](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1968.300136), and k-shortest path work extends a single path into a ranked sequence of alternatives [Yen 1971](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.17.11.712), [Eppstein 1998](https://doi.org/10.1137/S0097539795290477). Constrained shortest-path work shows what happens when one objective is optimised while another acts as a side constraint [Handler and Zang 1980](https://doi.org/10.1002/net.3230100403), [Hassin 1992](https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.17.1.36). In freight routing, these constraints are not abstract: a route may be cheap only if time, emissions, support, vehicle legality, or preference constraints are ignored.

The standard scalar problem is:

```text
p* = argmin_{p in P(s,t)} sum_{e in p} c_e
```

The constrained form is closer to:

```text
p* = argmin_p sum_e cost_e
subject to sum_e time_e <= T, sum_e emissions_e <= C, vehicle_constraints(p) = true
```

The project changes the endpoint again:

```text
route_search_output = {candidate paths}
thesis_output = {
  selected route or certified set or typed abstention,
  candidate-criticality ledger,
  evidence-world support,
  preference ambiguity,
  VOI action trace,
  artifact provenance
}
```

That is the central reason this system is stronger for thesis evidence than a shortest-path implementation alone. A shortest path is a computed object. A thesis route recommendation is an argued claim. The code therefore keeps bounded search as an input to certification rather than allowing the first good route to become the answer.

The implementation evidence is the bounded Dijkstra/A* and Yen-style generator in `backend/app/k_shortest.py`. It is not presented as new graph theory; it is the controlled candidate generator for the later evidence system:

```python
def _dijkstra_shortest_path(
    *,
    adjacency: dict[str, tuple[tuple[str, float], ...]],
    start: str,
    goal: str,
    banned_nodes: set[str] | None = None,
    banned_edges: set[tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
    max_hops: int = 220,
    explored_counter: list[int] | None = None,
    max_state_budget: int | None = None,
    max_repeat_per_node: int = 1,
    max_cost_limit: float | None = None,
    transition_state_fn: TransitionStateFn | None = None,
    heuristic_fn: HeuristicFn | None = None,
    deadline_monotonic_s: float | None = None,
) -> PathResult:
    ...
```

The project modification is visible in the parameters. `max_hops`, `max_state_budget`, `max_repeat_per_node`, `max_cost_limit`, transition-state functions, heuristic functions, and monotonic deadlines make search auditably bounded. A conventional shortest-path paper often assumes the graph problem is the object. This project uses the graph problem as a candidate-production subroutine whose incompleteness can be surfaced later as search deficiency.

### AX2. Multiobjective Shortest Paths And Why The Project Does Not Trust A Single Scalar Score

Multiobjective shortest-path work is directly relevant because road arcs can carry time, money, emissions, risk, and operational support at once. Martins' multicriteria shortest-path work explains why a single arc cost is insufficient for road-network problems [Martins 1984](https://doi.org/10.1016/0377-2217(84)90077-8). More recent multiobjective shortest-path work improves label-setting and targeted search [Maristany de las Casas et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cor.2021.105424), and dynamic multiobjective variants show why costs can depend on time and context [Maristany de las Casas et al. 2021 dynamic MOSP](https://doi.org/10.3390/a14020043). Lexicographic goal-based MOSP also matters because a decision maker may be interested only in a bounded portion of a large frontier [Mandow and Pérez-de-la-Cruz 2010](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2009.09.018), [Pulido, Mandow, and Pérez-de-la-Cruz 2014](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2014.05.008).

The academic Pareto relation is:

```text
a dominates b iff a_i <= b_i for every objective i
and a_i < b_i for at least one objective i.
```

The repository implements exactly that minimisation relation in tuple space with a tolerance:

```python
def dominates(a: tuple[float, ...], b: tuple[float, ...], *, tol: float = 1e-9) -> bool:
    if len(a) != len(b):
        raise ValueError("dimension mismatch")
    le_all = True
    lt_any = False
    for ai, bi in zip(a, b, strict=True):
        if ai > bi + tol:
            le_all = False
            break
        if ai < bi - tol:
            lt_any = True
    return le_all and lt_any
```

The project-specific move is what happens after this. A pure MOSP algorithm would aim to enumerate efficient paths. WhatIf Freight Router treats the nondominated frontier as evidence, not as a complete recommendation. A nondominated route can still be uncertified if evidence is stale, if a hidden challenger remains plausible, if the preference set still permits another winner, or if the route sits outside support. This fixes a weakness in many multiobjective route demos: they correctly show a frontier but do not explain which frontier member is safe to recommend.

### AX3. Epsilon Constraints, Crowding Distance, And Knee Points As Export Controls

The epsilon-constraint method is a classic way to turn a multiobjective problem into a constrained single-objective problem [Haimes, Lasdon, and Wismer 1971](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSMC.1971.4308298). NSGA-II crowding distance is a standard way to preserve spread among nondominated solutions [Deb et al. 2002](https://doi.org/10.1109/4235.996017). Knee-point literature explains that decision makers often care about frontier regions where small improvement in one objective causes large deterioration in another [Branke et al. 2004](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-30217-9_73).

The repository uses all three ideas, but not as a generic evolutionary optimiser. It uses them as export controls for small, inspectable route sets:

```python
def filter_by_epsilon(
    options: list[RouteOption],
    epsilon: EpsilonConstraints | None,
    objective_key: Callable[[RouteOption], tuple[float, ...]] | None = None,
) -> list[RouteOption]:
    if epsilon is None:
        return options

    filtered: list[RouteOption] = []
    for route in options:
        duration_s = float(route.metrics.duration_s)
        monetary_cost = float(route.metrics.monetary_cost)
        emissions_kg = float(route.metrics.emissions_kg)
        if epsilon.duration_s is not None and duration_s > epsilon.duration_s:
            continue
        if epsilon.monetary_cost is not None and monetary_cost > epsilon.monetary_cost:
            continue
        if epsilon.emissions_kg is not None and emissions_kg > epsilon.emissions_kg:
            continue
        filtered.append(route)
    return filtered
```

This differs from a textbook epsilon-constraint treatment because the bounds are not hidden inside an optimiser. They remain visible in the request and artifacts. That is better for the thesis because a reader can see whether a route disappeared because it was dominated, because it violated a hard physical bound, or because later certification rejected it.

The same design appears in crowding truncation:

```python
def _truncate_pareto_with_crowding(
    routes: list[RouteOption],
    *,
    max_alternatives: int,
    objective_key: Callable[[RouteOption], tuple[float, ...]],
) -> list[RouteOption]:
    if len(routes) <= max_alternatives:
        return list(routes)
    objectives = [objective_key(route) for route in routes]
    crowding = _crowding_distances(objectives)
    ranked_indices = sorted(
        range(len(routes)),
        key=lambda idx: (
            0 if math.isinf(crowding[idx]) else 1,
            -(crowding[idx] if not math.isinf(crowding[idx]) else float("inf")),
            objectives[idx],
            routes[idx].id,
        ),
    )
    selected_indices = ranked_indices[:max_alternatives]
    selected = [routes[idx] for idx in selected_indices]
    return sorted(selected, key=lambda option: (*objective_key(option), option.id))
```

The academic norm is to preserve diversity in an optimisation population. The project changes this into a reviewer-facing cap: keep a small number of alternatives, but make them spread out enough that the later proof panels are not just showing same-corridor duplicates. This is stronger than returning the first `k` alternatives because the capped set keeps objective-space contrast.

The knee heuristic is also deliberately labelled as a heuristic rather than a theorem:

```python
score = math.sqrt(
    sum((_norm(values[idx], mins[idx], maxs[idx]) ** 2) for idx in range(dim_count))
)
knee_route_id = min(scores, key=lambda item: (item[0], item[1].metrics.duration_s, item[1].id))[1].id
```

This is not a canonical knee detector. It is a closest-to-ideal marker that helps the UI and report explain a compromise route. The benefit is inspectability: the project does not hide a "best" route behind a vague recommendation label. It records why the route is a compromise candidate, and then still requires certification.

### AX4. MCDM Methods And The Modified VIKOR/TOPSIS/AHP Boundary

Multiple-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods such as TOPSIS [Hwang and Yoon 1981](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-48318-9), VIKOR [Opricovic and Tzeng 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(03)00020-1), AHP [Saaty 1980](https://doi.org/10.21236/ADA214804), and ELECTRE outranking [Roy 1968](https://doi.org/10.1051/ro/196802V100571) are relevant because they explain how human decision-makers can rank alternatives under multiple criteria. Keeney and Raiffa give the deeper multiattribute utility foundation [Keeney and Raiffa 1993](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139174084).

The normal weighted utility form is:

```text
U(r; w) = w_time T(r) + w_money M(r) + w_co2 C(r) + w_risk R(r)
```

The repo does not reject that form, but it refuses to let it be the whole decision. A scalar score can rank alternatives even when the evidence is unsupported or the user's weights are arbitrary. The project instead layers MCDM-style scoring underneath certification:

```text
rank_score(r) may identify a useful candidate,
but certified_decision(r) also requires support, gap, preference, and abstention checks.
```

This is a key "better than the norm" claim. TOPSIS and VIKOR are useful for compromise ranking, but a route thesis needs more than compromise. It needs to know whether a compromise is supported by evidence. AHP can structure weight elicitation, but it does not by itself prove that the selected route survives hidden challenger risk or stale fuel evidence. ELECTRE can express outranking, but it does not materialise this repository's evidence-world certificate or VOI action trace. The project fixes those gaps by preserving the MCDM layer as one part of a larger evidence contract.

### AX5. DCCS As A Decision-Critical Alternative To K-Shortest Enumeration

K-shortest path enumeration answers "what is the next path in the scalar order?" DCCS answers "which candidate is most likely to change the decision or the certificate if refined?" This is a project-specific adaptation of route enumeration, multiobjective diversity, and metareasoning.

The actual DCCS challenger score makes this visible:

```python
gain = (
    (config.objective_gap_weight * record.objective_gap)
    + (config.mechanism_gap_weight * record.mechanism_gap * support_gate)
    + (config.challenger_gain_weight * record.flip_probability * support_gate)
    + (0.25 * (1.0 - record.overlap))
    + (config.challenger_time_preservation_weight * record.time_preservation_bonus * time_bonus_scale)
    + (config.challenger_candidate_criticality_weight * criticality_score)
    + (config.challenger_expected_proxy_value_weight * record.expected_proxy_value)
    + (config.challenger_expected_audit_value_weight * record.expected_audit_value)
    + (config.challenger_preference_sensitivity_weight * record.preference_query_sensitivity)
    + (config.challenger_possible_best_change_weight * record.changes_possible_best_probability)
    + (config.challenger_necessary_best_change_weight * record.changes_necessary_best_probability)
    + (config.challenger_search_completeness_weight * record.search_completeness_contribution)
    + (config.challenger_hidden_challenger_weight * record.hidden_challenger_risk)
)
penalty = (
    (config.overlap_penalty_weight * record.overlap)
    + (config.stretch_penalty_weight * max(0.0, record.stretch - 1.0))
    + (config.cost_weight * record.predicted_refine_cost)
)
return gain / max(1e-9, penalty)
```

This is stronger than pure k-shortest enumeration for the thesis because it exposes what the candidate is for. The candidate may be useful because it is close on objectives, comes from a different mechanism, has high flip probability, stresses search completeness, or could change possible/necessary-best preference status. It may be less useful because it overlaps heavily, stretches too much, or costs too much to refine. In other words, the score is not route quality; it is expected decision value under incomplete search.

### AX6. Time-Dependent Routing And The Evidence-Refresh Difference

Time-dependent routing is a mature topic. Orda and Rom study shortest paths with time-dependent edge lengths [Orda and Rom 1990](https://doi.org/10.1145/79147.214078). Malandraki and Daskin formulate time-dependent vehicle routing [Malandraki and Daskin 1992](https://doi.org/10.1287/trsc.26.3.185), and Ichoua, Gendreau, and Potvin model vehicle dispatching with time-dependent travel times [Ichoua, Gendreau, and Potvin 2003](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(02)00147-9). Later work on real-time re-planning shows how live travel-time changes can disrupt existing plans [Gmira et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trc.2021.103379).

The project does not claim to solve the full time-dependent VRP. Its adaptation is evidence-state aware routing:

```text
time-dependent routing norm: edge travel time depends on departure time.
repo adaptation: evidence families can be fresh, stale, proxy, missing, or unsupported,
and the decision can request refresh or abstain instead of silently using a time estimate.
```

This fixes a thesis weakness in ordinary time-dependent route outputs. A travel-time value can be numerically precise but evidentially weak. WhatIf Freight Router records whether the time-sensitive evidence was strong enough to certify the decision, and if not the route result becomes conditional or abstained rather than falsely authoritative.

### AX7. Robust Optimisation, SAA, And Why REFC Does Not Overclaim Robustness

Robust optimisation begins from uncertainty sets and protection against all values in those sets [Soyster 1973](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.21.5.1154), [Ben-Tal and Nemirovski 1998](https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.23.4.769), [Ben-Tal, El Ghaoui, and Nemirovski 2009](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400831050). Stochastic programming and sample average approximation (SAA) work from finite scenario samples [Kleywegt, Shapiro, and Homem-de-Mello 2002](https://doi.org/10.1137/S1052623499363220), [Shapiro, Dentcheva, and Ruszczynski 2021](https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611976595), [Verweij et al. 2003](https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1021814225969). Bertsimas and Sim make the robustness tradeoff explicit through the "price of robustness" [Bertsimas and Sim 2004](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.1030.0065).

The robust norm is:

```text
x* = argmin_x max_{u in U} f(x, u)
```

The SAA norm is:

```text
x_N = argmin_x (1/N) sum_{i=1..N} F(x, xi_i)
```

The project's REFC stance is:

```text
do not claim x* for all U;
certify or refuse over the evidence worlds and support assumptions actually recorded.
```

The implementation reflects that stance through decision-region and flip-radius scaffolding rather than a universal robust optimum:

```python
certified = bool(
    support_flag
    and winner_point >= threshold_value
    and has_positive_gap
    and has_positive_budget
)
```

This is better for thesis defensibility because it prevents a common robust-routing overclaim. A route can be stable in the checked evidence worlds without being globally robust to every possible future state. The repo says exactly that and gives the reviewer a reason when the certificate is not closed.

### AX8. Confidence Bounds: Hoeffding, Confidence Sequences, And The Conservative Implementation

Hoeffding's inequality is the classical bounded-random-variable concentration result [Hoeffding 1963](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1963.10500830). Modern time-uniform work develops confidence sequences that remain valid under optional stopping [Howard et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1214/20-AOS1991), [Howard et al. preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.08240). Empirical Bernstein bounds can be tighter when variance is informative [Maurer and Pontil 2009](https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.3740). Conformal prediction gives distribution-free predictive sets under exchangeability assumptions [Vovk, Gammerman, and Shafer 2005](https://www.alrw.net/), [Shafer and Vovk 2008](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/papers/volume9/shafer08a/shafer08a.pdf).

The project intentionally uses a conservative anytime-Hoeffding style bound:

```python
def anytime_hoeffding_interval(
    *,
    success_count: int,
    sample_count: int,
    delta: float,
) -> ConfidenceInterval:
    delta_n = delta / (sample_count * (sample_count + 1))
    radius = math.sqrt(math.log(2.0 / delta_n) / (2.0 * sample_count))
    center = success_count / sample_count
    return ConfidenceInterval(
        lower=max(0.0, center - radius),
        upper=min(1.0, center + radius),
        center=center,
        radius=radius,
    )
```

The project modification is practical and thesis-facing. Instead of claiming a sophisticated empirical-Bernstein or conformal guarantee that the code does not implement, it uses a simple union-bound schedule and labels the method. That is better for the thesis because it is auditable and conservative. The downside is wider intervals. The upside is that the report can honestly explain exactly why the winner support lower bound is cautious.

### AX9. CVaR, Entropic Risk, And Thesis-Specific Tail Penalties

CVaR is a standard tail-risk measure in optimisation [Rockafellar and Uryasev 2000](https://doi.org/10.21314/JOR.2000.038). In transport, tail risk matters because a route with good mean cost can still be unacceptable if adverse worlds cause large delay, cost, or emission spikes.

The repository implements empirical CVaR by integrating the tail quantile and then uses a risk-family wrapper:

```python
def robust_objective(
    *,
    mean_value: float,
    cvar_value: float | None,
    risk_aversion: float,
    risk_family: str = "cvar_excess",
    risk_theta: float = 1.0,
) -> float:
    if cvar_value is None:
        return float(mean_value)
    tail_excess = max(0.0, float(cvar_value) - float(mean_value))
    risk = max(0.0, float(risk_aversion))
    family = str(risk_family or "cvar_excess").strip().lower()
    if family == "entropic":
        theta = max(1e-6, float(risk_theta))
        penalty = math.log1p(risk * math.expm1(theta * tail_excess)) / theta
        return float(mean_value) + penalty
    if family == "downside_semivariance":
        scale = max(1.0, abs(float(mean_value)))
        penalty = (tail_excess * tail_excess) / scale
        return float(mean_value) + (risk * penalty)
    return float(mean_value) + (risk * tail_excess)
```

The code comments already mark `entropic` and `downside_semivariance` as thesis-specific penalties on CVaR excess rather than canonical full-distribution risk measures. This is better than silently borrowing the names of risk measures and pretending they are exact. The thesis can say: the implementation uses CVaR correctly for empirical tail summaries, and it offers named engineering penalties for route scoring while explicitly refusing to overclaim those penalties as textbook risk measures.

### AX10. Freight Emissions, PRP, Green VRP, And Model-Scope Honesty

The Pollution-Routing Problem connects fuel, load, speed, emissions, and route choice [Bektaş and Laporte 2011](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trb.2011.02.004). Green vehicle-routing work extends routing to fuel and alternative-fuel constraints [Erdogan and Miller-Hooks 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tre.2011.08.001), while green VRP reviews show how broad the field has become [Moghdani et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2020.123691), [Asghari and Al-e-hashem 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijpe.2020.107899). Eco-routing studies show that fuel and emissions depend on speed, grade, congestion, and vehicle characteristics [Ericsson, Larsson, and Brundell-Freij 2006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trc.2006.10.001), [Ahn and Rakha 2013](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trd.2013.09.006), [Boriboonsomsin and Barth 2009](https://doi.org/10.3141/2139-03).

The project adapts this literature into transparent route-level evidence rather than a full PRP/Green-VRP solver. The code derives speed from actual segment duration, clamps to calibration surfaces, and keeps regional multipliers explicit:

```python
speed_kmh = (distance_km / (duration_s / 3600.0)) if duration_s > 0 else 0.0
grade_pct = float(grade) * 100.0
klass = _vehicle_class(vehicle, emissions_context)
load_factor = _derived_load_factor(vehicle, klass=klass)
load_factor = _clamp(load_factor, consumption_surface.axes.load_factor[0], consumption_surface.axes.load_factor[-1])
speed_value = _clamp(speed_kmh, consumption_surface.axes.speed_kmh[0], consumption_surface.axes.speed_kmh[-1])
grade_value = _clamp(grade_pct, consumption_surface.axes.grade_pct[0], consumption_surface.axes.grade_pct[-1])
region_mult = _regional_multiplier(snapshot.regional_multipliers, lat=route_centroid_lat, lon=route_centroid_lon)
```

The terrain calculation is similarly transparent:

```python
rolling_force = params.mass_kg * G_MPS2 * params.c_rr
aero_force = 0.5 * AIR_DENSITY_KG_M3 * params.drag_area_m2 * (v_ms ** 2)
grade_force = params.mass_kg * G_MPS2 * grade
baseline_force = max(250.0, rolling_force + aero_force)
raw_force = rolling_force + aero_force + max(grade_force, -0.85 * baseline_force)
uplift = raw_force / baseline_force
```

The improvement over black-box emissions scoring is not regulatory superiority. The improvement is traceability. HBEFA [HBEFA methodology](https://www.hbefa.net/en/methodology), COPERT [COPERT methodology](https://copert.emisia.com/copert/methodology/), MOVES [USEPA 2024, MOVES5](https://www.epa.gov/moves/latest-version-motor-vehicle-emission-simulator-moves), ISO 14083 [ISO 14083](https://www.iso.org/standard/78864.html), DESNZ conversion factors [DESNZ 2025](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/greenhouse-gas-reporting-conversion-factors-2025), and GLEC-style logistics carbon accounting [Smart Freight Centre GLEC Framework](https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3.2_21_10_25_1.pdf) give important context. This repository is informed by that context but does not claim formal compliance with those standards.

### AX11. VOI, Metareasoning, And Action-Valued Evidence Control

Howard's value-of-information theory links information to decision value [Howard 1966](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1966.300074). Horvitz develops computation/action tradeoffs under bounded resources [Horvitz 1990](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/computation-action-bounded-resources/). Russell and Wefald formalise metareasoning as selecting computations by expected value [Russell and Wefald 1991](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(91)90015-C). Knowledge-gradient work gives a related measurement-selection principle [Frazier, Powell, and Dayanik 2009](https://doi.org/10.1287/ijoc.1080.0314).

The repo's VOI controller is not exact global VOI. It is a deterministic myopic value-per-cost controller over actions the system can actually perform:

```text
standard EVSI: E_y[max_d E[U(d) | y, a]] - max_d E[U(d)]
repo Q(a): predicted certificate/margin/frontier/preference gain per action cost
```

The exact implemented score is:

```python
q_score = (
    (cfg.lambda_certificate * predicted_winner_lcb_gain(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_margin * predicted_gap_lcb_gain(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_frontier * predicted_boundary_contraction(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_radius_or_flip_budget * predicted_radius_or_flip_budget_gain(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_unresolved_mass * predicted_unresolved_mass_reduction(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_preference_ambiguity * predicted_preference_ambiguity_reduction(scored_action))
) / (cost + cfg.epsilon)
```

The improvement is domain alignment. Generic active learning may chase uncertainty that does not matter to the route decision. This controller asks whether an action moves the certificate, the margin, the frontier, the flip radius, unresolved mass, or preference ambiguity. It is better for the thesis because every action has a route-decision reason.

### AX12. Active Learning And Preference Elicitation As Typed Decision Updates

Active learning selects useful observations rather than collecting everything [MacKay 1992](https://doi.org/10.1162/neco.1992.4.4.590), [Cohn, Ghahramani, and Jordan 1996](https://doi.org/10.1613/jair.295), [Freund et al. 1997](https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1007330508534), [Settles 2009](https://burrsettles.com/pub/settles.activelearning_20090109.pdf). Preference elicitation asks for utility information only when it is decision-relevant [Chajewska, Koller, and Parr 2000](https://cdn.aaai.org/AAAI/2000/AAAI00-056.pdf), [Wang and Boutilier 2003](https://research.google/pubs/incremental-utility-elicitation-with-the-minimax-regret-decision-criterion/), [Boutilier et al. 2006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2006.02.003), [Viappiani and Boutilier 2010](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/3943-optimal-bayesian-recommendation-sets-and-myopically-optimal-choice-query-sets).

The project does not ask free-text preferences and hope they can be interpreted later. It defines typed query payloads:

```python
PreferenceQueryType = Literal["pairwise", "threshold", "ratio", "veto", "time_guard"]

class PairwisePreferenceQuery(BaseModel):
    query_type: Literal["pairwise"] = "pairwise"
    preferred_route_id: str
    challenger_route_id: str
    reason: str | None = None
    weight_hint: dict[str, float] = Field(default_factory=dict)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _validate_distinct_routes(self) -> "PairwisePreferenceQuery":
        if self.preferred_route_id == self.challenger_route_id:
            raise ValueError("pairwise preference routes must be distinct")
        return self
```

It also enforces monotone shrinkage:

```python
if after_size_int > before_size_int:
    raise ValueError("valid preference updates cannot increase compatible set size")
if after_volume_value > before_volume_value + 1e-12:
    raise ValueError("valid preference updates cannot increase compatible-set volume")
```

This is stronger than a normal route preference slider. A slider can make a route look precise even when the user has not resolved a decision-critical ambiguity. Typed queries let the repo record what was asked, why it was asked, how the compatible set changed, and whether a contradiction was detected. The improvement over generic active learning is that the query target is not model accuracy; it is route-decision certification.

### AX13. Selective Prediction, Reject Options, And Typed Abstention

Reject-option classification begins with the idea that a model should sometimes refuse to classify [Chow 1970](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406). Modern selective classification develops this idea for predictive systems [El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/papers/v11/el-yaniv10a.html), [Geifman and El-Yaniv 2017](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/7073-selective-classification-for-deep-neural-networks). Conformal prediction supplies calibrated prediction sets under exchangeability, but the repo does not claim conformal validity.

The project changes the reject option into typed route-decision abstention:

```text
classifier norm: abstain if confidence is too low.
repo norm: abstain with a route-specific blocker:
search, evidence, preference, support, budget, or model assumption.
```

That is more useful than a single "low confidence" flag because each blocker implies a different remedy. Search failure calls for candidate expansion. Evidence failure calls for evidence refresh. Preference failure calls for a query. Out-of-support failure calls for refusing extrapolation. Budget failure says no further action is available under the current limits. This is better for a thesis because it explains the failure mode instead of hiding it behind one probability.

### AX14. Decision Regions And Flip Radius As Route-Specific Stability Evidence

The project includes route-level stability objects that are inspired by robustness and adversarial-sensitivity ideas but are not claimed as universal adversarial robustness theorems. A decision region stores the nearest certificate boundary and the active challenger:

Publication citation bridge: flip radius should be described as a decision-stability diagnostic inspired by margin and sensitivity analysis. Margin methods in statistical learning made distance-to-boundary a central explanation for stability and generalisation [Cortes and Vapnik 1995](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00994018), while adversarial-sensitivity work shows how small input perturbations can flip model decisions [Goodfellow, Shlens, and Szegedy 2015](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6572). The repo's flip-radius surface is route-specific and evidence-bounded: it asks how close a route decision is to a certification or challenger boundary under the maintained evidence model, not whether the whole system is certifiably adversarially robust.

```python
nearest_boundary, nearest_axis = choose_decision_boundary(
    support_flag=support_flag,
    active_challenger_id=active_challenger_id,
    minimum_pairwise_gap=minimum_pairwise_gap,
    minimum_flip_budget=minimum_flip_budget_value,
    preference_direction=("certificate_margin" if nearest_pairwise is not None else None),
    dominant_evidence_family=getattr(flip_radius_state, "dominant_fragility_family", None),
)
```

The structured adversarial budget separates evidence, preference, and search deficiency:

```python
return StructuredAdversarialBudget(
    evidence_channel=evidence_channel,
    preference_channel=preference_channel,
    search_deficiency_channel=search_deficiency_channel,
    limiting_channel=limiting_channel,
    limiting_budget=limiting_budget,
    provenance=dict(provenance or {}),
)
```

The academic norm would often present one robustness radius or one uncertainty set. The repo's adaptation is better for route-decision explanation because it says which channel is limiting. A fragile route can be fragile because of evidence, because a user preference can flip it, or because search incompleteness leaves challengers alive. Those are different scientific claims.

Publication citation bridge: add MCDA robustness and sensitivity framing so flip radius is not read only as a machine-learning margin analogy. MCDA sensitivity analysis studies how criterion weights and alternative performances can alter deterministic rankings [Triantaphyllou and Sanchez 1997](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-5915.1997.tb01306.x), while Roy frames robustness in decision aiding as a response to ignorance and model mismatch [Roy 2010](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2008.12.036). The repo's pairwise gaps, runner-up gaps, and typed limiting channels fit this decision-aiding tradition: they expose how much evidence, preference, or search movement is needed before the recommended route becomes unstable.

### AX15. Commercial Systems: What They Solve And What This Thesis Adds

Commercial and open systems define the practical baseline. OSRM provides high-performance OSM routing [OSRM documentation](https://project-osrm.org/docs/v26.4.0/). openrouteservice exposes routing/geospatial APIs over OSM-derived infrastructure [openrouteservice endpoints](https://giscience.github.io/openrouteservice/api-reference/endpoints/). GraphHopper exposes routing, matrices, route optimisation, geocoding, and map matching [GraphHopper API documentation](https://docs.graphhopper.com/openapi). Google Routes provides routing [Google Routes](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes), while Google Route Optimization solves fleet/job optimisation problems [Google Route Optimization](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/route-optimization/overview). HERE Tour Planning solves VRP-like tour-planning workflows [HERE Tour Planning](https://docs.here.com/tour-planning/docs/introduction-tour-planning). ArcGIS provides a Vehicle Routing Problem analysis layer [ArcGIS VRP layer](https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/latest/tool-reference/network-analyst/make-vehicle-routing-problem-analysis-layer.htm). PTV xTour provides tour-planning APIs [PTV xTour](https://api.cloud.ptvgroup.com/manual/Content/API-Documentation/xtour/API_Documentation.html). Trimble/PC*Miler exposes truck-routing reports, PC*Miler practical miles, directions, trip cost, and detailed paths [Trimble Route Reports](https://developer.trimblemaps.com/restful-apis/routing/route-reports/overview/). Descartes Route Planner targets complex route planning and dynamic optimisation [Descartes Route Planner](https://www.descartes.com/resources/knowledge-center/descartes-route-planner). Transporeon focuses on transport execution, visibility, planning, and carrier assignment [Transporeon Transport Execution](https://www.transporeon.com/en/platform/transport-execution-visibility-hub).

The thesis comparison should be written carefully:

```text
Commercial systems are broader and more operationally mature.
WhatIf Freight Router is narrower but more inspectable as a local evidence artifact.
```

That is not a weak claim. It is the correct claim. These systems can optimise tours, expose routing APIs, support carriers, and execute logistics workflows. What they generally do not expose in public documentation is this repository's local proof object: DCCS candidate ledgers, sampled-world certificate summaries, VOI action traces, preference shrinkage traces, typed abstention classes, generated artifact manifests, theorem-map claim boundaries, and docs consistency gates. This project is more appropriate for the thesis because the examiner can trace the decision from code to artifact to report.

### AX16. Reproducibility, FAIR, And Why The Report Itself Is Part Of The Method

Reproducibility is not an afterthought. FAIR principles explain why research objects should be findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable [Wilkinson et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18). Reproducible computational research requires code, data, workflow, and negative-result discipline [Peng 2011](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1213847), [Wilson et al. 2014](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.1001745), [Sandve et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285). This project adapts those principles to a route-decision system.

The important adaptation is that the report is not merely commentary. It is a master evidence index. The backend emits artifacts, the docs checker enforces local links and endpoint parity, the theorem map bounds formal claims, and the negative-results documents prevent claim boundaries from being rewritten as success. That is better than a notebook-only thesis because a reviewer can check whether a claim points to a real generated file, a source module, a test surface, or only an aspiration.
