### AX18. The Safe High-Level Claim After Adding These Sources

The literature review should now make a confident but bounded claim. The project uses established foundations such as shortest paths, Pareto dominance, VIKOR, CVaR, value of information, conformal-prediction comparators, green VRP, and route optimisation, then turns those ingredients into a local route-decision evidence contract. Its thesis contribution is stronger than a path/frontier/score/plan output because it returns a decision state that can be certified, challenged, refreshed, preference-qualified, abstained, and replayed.

That is the core applied contribution: route recommendation becomes an auditable object rather than an opaque endpoint response.

### AX19. Deeper K-Shortest-Path Literature And The Project's Search-Adequacy Deviation

The shortest-path literature is much broader than the usual Dijkstra/A*/Yen summary. Dreyfus' survey is important because it already treated the second, third, and later shortest paths, time-dependent travel times, and via-node requirements as variants of the same route-search family rather than separate problems [Dreyfus 1969](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.17.3.395). Lawler's k-best framework generalises the idea of enumerating ordered alternatives across discrete optimisation problems [Lawler 1972](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.18.7.401). Modern k-shortest-simple-path work focuses on improving the time and space behaviour of exact enumeration [Hershberger, Maxel, and Suri 2007](https://doi.org/10.1145/1290672.1290682), and recent experimental algorithmics still treats k-shortest simple paths as an active engineering problem [Al Zoobi, Coudert, and Nisse 2023](https://doi.org/10.1145/3626567).

Those papers answer an algorithmic question: how can the first `k` simple paths be enumerated correctly and efficiently? The thesis problem is different. The thesis needs to know whether the candidate-generation stage was good enough for a downstream decision. That is why the project keeps path-search statistics and explicit failure modes alongside the first alternatives returned by routing support:

```python
return tuple(shortest), {
    "explored_states": int(explored_counter[0]),
    "generated_candidates": int(generated_candidates),
    "pruned_constraints": int(pruned_constraints),
    "termination_reason": termination_reason,
    "no_path_reason": (
        ""
        if shortest
        else normalize_no_path_reason(first_error or termination_reason)
    ),
    "first_error": first_error,
}
```

This is a deliberate deviation from ordinary k-shortest output. A normal k-shortest API can return `k` paths with no explanation of whether the search stopped because it succeeded, because the candidate pool exhausted, because a deadline fired, or because state budget limits blocked exploration. The repository makes those reasons part of the decision evidence. That is better for the thesis because a route can be rejected or abstained for incomplete search instead of being silently treated as the best available answer.

The actual bounded search also encodes operational compromises that many algorithm papers abstract away:

```python
if max_state_budget is not None and max_state_budget > 0 and explored_counter is not None:
    if explored_counter[0] >= max_state_budget:
        raise PathNotFoundError("state budget exceeded")
...
if max_cost_limit is not None and new_cost > max_cost_limit:
    continue
...
if max_candidate_pool is not None and max_candidate_pool > 0 and len(candidates) > max_candidate_pool:
    candidates = heapq.nsmallest(max_candidate_pool, candidates)
    heapq.heapify(candidates)
```

Academic shortest-path work often analyses asymptotic correctness under a specified problem model. This project has to operate as a thesis artifact under finite runtime, finite memory, live API failure, user-facing report size, and repeatability constraints. `max_state_budget`, `max_cost_limit`, `max_candidate_pool`, `deadline_monotonic_s`, and the explicit `termination_reason` are therefore not incidental parameters. They convert an algorithmic subroutine into an auditable evidence-producing component.

The modified contribution can be written as:

```text
standard KSP: compute ordered paths P_1, ..., P_k
repo KSP: compute bounded paths plus adequacy metadata A
certification input: (P_1, ..., P_m, A), where A can later block certification
```

That is why the implementation is better for this project than simply delegating all candidate generation to an external route API. External engines may be faster or more geographically complete, but they normally do not expose this exact adequacy object inside the thesis repository.

### AX20. Multiobjective Search Beyond Pareto: Labels, Heuristics, And Why This Project Avoids Frontier Worship

Bicriterion and multiobjective shortest-path research shows why route search becomes hard as soon as each edge has more than one cost. Hansen's bicriterion path work gives early complexity and algorithmic structure for two-criterion paths [Hansen 1980](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-48782-8_9). Skriver and Andersen show how label-correcting algorithms can be made faster for bicriterion shortest paths with domination conditions [Skriver and Andersen 2000](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0305-0548(99)00037-4). Mandow and Perez-de-la-Cruz extend A* ideas into multiobjective heuristic search through NAMOA* [Mandow and Perez-de-la-Cruz 2010](https://doi.org/10.1145/1754399.1754400).

The repository uses the same conceptual foundation: route quality is vector-valued. Its contribution then goes beyond Pareto enumeration. That matters because "frontier worship" is a common weakness in applied multiobjective projects: a system shows a nice nondominated set and then leaves the actual decision unresolved. The project explicitly treats the frontier as a candidate surface to be interrogated by support, preference, confidence, and VOI.

The thesis contrast is:

```text
multiobjective path norm:
  enumerate labels or approximate the efficient frontier

WhatIf Freight Router:
  expose candidate frontier, then ask:
    is the selected route supported?
    is the pairwise gap stable?
    can hidden challengers flip the winner?
    do incomplete preferences still allow another route?
    is the next best action to search, refresh, ask, resample, stop, or abstain?
```

This is a stronger applied design than returning a Pareto plot because the thesis problem is not "can a frontier be generated?" The thesis problem is "can a route decision be justified under incomplete information?" The code therefore combines Pareto filtering with later route-specific state rather than claiming that nondominance equals recommendation.

### AX21. Scalarisation, VIKOR, Tchebycheff, And The Modified Route-Selection Formula

Weighted sums and scalarisation are standard tools in multiobjective optimisation. Marler and Arora discuss why weighted sums are attractive but limited when the Pareto front is nonconvex or weights are hard to interpret [Marler and Arora 2010](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00158-009-0460-7). Augmented Tchebycheff methods are used because they can target nondominated compromise points more reliably than a plain weighted sum in some settings [Steuer and Choo 1983](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02591870). VIKOR ranks compromise alternatives using a mixture of group utility and individual regret [Opricovic and Tzeng 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(03)00020-1), with later comparative work clarifying how VIKOR differs from TOPSIS and outranking approaches [Opricovic and Tzeng 2007](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2006.01.020).

The standard VIKOR shape is:

```text
S_i = sum_j w_j (f_j(i) - f_j*) / (f_j^- - f_j*)
R_i = max_j w_j (f_j(i) - f_j*) / (f_j^- - f_j*)
Q_i = v (S_i - S*) / (S^- - S*) + (1 - v) (R_i - R*) / (R^- - R*)
```

The repository preserves baseline formulas through explicit math profiles, then adds a deliberately engineered profile for route choice:

```python
if math_profile == "academic_reference":
    score = weighted_sum
elif math_profile == "academic_tchebycheff":
    score = weighted_regret + (tchebycheff_rho * weighted_sum)
elif math_profile == "academic_vikor":
    score = vikor_q
elif math_profile == "modified_vikor_distance":
    score = (
        vikor_q
        + (balance_weight * balance_penalty)
        + (distance_weight * n_distance)
        + (eta_distance_weight * eta_distance_penalty)
        + (knee_weight * knee_penalty)
        - (entropy_weight * entropy_reward)
        + time_preservation_penalty
    )
```

This is a critical thesis example because it shows exactly how the academic norm was changed. `academic_reference`, `academic_tchebycheff`, and `academic_vikor` are retained as named baselines. The project's default `modified_vikor_distance` adds route-domain penalties and rewards:

```text
modified score =
  VIKOR compromise
  + balance penalty
  + distance penalty
  + ETA-distance interaction penalty
  + knee imbalance penalty
  - entropy reward for multi-objective improvement spread
  + backend time-preservation penalty
```

The route-selection parameters are also visible in settings. The default profile is `modified_vikor_distance`; `route_selection_modified_regret_weight` is retained for the `modified_hybrid` and fallback profiles rather than being applied inside the default VIKOR-distance branch:

```python
route_selection_math_profile: str = Field(default="modified_vikor_distance")
route_selection_modified_regret_weight: float = Field(default=0.35, ge=0.0, le=2.0)
route_selection_modified_balance_weight: float = Field(default=0.10, ge=0.0, le=2.0)
route_selection_modified_distance_weight: float = Field(default=0.22, ge=0.0, le=2.0)
route_selection_modified_eta_distance_weight: float = Field(default=0.18, ge=0.0, le=2.0)
route_selection_modified_entropy_weight: float = Field(default=0.08, ge=0.0, le=2.0)
route_selection_modified_knee_weight: float = Field(default=0.12, ge=0.0, le=2.0)
route_selection_tchebycheff_rho: float = Field(default=0.001, ge=0.0, le=0.1)
route_selection_vikor_v: float = Field(default=0.5, ge=0.0, le=1.0)
```

These values are not magic constants. The thesis justification is:

- `VIKOR_V = 0.5` keeps the compromise exactly balanced between group utility and worst-objective regret instead of biasing toward majority utility or max-regret avoidance.
- `tchebycheff_rho = 0.001` keeps the augmented weighted-sum term as a tie-breaking perturbation rather than letting it dominate max-regret behaviour.
- `balance_weight = 0.10` and `knee_weight = 0.12` make imbalance visible without overturning the main VIKOR score.
- `distance_weight = 0.22` and `eta_distance_weight = 0.18` encode a freight-routing reality: two routes with similar time/money/CO2 can differ in operational plausibility because extra distance increases exposure to congestion, evidence drift, and route complexity.
- `entropy_weight = 0.08` rewards improvements that are spread across objectives, discouraging a highlighted route from being chosen purely because it wins one objective while degrading the others. It is still only one term in the scalar score, so it biases the ranking rather than proving a one-objective-heavy route can never win.
- all route-selection weights are bounded with `ge=0.0, le=2.0`, so environment tuning cannot silently create extreme, unreviewable scalarisation behaviour.

This is better than a plain TOPSIS/VIKOR/AHP deployment for the thesis because it keeps the academic baselines available, names the engineering extensions, and then still refuses to treat the resulting scalar score as certification. A route can win `modified_vikor_distance` and still fail evidence support or preference stability.

### AX22. Robust Shortest Path And Why The Project Uses Bounded Evidence Worlds Instead Of A Universal Minimax Claim

Robust optimisation offers a natural comparison because freight-route metrics are uncertain. Bertsimas, Brown, and Caramanis survey robust optimisation as a modelling approach for optimisation under uncertainty [Bertsimas, Brown, and Caramanis 2011](https://doi.org/10.1137/080734510). Kouvelis and Yu give a robust discrete-optimisation framework that is especially relevant to combinatorial decisions [Kouvelis and Yu 1997](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4757-2620-6). Robust shortest-path variants with interval data can be computationally hard [Zielinski 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(03)00373-4), and exact robust shortest-path algorithms depend on the chosen uncertainty and regret model [Montemanni and Gambardella 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0305-0548(03)00114-X).

The mathematical robust shortest-path ideal is:

```text
p* = argmin_p max_{c in U} cost(p, c)
```

The repository does not claim to solve that for every possible road-cost uncertainty set. It uses bounded, replayable evidence worlds:

```python
def compute_certificate(
    routes: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
    *,
    worlds: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
    selector_weights: tuple[float, float, float] = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0),
    threshold: float = 0.67,
    active_families: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    ...
) -> CertificateResult:
    # Winner frequency over the bounded world set is used as a sample-average
    # robustness certificate for the fixed selector, not as a posterior
    # probability claim about the unknown global optimum.
```

The project is better for its thesis goal because it avoids a false theorem. A commercial route system may say "optimised" and a robust-optimisation paper may prove a minimax property under a specific uncertainty set. This project says exactly what its certificate means: winner frequency over a bounded world manifest under recorded evidence families, selector settings, support state, and threshold. That is less grand than universal robustness, but more scientifically honest and more reproducible.

The world manifest is deterministic rather than uncontrolled Monte Carlo:

```python
digest = hashlib.sha1(f"{seed}|{idx}|{family}|{','.join(states)}".encode("utf-8")).digest()
threshold = (int.from_bytes(digest[:8], "big") % 1_000_000) / 1_000_000.0
...
payload["manifest_hash"] = _stable_hash([
    json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), default=str)
])
```

This deviation matters. Ordinary stochastic evaluation can be hard to replay if random draws, live evidence, and code versions are not tied together. The manifest hash means the stress-world set is part of the evidence. A thesis examiner can ask whether a route won because of an actual evidence-world set, not because of an undocumented random seed or an API state that no longer exists.

### AX23. Risk Measures, CVaR, Quantiles, And The Project's Tail-Risk Adaptation

Risk measures are another place where the report needs careful citation. Artzner, Delbaen, Eber, and Heath introduced coherent risk-measure axioms [Artzner et al. 1999](https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9965.00068). Acerbi and Tasche explain expected shortfall as a coherent alternative to value-at-risk [Acerbi and Tasche 2002](https://doi.org/10.1111/1468-0300.00091). Rockafellar and Uryasev made CVaR optimisation computationally tractable through an optimisation formulation [Rockafellar and Uryasev 2000](https://doi.org/10.21314/JOR.2000.038). Hyndman and Fan matter because even quantile definitions differ across statistical packages [Hyndman and Fan 1996](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.1996.10473566).

The repository explicitly fixes the quantile convention:

```python
# Use the Hyndman-Fan type-7 sample quantile convention:
pos = q_clamped * (len(ordered) - 1)
lo = int(math.floor(pos))
hi = int(math.ceil(pos))
if lo == hi:
    return ordered[lo]
t = pos - lo
return ordered[lo] + ((ordered[hi] - ordered[lo]) * t)
```

It then computes empirical CVaR by integrating the tail quantile function:

```python
tail_integral = 0.0
for start, end in zip(knots, knots[1:], strict=False):
    q_start = quantile(ordered, start)
    q_end = quantile(ordered, end)
    tail_integral += 0.5 * (q_start + q_end) * (end - start)

denom = max(1e-12, 1.0 - alpha_clamped)
result = tail_integral / denom
threshold = quantile(ordered, alpha_clamped)
return max(result, threshold)
```

The standard CVaR idea is:

```text
CVaR_alpha(X) = E[X | X >= VaR_alpha(X)]    for suitable continuous loss distributions
```

The repository adaptation is:

```text
route_tail_score =
  empirical type-7 tail quantile integral
  over finite sampled route utility values
```

The risk objective then keeps the default conservative and transparent:

```python
tail_excess = max(0.0, float(cvar_value) - float(mean_value))
if family == "entropic":
    penalty = math.log1p(risk * math.expm1(theta * tail_excess)) / theta
    return float(mean_value) + penalty
if family == "downside_semivariance":
    penalty = (tail_excess * tail_excess) / scale
    return float(mean_value) + (risk * penalty)
return float(mean_value) + (risk * tail_excess)
```

The comments in the code are important evidence because they avoid overclaiming:

```python
# This is a thesis-specific entropic-style tail penalty, not the
# canonical entropic risk measure on the full loss distribution.
...
# This is a thesis-specific quadratic penalty on CVaR excess, not the
# textbook downside semivariance definition over centered tail losses.
```

This is better than just importing a finance risk formula because route utility is not a liquid portfolio return. The repo needs a tail-risk signal that can be explained for sampled freight-route worlds. The adaptation says: penalise the excess of tail utility over mean utility, keep the calculation dimensionless, and label nonstandard risk families as thesis-specific. That gives the thesis a defensible risk story without pretending to solve portfolio-theory CVaR optimisation.

### AX24. Confidence Sequences, Optional Stopping, And Why The Project Uses Conservative Winner Support

Hoeffding's bounded-sum inequality is the baseline for simple finite-sample concentration [Hoeffding 1963](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1963.10500830). Modern confidence-sequence work gives tighter and more general anytime-valid tools [Howard et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1214/20-AOS1991). The repository deliberately uses a conservative Hoeffding union-bound sequence instead of a more complex empirical-Bernstein or mixture boundary:

```python
def anytime_hoeffding_interval(
    success_count: int,
    sample_count: int,
    *,
    delta: float = DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE_DELTA,
) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Return a conservative anytime-valid Bernoulli interval.

    The construction uses Hoeffding's inequality with a summable time schedule
    ``delta_n = delta / (n (n + 1))``. By a union bound over all ``n >= 1``,
    the interval is valid uniformly over optional stopping times.
    """
    ...
    log_term = math.log((2.0 * n * (n + 1)) / delta_value)
    radius = math.sqrt(max(0.0, log_term) / (2.0 * n))
    return max(0.0, empirical - radius), min(1.0, empirical + radius)
```

The exact implemented bound is:

```text
delta_n = delta / (n(n+1))
radius_n = sqrt(log(2n(n+1)/delta) / (2n))
LCB_n = max(0, p_hat_n - radius_n)
UCB_n = min(1, p_hat_n + radius_n)
```

This is conservative, but that conservatism is a design choice. More advanced methods could be tighter, but they would add assumptions and complexity that are not necessary for the thesis objective. The project is evaluating a bounded sampled-world winner frequency, not proving a distribution-free prediction set for future road states.

That boundary is especially important because conformal prediction is a tempting but incorrect overclaim here. Conformal prediction gives distribution-free predictive coverage under exchangeability [Lei et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2017.1307116), and weighted conformal prediction extends the idea under covariate shift assumptions [Tibshirani et al. 2019](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/8522-conformal-prediction-under-covariate-shift). The repository does not claim exchangeability, calibrated future traffic coverage, or conformal validity. It uses typed abstention and bounded evidence support instead. That is a better thesis claim because it is true for the implementation.

### AX25. VOI, Bounded Rationality, And Why The Controller Stops Instead Of Searching Forever

Value of information begins with the expected value of an experiment or observation [Lindley 1956](https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177728069), [Howard 1966](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1966.300074). Bounded-rationality work explains why real decision systems must act under limited time and computation [Simon 1955](https://doi.org/10.2307/1884852), and bounded-optimal-agent theory gives the AI version of that resource-constrained view [Russell and Subramanian 1995](https://doi.org/10.1613/jair.133). Decision-theoretic active learning adds the idea that labels or measurements should be selected by expected decision value rather than generic uncertainty [Kapoor, Horvitz, and Basu 2007](https://www.ijcai.org/Proceedings/07/Papers/141.pdf).

The repo's VOI configuration is therefore part of the thesis design, not arbitrary plumbing:

```python
class VOIConfig:
    certificate_threshold: float = 0.67
    stop_threshold: float = 0.02
    search_budget: int = 3
    evidence_budget: int = 2
    max_iterations: int = 8
    top_k_refine: int = 2
    resample_increment: int = 25
    lambda_certificate: float = 0.60
    lambda_margin: float = 0.25
    lambda_frontier: float = 0.15
    lambda_radius_or_flip_budget: float = 0.02
    lambda_unresolved_mass: float = 0.02
    lambda_preference_ambiguity: float = 0.02
    epsilon: float = 1e-9
    near_tie_threshold: float = 0.03
    search_completeness_threshold: float = 0.84
    search_completeness_action_bonus: float = 0.22
    evidence_uncertainty_threshold: float = 0.08
```

The tuning is defensible:

- `certificate_threshold = 0.67` means the winner needs at least roughly two-thirds bounded-world support before the controller treats it as certificate material. This is high enough to reject weak plurality winners, but not so high that every uncertain freight choice becomes impossible.
- `stop_threshold = 0.02` prevents the controller from spending budget on actions with negligible predicted decision value.
- `search_budget = 3`, `evidence_budget = 2`, and `max_iterations = 8` make the controller bounded-rational. It can improve the evidence state, but it cannot search forever.
- `lambda_certificate = 0.60` dominates because the main thesis objective is certification, not curiosity.
- `lambda_margin = 0.25` makes pairwise winner-gap improvement important because a supported winner with a tiny margin is fragile.
- `lambda_frontier = 0.15` keeps frontier contraction relevant without letting UI frontier neatness dominate certificate support.
- the small `0.02` weights for flip radius, unresolved mass, and preference ambiguity keep secondary signals alive without overwhelming the main certificate and margin terms.
- `search_completeness_threshold = 0.84` and `search_completeness_action_bonus = 0.22` ensure incomplete search can actively trigger refinement instead of being buried under evidence scores.

The action score is:

```python
q_score = (
    (cfg.lambda_certificate * predicted_winner_lcb_gain(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_margin * predicted_gap_lcb_gain(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_frontier * predicted_boundary_contraction(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_radius_or_flip_budget * predicted_radius_or_flip_budget_gain(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_unresolved_mass * predicted_unresolved_mass_reduction(scored_action))
    + (
        cfg.lambda_preference_ambiguity
        * predicted_preference_ambiguity_reduction(scored_action)
    )
) / (cost + cfg.epsilon)
```

The standard EVSI expression is:

```text
EVSI(a) = E_y [ max_d E[U(d) | y, a] ] - max_d E[U(d)]
```

The repo's practical version is:

```text
Q(a) =
  weighted predicted certificate, margin, frontier, robustness,
  unresolved-mass, and preference-ambiguity gain
  divided by explicit action cost
```

This is better than generic active learning because it asks only for actions that can change the route decision. A label or refresh that improves model accuracy but cannot change certificate support, route margin, search completeness, or preference ambiguity is not worth much in this controller.

The stop rule is equally important:

```python
while state.iteration_index < cfg.max_iterations:
    ...
    current_certificate = _as_float(state.certificate.get(state.winner_id, certificate_value))
```

The surrounding controller logic certifies if the threshold is cleared, otherwise acts only while feasible actions have value above the stop threshold and budget remains. This is a thesis-level improvement over "keep refining until it looks good" because the stop condition is inspectable, finite, and replayable.

### AX26. Preference Elicitation, Regret, And Necessary/Possible Winner Evidence

Preference elicitation literature is relevant because a freight route can be better under one user's weights and worse under another's. Minimax-regret elicitation asks for preference information that reduces worst-case decision loss [Wang and Boutilier 2003](https://research.google/pubs/incremental-utility-elicitation-with-the-minimax-regret-decision-criterion/), and constraint-based elicitation can select queries based on regret or decision impact [Boutilier et al. 2006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2006.02.003), [Braziunas and Boutilier 2007](https://www.cs.toronto.edu/~cebly/Papers/BraziunasBoutilier_uai07-abs.html). Necessary and possible winner concepts from computational social choice are useful analogies because they separate alternatives that must win from those that can still win under incomplete information [Konczak and Lang 2005](https://www.eecs.harvard.edu/cs286r/courses/fall11/papers/KL05.pdf), [Xia and Conitzer 2011](https://doi.org/10.1613/jair.3186).

The repository does not solve a complete continuous minimax-regret optimisation problem. It implements a route-decision approximation: query types are structured, updates record compatible-set evidence, and route-level possible/necessary winner fields are stored as inspected evidence summaries rather than theorem-complete winner proofs. The code makes query semantics explicit:

```python
PreferenceQueryType = Literal["pairwise", "threshold", "ratio", "veto", "time_guard"]
```

When before/after compatible-set summaries are supplied, the update rule enforces non-increasing evidence rather than allowing a preference answer to expand the recorded compatible set:

```python
if after_size_int > before_size_int:
    raise ValueError("valid preference updates cannot increase compatible set size")
if after_volume_value > before_volume_value + 1e-12:
    raise ValueError("valid preference updates cannot increase compatible-set volume")
```

This supports the intended thesis equation when the compatible-set state is present:

```text
C_{t+1} ~= C_t intersect constraint(answer_t)
|C_{t+1}| <= |C_t|
volume(C_{t+1}) <= volume(C_t)
```

The `~=` matters. The implementation can also append query history or update weights without proving a full continuous preference-space intersection. The improvement over ordinary preference sliders is that every answer has an audit trail. A slider value can be changed without preserving what ambiguity it resolved. Here, the query type, route ids, answer, compatible-set shrinkage evidence when available, contradiction state, and terminal decision state remain visible. That is why this design is better for a thesis about evidence than a generic weight panel.

The necessary/possible winner phrasing is:

```text
necessary-best in this repo:
  route is marked necessary under the inspected compatible preference evidence

possible-best in this repo:
  route remains possible under the inspected preference evidence and stored summaries

non-claim:
  existential proof over all compatible preference completions, or exact theorem-complete
  enumeration over all continuous utility functions
```

This caveat strengthens the work. It shows the thesis understands the academic norm and does not pretend that a practical FastAPI backend has solved the full social-choice or utility-elicitation problem.

### AX27. Typed Abstention As A Route-Decision Reject Option With Remedies

Reject-option classification gives the baseline idea: a system should sometimes refuse to make a prediction [Chow 1970](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406). Selective classification develops this into a confidence/coverage tradeoff [El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/papers/v11/el-yaniv10a.html), [Geifman and El-Yaniv 2017](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/7073-selective-classification-for-deep-neural-networks). Post-selection inference also warns that evidence can be distorted if the analysis ignores how a decision was selected [Fithian, Sun, and Taylor 2014](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.2597).

The repo changes the generic reject option into a route-specific diagnostic object:

```python
TypedAbstentionReason = Literal[
    "typed_abstention_recommended",
    "uncertified_due_to_search",
    "uncertified_due_to_evidence",
    "uncertified_due_to_preference",
    "uncertified_due_to_out_of_support_world_model",
    "uncertified_due_to_budget",
    "uncertified_due_to_model_assumption",
]
```

Each reason has a remedy:

```python
return {
    "typed_abstention_recommended": "expand_worlds",
    "uncertified_due_to_search": "expand_search",
    "uncertified_due_to_evidence": "refresh_evidence",
    "uncertified_due_to_preference": "ask_preference",
    "uncertified_due_to_out_of_support_world_model": "expand_world_model",
    "uncertified_due_to_budget": "increase_budget",
    "uncertified_due_to_model_assumption": "review_model_assumptions",
}[self.reason_code]
```

That is a significant applied improvement. A classifier-style abstention usually says "do not know". This route system says why the recommendation cannot be certified and what kind of action would be needed next. Search, evidence, preference, support, budget, and model-assumption failures are scientifically different. The thesis can therefore discuss failed certifications as meaningful results rather than treating them as missing outputs.

### AX28. Freight Emissions Standards And Why The Project Claims Transparency Rather Than Regulatory Replacement

The freight-emissions literature and standards ecosystem is large, and it positions the implementation precisely. The Pollution-Routing Problem shows how load, speed, distance, and fuel use enter routing objectives [Bektas and Laporte 2011](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trb.2011.02.004). The green vehicle routing problem supplies a foundational alternative-fuel routing model [Erdogan and Miller-Hooks 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tre.2011.08.001), while later green-VRP surveys and reviews show that emissions-aware routing has many variants and constraints [Moghdani et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2020.123691), [Asghari and Al-e-hashem 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijpe.2020.107899). Eco-routing studies also show that fuel and emissions depend on speed, road grade, congestion, and vehicle characteristics [Ahn and Rakha 2013](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trd.2013.09.006), [Boriboonsomsin and Barth 2009](https://doi.org/10.3141/2139-03). Operational emission models and standards such as HBEFA, COPERT, MOVES, ISO 14083, UK DESNZ conversion factors, and GLEC are the proper comparators for formal emissions accounting [HBEFA methodology](https://www.hbefa.net/en/methodology), [COPERT methodology](https://copert.emisia.com/copert/methodology/), [USEPA 2024, MOVES5](https://www.epa.gov/moves/latest-version-motor-vehicle-emission-simulator-moves), [ISO 14083](https://www.iso.org/standard/78864.html), [DESNZ conversion factors 2025](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/greenhouse-gas-reporting-conversion-factors-2025), [Smart Freight Centre 2025, GLEC Framework v3.2](https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3.2_21_10_25_1.pdf).

The project's safe claim is:

```text
not: this replaces HBEFA, COPERT, MOVES, ISO 14083, or GLEC accounting
yes: this exposes route-level emissions evidence inside the decision package
```

That distinction is crucial. Formal emissions models are broader and more validated. The project's advantage is transparency and decision integration. It puts the emissions calculation beside route candidates, preference tradeoffs, uncertainty, support state, and artifact provenance. A route is not merely "lower CO2" in a UI label; its emissions component participates in scalarisation, Pareto vectors, risk summaries, and certification evidence.

The implementation can be explained with the same structure as the academic formulas:

```text
PRP / eco-routing norm:
  fuel = f(distance, speed, load, road grade, vehicle parameters)
  emissions = fuel * emission_factor

repo adaptation:
  emissions evidence is route-level, normalised for utility,
  stress-tested in evidence worlds,
  and never claimed as a regulator-grade inventory model.
```

That is better for this thesis than using a black-box emissions API alone. A black-box API might be more accurate for a jurisdiction, but it would not automatically explain how the emissions value affected certification, VOI, preference ambiguity, and abstention.

### AX29. Commercial Route Systems And The Narrow But Strong Thesis Claim

Commercial/open systems are the obvious "why did you not just use X?" alternatives. OSRM is a high-performance routing engine [Project OSRM 2026, OSRM v26.4.0 API docs](https://project-osrm.org/docs/v26.4.0/). openrouteservice provides directions and route APIs with routing options and extra info [openrouteservice Directions Service](https://giscience.github.io/openrouteservice/api-reference/endpoints/directions/). GraphHopper exposes route, matrix, optimisation, and custom-model capabilities [GraphHopper Routing API](https://docs.graphhopper.com/openapi/routing). Google Routes provides route computation [Google Routes API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes), and Google Route Optimization plans fleet routes with time, cost, and capacity constraints [Google Route Optimization API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/route-optimization/overview). HERE Tour Planning covers vehicle-routing variants including capacity, time windows, multi-depot, open VRP, heterogeneous fleet, pickup/delivery, priorities, territories, shifts, and reloads [HERE Tour Planning API](https://docs.here.com/tour-planning/docs/introduction-tour-planning). ArcGIS provides GIS-integrated VRP tooling [ArcGIS VRP layer](https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/latest/tool-reference/network-analyst/make-vehicle-routing-problem-analysis-layer.htm). PTV xTour provides tour-planning APIs [PTV xTour](https://api.cloud.ptvgroup.com/manual/Content/API-Documentation/xtour/API_Documentation.html). Trimble PC*Miler exposes commercial-vehicle route and mileage APIs [Trimble PC*Miler](https://developer.trimble.com/docs/pc-miler/) and route reports [Trimble Route Reports](https://developer.trimblemaps.com/restful-apis/routing/route-reports/overview/). ORTEC and Descartes are operational comparators for routing, dispatch, and route optimisation [ORTEC Vehicle Routing](https://ortec.com/en/solutions/vehicle-routing), [Descartes Route Planner](https://www.descartes.com/resources/knowledge-center/descartes-route-planner). Transporeon is a broader transport-management, execution, visibility, and collaboration comparator rather than a route-engine comparator [Transporeon](https://www.transporeon.com/en).

This thesis does not claim broad operational superiority over those systems. Taken collectively, this comparator set includes systems that are stronger for enterprise coverage, live traffic, fleet dispatch, legal truck constraints, commercial support, and integration. The correct claim is narrower and stronger:

```text
commercial systems are better operational products;
WhatIf Freight Router is the better thesis evidence artifact.
```

It is better for thesis evidence because the repo exposes:

- source-readable route-selection math instead of only API responses;
- DCCS candidate-criticality records instead of opaque alternative generation;
- bounded evidence-world manifests instead of undocumented stochastic state;
- winner support, confidence bounds, and support flags instead of a single ranked route;
- typed preference queries and shrinkage traces instead of unlogged preference tweaks;
- typed abstention reasons instead of generic failure messages;
- theorem-map and negative-result boundaries instead of promotional product claims;
- docs checks and artifact indices that make the generated results inspectable.

This is the right publishable framing. The contribution is not "I built a better Google Maps". The contribution is "I built a local, inspectable route-decision certification architecture that turns routing outputs into auditable evidence objects."

### AX30. Final Literature-Backed Claim With Equations And Code-Level Differences

The thesis can now make a precise, well-cited argument:

```text
1. Classical routing gives paths.
2. Multiobjective routing gives frontiers.
3. MCDM gives scalar rankings.
4. Robust/stochastic optimisation gives uncertainty-aware objectives.
5. VOI and active learning give action selection.
6. Selective prediction gives abstention.
7. Reproducible research gives artifact discipline.

WhatIf Freight Router combines these into:
  certified_route_decision =
    route candidates
    + frontier evidence
    + modified route scalarisation
    + bounded evidence-world support
    + conservative winner confidence
    + preference-compatible-set state
    + VOI action trace
    + typed abstention
    + reproducibility artifacts
```

The code-level changes from academic norms are specific:

```text
standard shortest path:
  p* = argmin_p sum_e c_e

repo:
  bounded candidates + search adequacy metadata,
  where inadequacy can block certification
```

```text
standard VIKOR:
  Q = v*S_scaled + (1-v)*R_scaled

repo:
  Q_route = Q
    + balance
    + distance
    + ETA-distance
    + knee imbalance
    - entropy improvement spread
```

```text
standard robust optimisation:
  argmin_x max_{u in U} f(x,u)

repo:
  certificate over deterministic bounded evidence-world manifest,
  with no posterior/global-optimum overclaim
```

```text
standard CVaR:
  tail conditional expectation or optimisation objective

repo:
  type-7 empirical tail integral over route utility samples
  + labelled thesis-specific tail penalties
```

```text
standard active learning:
  ask for labels that reduce model uncertainty

repo:
  ask/refresh/search/resample only when predicted decision value per cost is positive
```

```text
standard reject option:
  abstain when confidence is low

repo:
  abstain with typed route-specific reason and recommended remedy
```

This is why the project can be described as better than the alternatives for the stated research problem. It is not better at every task. It is better at preserving enough evidence for a thesis reader to understand why a freight-route decision was made, why it might fail, what evidence supports it, what assumptions limit it, and what action would improve it.

### AX31. Published-Paper Argument Inventory: Everything The Paper Needs To Say Explicitly

A publishable paper built from this repository must make its contribution legible as a decision-support architecture. The mature claim is that freight routing is treated as a multi-layer evidence problem: a path candidate is generated, stress-tested, compared under multiple objectives, checked against preference ambiguity, exposed through confidence/support records, and either certified or rejected with a typed remedy. That statement connects classic shortest-path algorithms, vehicle-routing research, multi-criteria decision analysis, robust optimization, value-of-information control, selective prediction, eco-routing, and reproducible software engineering into one applied systems artifact.

The paper's opening problem statement can cite shortest-path foundations such as Dijkstra's algorithm [Dijkstra 1959](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01386390), K-shortest loopless paths [Yen 1971](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.17.11.712), and road-network route-planning surveys [Bast et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-49487-6_2). Those sources establish that computing a route is a mature problem. The harder thesis problem is not "can a path be found?" but "can a freight route recommendation be justified when objectives conflict, data sources disagree, and the decision maker's tradeoffs are not fully known?" Multiobjective shortest-path literature [Martins 1984](https://doi.org/10.1016/0377-2217(84)90077-8), multi-attribute decision making [Hwang and Yoon 1981](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-48318-9), VIKOR compromise ranking [Opricovic and Tzeng 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(03)00020-1), robust optimization [Ben-Tal and Nemirovski 1998](https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.23.4.769), [Bertsimas and Sim 2004](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.1030.0065), and selective prediction [Chow 1970](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406) support that harder framing.

The paper should be explicit that the system does not replace commercial routing engines or full fleet optimizers. Vehicle-routing work begins with the truck dispatching problem [Dantzig and Ramser 1959](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.6.1.80), savings heuristics [Clarke and Wright 1964](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.12.4.568), and exact/branch-price-cut VRP methods [Toth and Vigo 2002](https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9780898718515), [Costa, Contardo, and Desaulniers 2019](https://doi.org/10.1287/trsc.2018.0878). Google OR-Tools provides a generic solver for VRP variants [OR-Tools routing](https://developers.google.com/optimization/routing) and a published routing-solver description [OR-Tools vehicle routing solver](https://research.google/pubs/or-tools-vehicle-routing-solver-a-generic-constraint-programming-solver-with-heuristic-search-for-routing-problems/). The repository is not trying to beat those systems at fleet-scale depot scheduling. It is solving a different research gap: a single OD freight route decision can be made auditable, preference-aware, uncertainty-aware, and reproducible without hiding the evidence in a black-box service.

The key contribution sentence for a paper can therefore be:

```text
WhatIf Freight Router converts route computation into certified route-decision evidence:
candidate paths are not final answers; they are inspectable alternatives whose
multiobjective scores, uncertainty worlds, preference compatibility, confidence
state, VOI actions, and abstention reasons are stored as reviewer-readable artifacts.
```

This framing is stronger than saying "the route is better" because it is falsifiable. A reviewer can inspect the route candidates, the scoring parameters, the evidence-world manifest, the confidence sequence, the preference-state summary, and the abstention record. That is the publishable artifact: a route decision whose support and limitations are as visible as the route line itself.

### AX32. Vehicle-Routing Literature Boundary: Why This Is Not An Exact VRP Paper

The freight-routing literature gives an obvious challenge: a reviewer may ask why the project does not formulate the whole problem as a vehicle routing problem. The correct answer is that VRP and this repo have different decision objects. Classical VRP optimizes a set of vehicle tours serving multiple customers under capacity, depot, time-window, and resource constraints. The original VRP was posed for gasoline truck dispatch [Dantzig and Ramser 1959](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.6.1.80). Clarke and Wright's savings heuristic is a constructive method for depot-to-customer tour savings [Clarke and Wright 1964](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.12.4.568). Modern exact VRP algorithms use branch-and-bound, branch-and-cut, branch-price-and-cut, set partitioning, column generation, and problem-specific valid inequalities [Toth and Vigo 2002](https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9780898718515), [Baldacci et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2011.07.037), [Costa, Contardo, and Desaulniers 2019](https://doi.org/10.1287/trsc.2018.0878).

This repository's unit of analysis is not a fleet tour set. It is a route-decision record for a specific origin-destination movement, with evidence attached to the decision. That is why the report must not claim "solves VRP". It should say that the project sits next to VRP work: it can feed route-cost/evidence objects into higher-level logistics planning, but its direct research object is certification of one freight-route recommendation under ambiguous objectives and evidence. This is also why exact VRP methods are not the right baseline for the main contribution. Exact VRP methods are excellent when the objective is tour optimality over many stops. They do not, by themselves, produce typed evidence about why a single route was certified, what preference query would help, or why the system abstained.

The code reflects this boundary through candidate-level evidence rather than depot-tour constraints. `DCCSConfig` does not define vehicle capacity, customer service, depot return, or time-window feasibility. It defines search budget, candidate diversity, overlap penalties, objective support, preference sensitivity, and hidden-challenger/search-completeness signals:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DCCSConfig:
    mode: str = "bootstrap"
    pipeline_variant: str = "dccs"
    search_budget: int = 3
    bootstrap_seed_size: int = 2
    near_duplicate_threshold: float = 0.82
    objective_gap_weight: float = 1.0
    mechanism_gap_weight: float = 0.45
    overlap_penalty_weight: float = 1.25
    bootstrap_coverage_weight: float = 1.00
    bootstrap_diversity_weight: float = 0.75
    challenger_search_completeness_weight: float = 0.18
    challenger_hidden_challenger_weight: float = 0.12
```

That snippet is central for the paper. It shows that the project optimizes evidence usefulness under a bounded route-candidate budget, not fleet-wide delivery optimality. A fleet optimizer would normally ask "which tours minimize fleet cost?" This project asks "which route candidates must be refined so that a certified single-route decision is defensible?" That is a narrower problem, but the narrowness is a strength for an applied thesis because it enables precise evidence objects, readable failure reasons, and direct audit traces.

### AX33. Algorithm-Engineering Boundary: Why Fast Road Routing Engines Are Comparators, Not The Contribution

Road routing engines use decades of algorithm engineering to return paths quickly on large networks. Dijkstra's algorithm is the baseline single-source shortest-path method [Dijkstra 1959](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01386390). A* adds goal-directed search with heuristics [Hart, Nilsson, and Raphael 1968](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1968.300136). Contraction Hierarchies add preprocessing shortcuts for extremely fast road-network queries [Geisberger et al. 2008](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68552-4_24). Bast and coauthors survey the broader road-network route-planning field, including hierarchical, goal-directed, and transit-node methods [Bast et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-49487-6_2). OSRM, GraphHopper, openrouteservice, Google Routes, HERE, ArcGIS, PTV, and Trimble all exist in that operational ecosystem.

The paper should concede that those engines are better at production-scale route serving. The repo's contribution is not a faster shortest-path kernel. It is a certification wrapper around route alternatives. That distinction matters because otherwise reviewers will compare the wrong thing. OSRM and GraphHopper are excellent path services; they do not, by default, expose a theorem-map-style evidence ledger, confidence sequence, preference-compatible set, VOI trace, and typed abstention record for a thesis reviewer.

The implementation makes this boundary visible by turning route-source disagreement and source diversity into evidence-control signals. When the origin-destination case is ambiguous, the backend can preemptively seed comparator candidates only when ambiguity, source support, and corridor coverage justify the extra cost:

```python
support_ratio = max(0.0, min(1.0, _as_float_or_zero(req.od_ambiguity_support_ratio)))
source_entropy = max(0.0, min(1.0, _as_float_or_zero(req.od_ambiguity_source_entropy)))

if ambiguity_strength >= settings.route_dccs_preemptive_comparator_min_ambiguity:
    comparator_trigger_reasons.append("ambiguity")
    if support_ratio >= 0.55:
        strong_trigger_reasons.append("ambiguity_supported")

if engine_disagreement_prior >= settings.route_dccs_preemptive_comparator_min_engine_disagreement:
    comparator_trigger_reasons.append("engine_disagreement")
    strong_trigger_reasons.append("engine_disagreement")

if comparator_trigger_reasons and support_ratio >= 0.65 and source_entropy >= 0.50:
    strong_trigger_reasons.append("multi_source_support")
```

This is a deliberate deviation from "always query every engine" or "trust the fastest engine". It is closer to rule-based computation selection and metareasoning than to route serving. The system spends extra route-search effort when the decision is likely to be affected by missing or conflicting alternatives. That is why the paper can say the implementation is more appropriate than black-box route services for this research evidence problem: it records why comparator search was triggered, suppressed, or considered insufficient.

Publication citation bridge: comparator invocation is a rule-based computation-selection policy, with algorithm selection as the closest framing rather than a claim that the repo implements a learned per-instance solver selector. Rice's algorithm-selection problem frames the general question of matching problem instances to algorithms or solvers [Rice 1976](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0065-2458(08)60520-3), and modern algorithm-selection surveys describe per-instance selection as a practical machine-learning/optimization systems problem [Kerschke et al. 2019](https://doi.org/10.1162/evco_a_00242). Here, the available actions are narrower: keep the current candidate evidence, suppress comparator seeding with a recorded reason, or preemptively seed OSRM/ORS comparator candidates when ambiguity, support, engine disagreement, hard-case, source-entropy, and corridor-coverage gates pass.

### AX34. Multi-Criteria Decision Literature: Why One-Shot Weights Are Not Enough

Freight route choice is naturally multi-criteria. Travel time, money, emissions, route distance, toll exposure, terrain, weather, stochastic delay, and evidence support can conflict. The paper should cite the broad multi-attribute decision-making tradition [Hwang and Yoon 1981](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-48318-9), AHP [Saaty 1986](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.32.7.841), TOPSIS [Hwang and Yoon 1981](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-48318-9), PROMETHEE [Brans and Vincke 1985](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.31.6.647), ELECTRE reviews [Govindan and Jepsen 2016](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2015.09.019), VIKOR [Opricovic and Tzeng 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(03)00020-1), and weighted-sum limitations [Marler and Arora 2010](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00158-009-0460-7). The point is not that the repo invents MCDA. The point is that it refuses to let MCDA become a hidden one-shot ranking.

The modified route-selection layer has two implementation surfaces that the paper must keep separate. `frontend/app/lib/weights.ts` exposes the selector profile family and default constants for UI-side explanation: VIKOR compromise score, balance penalty, route-distance penalty, ETA-distance interaction penalty, knee penalty, and entropy reward. Backend route selection in `backend/app/main.py` additionally applies objective scale floors and a `time_preservation_penalty`, so the backend default is `VIKOR Q + balance + distance + ETA-distance + knee - entropy + time-preservation penalty`. The preference layer separately records explicit time-guard queries when the user states a hard arrival or maximum-travel-time constraint.

```python
time_preservation_penalties = _time_preservation_tradeoff_penalties(
    times,
    moneys,
    emissions,
    wt=wt,
    wm=wm,
    we=we,
)

elif math_profile == "modified_vikor_distance":
    score = (
        vikor_q
        + (balance_weight * balance_penalty)
        + (distance_weight * n_distance)
        + (eta_distance_weight * eta_distance_penalty)
        + (knee_weight * knee_penalty)
        - (entropy_weight * entropy_reward)
        + time_preservation_penalty
    )
```

This is a publishable design point because it answers a common criticism of MCDA: weights alone can look precise while hiding unacceptable tradeoffs. The repository keeps ordinary compromise ranking transparent, adds a backend time-preservation penalty when selecting a route, and still stores hard or semi-hard temporal concerns as explicit preference evidence when they come from a user query. The paper can contrast this with TOPSIS/VIKOR/AHP-style one-shot rankings: those methods can be useful, but a thesis-grade freight decision needs rank, support, explanation, preference-state history, and failure mode together.

Preference ambiguity should also be cited. Robust ordinal regression and imprecise-preference methods are relevant because the decision maker's true utility function may be only partially known [Greco, Mousseau, and Slowinski 2008](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2007.08.013), [Corrente, Greco, and Slowinski 2012](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.6317). Active preference elicitation and regret-based decision support are also relevant [Boutilier 2002](https://doi.org/10.1613/jair.1021), [Boutilier et al. 2006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2006.02.003), [Boutilier 2013](https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199856800.003.0041). The repo's preference-state machinery should be described as an engineering realization of that idea: do not pretend unknown weights are known; record the compatible-set evidence, ask typed questions when valuable, and abstain when ambiguity remains decision-critical.

### AX35. Robust Optimization And Scenario Evidence: Why The Project Uses Bounded Evidence Worlds

Robust optimization normally asks for decisions that perform acceptably over an uncertainty set. Ben-Tal and Nemirovski established robust convex optimization as a principled way to handle uncertain data [Ben-Tal and Nemirovski 1998](https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.23.4.769). Bertsimas and Sim made the "price of robustness" explicit by trading nominal performance against protection level [Bertsimas and Sim 2004](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.1030.0065). Robust shortest-path work shows why deterministic shortest paths are often insufficient when travel time, disruption, or cost is uncertain [Montemanni and Gambardella 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0305-0548(03)00114-X), and newer surveys organize robust/distributionally robust shortest-path models for practical uncertainty [Filippi, Maggioni, and Speranza 2025](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cor.2025.107096).

The repository deliberately does not claim universal minimax optimality. Instead it builds certificates over a deterministic, replayable evidence-world manifest. That is a more honest applied contribution because the data sources, perturbation priors, and route-candidate set are bounded by what the code can inspect. It is closer to sample-average approximation and scenario stress testing than to a global robust-optimization theorem [Shapiro, Dentcheva, and Ruszczynski](https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9780898718751), [Campi and Garatti 2006](https://doi.org/10.1109/TAC.2006.875041), [Saltelli et al. 2008](https://doi.org/10.1002/9780470725184).

The code makes the scope explicit:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CertificateConfig:
    seed: int = 0
    world_count: int = 64
    threshold: float = 0.67
    selector_weights: tuple[float, float, float] = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
    state_catalog: tuple[str, ...] = EVIDENCE_STATES
```

The paper can explain that `world_count = 64` is not a magic universal sample size. It is a bounded replay budget chosen to make stress evidence cheap enough to run inside an interactive/local thesis pipeline while still giving enough worlds for support fractions, fragility summaries, and confidence traces. The certificate threshold `0.67` is likewise not a legal safety threshold. It is an explicit project-level standard for "enough empirical support within the evidence worlds to continue treating the selected route as certified." Because the values are named settings and stored in artifacts, they can be swept, criticized, or tightened. That is better scientific practice than burying the robustness level inside an opaque service response.

The evidence tensor also shows why the project is route-specific rather than generic:

```python
def _evidence_tensor(route: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, dict[str, float]]:
    raw = route.get("evidence_tensor", route.get("dependency_tensor", {}))
    if isinstance(raw, Mapping):
        out: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
        for family, objective_map in raw.items():
            ...
            inner[str(objective)] = max(0.0, min(1.0, _as_float(weight)))
```

This tensor matters for the paper because it connects evidence families to objectives. Weather, toll, terrain, fuel, carbon, and stochastic signals do not all affect time, money, and emissions equally. The project improves over a generic "add uncertainty" statement by recording which evidence family can move which objective and by exposing fragility by family.

### AX36. Risk, Confidence, And Selective Abstention: Why The Paper Must Separate Uncertainty Types

A strong paper must avoid mixing all uncertainty into one confidence score. Route uncertainty includes stochastic objective variation, tail-risk aversion, evidence-source support, winner-frequency evidence, optional-stopping-safe confidence, preference ambiguity, and out-of-support conditions. Each has a different academic lineage.

Risk-measure citations belong in the route-objective layer. Coherent risk measures explain why risk cannot be reduced to expected value [Artzner et al. 1999](https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9965.00068). CVaR/expected shortfall gives a tractable tail-risk summary [Rockafellar and Uryasev 2000](https://doi.org/10.21314/JOR.2000.038), while sample quantile definitions matter for reproducibility [Hyndman and Fan 1996](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.1996.10473566). The repo implements this in `risk_model.py`:

```python
def cvar(values: Iterable[float], *, alpha: float = 0.95) -> float:
    ordered = sorted(float(v) for v in values)
    ...
    tail_integral += 0.5 * (q_start + q_end) * (end - start)
    result = tail_integral / max(1e-12, 1.0 - alpha_clamped)
    threshold = quantile(ordered, alpha_clamped)
    return max(result, threshold)

def robust_objective(...):
    tail_excess = max(0.0, float(cvar_value) - float(mean_value))
    return float(mean_value) + (risk * tail_excess)
```

The important paper point is that this is not just "mean plus variance". It is a tail-excess penalty over route utility samples, with type-7 quantiles and a labelled CVaR-style tail integral. The code also labels its entropic and semivariance branches as thesis-specific adaptations rather than pretending they are canonical definitions. That honesty prevents overclaiming.

Confidence-sequence citations belong in the certification layer. Hoeffding's inequality [Hoeffding 1963](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1963.10500830) and modern confidence sequences [Howard et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1214/20-AOS1991) support optional-stopping-safe language. The repo's `winner_confidence_sequence` records lower/upper bounds for the route's observed wins:

```python
for sample_count, observation in enumerate(observations, start=1):
    success_count += 1 if _coerce_probability(observation) > 0.0 else 0
    point_estimate = success_count / float(sample_count)
    lower_bound, upper_bound = anytime_hoeffding_interval(
        success_count,
        sample_count,
        delta=delta,
    )
```

Selective prediction citations belong in the terminal decision layer. Chow's reject-option work establishes that abstaining can be rational when classification risk is too high [Chow 1970](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406). Selective classification formalizes prediction with coverage/risk tradeoffs [El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/el-yaniv10a.html), and later work emphasizes calibrated abstention for modern models [Geifman and El-Yaniv 2017](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.08500). Conformal prediction is relevant as a nearby distribution-free uncertainty framework, but the repo should not claim conformal coverage unless a conformal calibration set is actually used [Angelopoulos and Bates 2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.07511), [Lei et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2017.1307116).

The code implements typed abstention rather than generic failure:

```python
TypedAbstentionReason = Literal[
    "uncertified_due_to_search",
    "uncertified_due_to_evidence",
    "uncertified_due_to_preference",
    "uncertified_due_to_out_of_support_world_model",
    "uncertified_due_to_budget",
    "uncertified_due_to_model_assumption",
]

def recommended_action(self) -> str:
    return {
        "uncertified_due_to_search": "expand_search",
        "uncertified_due_to_evidence": "refresh_evidence",
        "uncertified_due_to_preference": "ask_preference",
        "uncertified_due_to_out_of_support_world_model": "expand_world_model",
        "uncertified_due_to_budget": "increase_budget",
        "uncertified_due_to_model_assumption": "review_model_assumptions",
    }[self.reason_code]
```

This is a concrete improvement over a route API that returns either a path or an error. The paper can claim typed abstention as a decision-quality feature: the system explains what kind of uncertainty blocked certification and what action would most directly address it.

### AX37. Emissions, Eco-Routing, And Standards: Why Transparency Is The Strong Claim

Environmental freight routing must be careful. The pollution-routing problem connects routing, speed, load, fuel, and emissions [Bektas and Laporte 2011](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trb.2011.02.004). Green VRP work extends routing to alternative fuel and environmental objectives [Erdogan and Miller-Hooks 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tre.2011.08.001). Eco-routing papers show that fuel and emissions can depend on traffic, speed, vehicle type, and grade [Barth and Boriboonsomsin 2008](https://doi.org/10.3141/2058-20), [Boriboonsomsin and Barth 2009](https://doi.org/10.3141/2139-03), [Boriboonsomsin et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1109/TITS.2012.2204051). Road-grade effects deserve explicit mention because the repo models terrain and grade; this is not just a cosmetic map feature.

Standards and official models also matter. ISO 14083 provides a transport-chain GHG quantification and reporting standard [ISO 14083:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/78864.html). GLEC, EN 16258, COPERT, HBEFA, MOVES, DESNZ/DEFRA factors, and related transport-emission inventories provide regulatory or industry accounting context. The paper must say that this repo is not a regulatory inventory replacement. It is a transparent routing-decision model that exposes how emissions entered the route choice.

The code supports that claim through explicit segment energy and scope adjustment:

```python
speed_kmh = (distance_km / (duration_s / 3600.0)) if duration_s > 0 else 0.0
grade_pct = float(grade) * 100.0

load_factor = _derived_load_factor(vehicle, klass=klass)
speed_value = _clamp(speed_kmh, consumption_surface.axes.speed_kmh[0], ...)
grade_value = _clamp(grade_pct, consumption_surface.axes.grade_pct[0], ...)
temp_value = _clamp(emissions_context.ambient_temp_c, ...)
```

```python
def apply_scope_emissions_adjustment(...):
    if scope == "ttw":
        return max(0.0, float(emissions_kg))
    if is_ev_mode:
        grid_intensity = profile[int(hour) % 24]
        wtw_factor = max(0.85, min(1.45, grid_intensity / 0.20))
        factor = max(0.95, min(1.75, wtw_factor * 1.18)) if scope == "lca" else wtw_factor
```

The paper can say the project improves on a black-box "CO2 number" by making the route-emissions assumptions inspectable: vehicle class, speed, load factor, grade, ambient temperature, fuel/electricity price, scope mode, and regional-hourly grid modulation all become evidence. That is better for thesis review because the emissions route-decision is explainable. It is not necessarily better than official inventory tools for corporate reporting, and the report should keep that boundary.

### AX38. Evaluation Methodology And Claim Discipline: What A Published Paper Must Defend

A published paper needs a methods story that goes beyond "I ran tests". The repo's evaluator is closer to empirical software-engineering case-study evidence than to a single benchmark leaderboard. Case-study reporting guidance in software engineering [Runeson and Host 2009](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10664-008-9102-8) and experimentation methodology [Wohlin et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-29044-2) support explicit threats-to-validity language. Reproducible research work argues that code and data are central scientific artifacts, not just supplements [Buckheit and Donoho 1995/1998](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-2544-7_5). FAIR data principles support rich metadata and reusable artifacts [Wilkinson et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18).

The paper should describe evaluation as a set of named lanes: broad cold proof, focused REFC proof, focused VOI proof, DCCS diagnostic probe, hot-rerun proof, preference proof, optional-stopping coverage, proxy-audit calibration, perturbation/flip-radius, threshold sensitivity, public transfer, and synthetic ground truth. That language is in `docs/evaluation_card.md` and the evaluator source. It is better than presenting one aggregate score because the system's contribution has multiple evidence surfaces. DCCS, REFC, and VOI each expose different kinds of adequacy evidence; VOI may be budget-sensitive; support-fragile and collapse-prone cohorts may behave differently from average cases.

The statistics layer should be conservative. Bootstrap confidence intervals are appropriate when analytic intervals for complex metrics are awkward [Efron and Tibshirani 1993](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4899-4541-9), and Holm correction is appropriate when multiple claims are tested [Holm 1979](https://www.jstor.org/stable/4615733). The report already records that repeated-run artifacts include BCa-bootstrap CI and Holm-adjusted claim summaries when repeated runs are present. The published paper must preserve that conditional wording: repeated-run artifacts are stronger evidence only where repeated runs actually exist.

The current evaluator state is important for honesty. The report records that the latest checked full-suite assessment is publishable under the applied-evidence policy and adoption-supported for the measured benchmark framing, while deployment-grade and theorem-grade claims remain outside the current evidence scope. This is not a weakness to hide. It is a claim-discipline strength. A paper can separate "the architecture is implemented and evidence-rich" from "the system is deployment certified". In applied systems research, this is often more credible than forcing a false universal-green narrative.

### AX39. Explainability, Documentation, And Accountability As Part Of The Method

The project is not just optimizing routes; it is making route decisions inspectable. Explainability literature supports the need to match explanation to decision context [Doshi-Velez and Kim 2017](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.08608), and local explanation methods such as LIME popularized the question of why a user should trust a prediction [Ribeiro, Singh, and Guestrin 2016](https://aclanthology.org/N16-3020/). Broader XAI surveys emphasize that explanations need to support responsible decisions rather than simply decorate outputs [Arrieta et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.inffus.2019.12.012). Model cards [Mitchell et al. 2019](https://doi.org/10.1145/3287560.3287596) and datasheets for datasets [Gebru et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1145/3458723) support the repo's documentation-heavy stance.

The paper can make a concrete argument: for this domain, explanation is not a post-hoc natural-language paragraph. Explanation is an evidence object. A route decision is explained by its candidate generation path, objective vector, selected-route source, evidence tensor, support flag, confidence state, preference compatibility, VOI trace, abstention reason, artifact manifest, and claim-matrix status. That is why the thesis-codebase report itself is part of the method. It is the master evidence base that lets a reviewer recover the implementation logic without reading every file.

This also distinguishes the project from black-box commercial APIs. A route API can return ETA, distance, geometry, tolls, and emissions-like summaries. It may be operationally superior. But unless it exposes decision-state evidence, it cannot answer the academic questions this repo is built around:

```text
Why did this route win?
Which objective made it fragile?
Which evidence source would change the answer?
Which preference question would reduce ambiguity?
Was the winner supported across stress worlds?
What stopped certification if no singleton decision was safe?
Which generated artifacts prove the claim?
```

Those are paper-level questions. The repo answers them through code and artifacts, not through a marketing claim.

### AX40. Reviewer Objections And The Paper-Ready Answers

A reviewer may ask why the project does not simply use Google Maps, HERE, OSRM, GraphHopper, ArcGIS, PTV, OR-Tools, or a commercial TMS. The answer is not that those systems are weak. Many are stronger for map coverage, real-time traffic, legal truck constraints, support, optimization scale, and operational integration. The paper's answer is that they solve different problems. WhatIf Freight Router is designed to expose and preserve the evidence behind a route decision. That makes it stronger as a research artifact when the evaluation target is interpretability, reproducibility, preference ambiguity, and certification.

A reviewer may ask why exact optimization is not used everywhere. The answer is that exactness over the wrong abstraction does not solve the thesis problem. An exact shortest path under one scalar edge cost still hides multiobjective tradeoffs. An exact VRP tour set still does not explain the route-level evidence state. A robust optimization formulation with an unvalidated uncertainty set may look mathematically stronger while being less honest about data support. The repo uses bounded evidence worlds, explicit thresholds, and typed abstention because they keep the assumptions visible.

A reviewer may ask whether the system is genuinely novel or only an assembly of known pieces. The neutral, defensible answer is that the architecture is distinctive as an integrated, inspectable freight-route decision evidence pipeline. Its individual ingredients are established: shortest paths, K-shortest paths, MCDA, robust optimization, CVaR, confidence sequences, preference elicitation, VOI, selective prediction, eco-routing, and reproducibility artifacts. The contribution is the composition and implementation discipline: those ingredients are wired into a local, source-readable system where every route decision can carry its evidence, uncertainty, preference state, and failure mode.

A reviewer may ask whether the emissions model is accurate enough. The paper should answer that emissions are model-conditioned and route-comparative, not regulator-grade absolute inventories. The system is useful because it exposes the assumptions affecting route choice. It should not claim to replace ISO 14083, GLEC, HBEFA, COPERT, MOVES, or corporate carbon-accounting systems.

A reviewer may ask whether the evaluation is complete. The answer is that the repo has many explicit lanes and checked artifacts, and the current report still records deployment and theorem boundaries. The paper can be strong while honest: it can present an implemented architecture, demonstrate evidence-rich behavior, show negative results and limitations, and state exactly which claims are not deployment-ready or theorem-complete.

### AX41. Equation-Level Summary Of The Novelty Claim

The final paper can use the following equation-level story.

Classical shortest path:

```text
p* = argmin_p sum_{e in p} c_e
```

This is insufficient because a freight route is a decision under conflicting objectives, uncertain evidence, and incomplete preferences as well as an edge-cost problem.

Multiobjective route candidate:

```text
x_r = (time_r, money_r, co2_r, risk_r, support_r, provenance_r)
```

The repo's route candidate is not just geometry. It carries objective, risk, support, and provenance features used later by certification.

Modified route ranking:

```text
score_r =
  VIKOR_or_compromise_score_r
  + balance_penalty_r
  + distance_penalty_r
  + eta_distance_penalty_r
  + knee_imbalance_penalty_r
  + time_preservation_penalty_r
  - entropy_spread_reward_r
```

This is the practical deviation from standard multicriteria decision analysis (MCDA). The score is still transparent, but it includes freight-specific guards against unhelpful compromise routes. The backend implementation also uses objective normalisation floors before these terms are combined, so the paper should describe the equation as the decision contract after scale-safe normalisation rather than as a raw-unit weighted sum.

Bounded evidence-world certificate:

```text
certificate(r) =
  count(world in W where r wins under selector and evidence perturbation) / |W|

certified(r) =
  certificate(r) >= threshold
  and support_flag(r, W) is acceptable
  and search/preference/evidence blockers are absent
```

This differs from universal robust optimization:

```text
argmin_x max_{u in U} f(x, u)
```

The repo does not claim all possible uncertainty. It certifies within an explicit evidence-world manifest, then exposes the manifest and limitations.

VOI action selection:

```text
Q(a) =
  (
    predicted_certificate_gain
    + predicted_margin_gain
    + predicted_frontier_gain
    + predicted_preference_shrinkage
    + predicted_search_completeness
  ) / (action_cost + epsilon)
```

The exact implementation has action-specific terms, but the paper-level story is that extra computation or user questioning is itself a decision. That ties the repo to bounded rationality [Simon 1955](https://doi.org/10.2307/1884852), rational metareasoning [Russell and Wefald 1991](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(91)90015-C), and value-of-information decision theory [Howard 1966](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1966.300074).

Typed abstention:

```text
if no certified singleton:
  return abstain(reason_code, remedy, trigger_metric, evidence_family)
```

This is a central design improvement over returning a weak route anyway. In a safety- or cost-sensitive freight setting, the system should sometimes say "expand search", "refresh evidence", "ask preference", or "increase budget" rather than hide uncertainty behind a ranked list.

This coverage map is the safest high-level guarantee for the published paper. It prevents the literature review from becoming a list of unrelated citations. Each external literature family is tied to a code or artifact surface and a scoped claim. That is the right standard for a top applied thesis paper because it makes novelty, limits, evidence, and reproducibility inspectable together.

### AX43. MCDA-Aware But Not Just AHP, TOPSIS, Or Outranking

The project is positioned as an applied MCDA decision-aiding system rather than only as a route optimiser. MCDA is the correct family because the decision is not reducible to a single natural unit: time, money, emissions, distance, route shape, evidence support, uncertainty, and preference ambiguity are all simultaneously relevant. This matches the integrated MCDA framing in Belton and Stewart [Belton and Stewart 2002](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4615-1495-4), the state-of-the-art MCDA survey edited by Greco, Ehrgott, and Figueira [Greco et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4939-3094-4), and Tsoukias's distinction between decision theory and decision-aiding methodology [Tsoukias 2007](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2007.02.039). The repository contribution is not that weighted sums, VIKOR, Pareto dominance, or compromise scoring were invented here. The contribution is that these methods are embedded inside a route-decision pipeline that also preserves search evidence, preference ambiguity, certification state, abstention causes, and traceable remedies.

AHP is a useful comparator because it is widely used for weighting and transport/logistics decisions, with Vaidya and Kumar reviewing broad AHP applications [Vaidya and Kumar 2006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2004.04.028). However, AHP requires pairwise judgement matrices and introduces consistency, scale-interpretation, and rank-reversal concerns; Belton and Gear's classic critique is directly relevant [Belton and Gear 1983](https://doi.org/10.1016/0305-0483(83)90047-6). This project avoids forcing an operator to complete an AHP matrix before every route. Instead, it normalises direct route-objective weights and only asks structured preference questions when ambiguity matters.

```python
# backend/app/models.py
class Weights(BaseModel):
    """User preference weights. Backend normalises to avoid UI mistakes."""

    time: float = Field(..., ge=0)
    money: float = Field(..., ge=0)
    co2: float = Field(..., ge=0)

# backend/app/risk_model.py
w_sum = max(float(w_time) + float(w_money) + float(w_emissions), 1e-9)
wt = max(0.0, float(w_time)) / w_sum
wm = max(0.0, float(w_money)) / w_sum
we = max(0.0, float(w_emissions)) / w_sum
```

TOPSIS is another natural comparator because it ranks alternatives by distance from positive and negative ideal points, originally formalised by Hwang and Yoon [Hwang and Yoon 1981](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-48318-9) and surveyed in applications by Behzadian and coauthors [Behzadian et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2012.05.056). The project deliberately avoids being "just TOPSIS" because route choice is not only geometric closeness to an ideal vector. A route can be close to an ideal point and still be unsupported by evidence, fragile under sampled worlds, or preference-ambiguous. The implementation therefore uses compromise scoring and freight-specific penalties, then treats the scalar score as a recommendation candidate rather than a proof.

Outranking methods such as ELECTRE and PROMETHEE are also important alternatives. ELECTRE originates in Roy's outranking approach [Roy 1968](https://doi.org/10.1051/ro/196802V100571), and PROMETHEE was introduced by Brans and Vincke [Brans and Vincke 1985](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.31.6.647). These methods are strong when the decision maker can justify concordance, discordance, veto, and preference thresholds. For this project, those thresholds would become another opaque layer unless exposed and audited.
