It also enforces the maintained-doc policy that ad hoc interactive-analysis artifacts are not the authoritative artifact surface in this repo:

```python
# scripts/check_docs.py
THEOREM_ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:THM|LB)-\d{2}\b")
ALLOWED_THEOREM_STATUSES = {
    "theorem-backed",
    "partial-proof",
    "empirical-surface",
    "scaffold-only",
}
ALLOWED_CLAIM_STATUSES = {
    "theorem-backed",
    "empirical",
    "heuristic-but-measured",
    "non-claim / descriptive only",
}
```

The `main()` check surface then ties `Markdown link validity`, `Docs index/orphan/related-doc coverage`, `Referenced local path existence`, `Endpoint parity against backend/app/main.py`, and `Theorem-map / claim-matrix semantic consistency` together. The unconditional `Notebook reference ban` is run after the selected checks:

```python
# scripts/check_docs.py
if selected["links"]:
    total += print_result("Markdown link validity", run_link_check())
if selected["orphans"]:
    total += print_result("Docs index/orphan/related-doc coverage", run_orphan_check())
if selected["paths"]:
    total += print_result("Referenced local path existence", run_path_check())
if selected["endpoints"]:
    total += print_result("Endpoint parity against backend/app/main.py", run_endpoint_check())
if selected["theorem_claims"]:
    total += print_result(
        "Theorem-map / claim-matrix semantic consistency",
        run_theorem_claim_consistency_check(),
    )

total += print_result("Notebook reference ban", run_forbidden_notebook_check())
```

This is better than a normal README-based project because the report is not allowed to become a free-standing narrative. Claims must stay connected to maintained evidence surfaces. For a publishable applied-systems paper, that matters as much as algorithmic novelty: a reviewer can inspect the artifact, rerun the checks, and see whether the report still matches the code.

Artifact-review framing also belongs in the paper. The repo creates signed manifests, route artifacts, theorem hooks, companion summaries, and provenance contexts. This aligns with FAIR data principles [Wilkinson et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18), W3C PROV-DM [W3C PROV-DM](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/), and ACM artifact review and badging [ACM artifact review](https://www.acm.org/publications/policies/artifact-review-and-badging-current). The run-store code shows that provenance is not a prose aspiration:

```python
# backend/app/run_store.py
ROUTE_ARTIFACT_PROVENANCE_SCHEMA_VERSION = "route-artifact-provenance-v1"
ROUTE_ARTIFACT_IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION = "route-artifact-identity-v1"
ROUTE_CONTROLLER_POLICY_VERSION = "voi-controller-policy-v1"
ROUTE_PREFERENCE_MODEL_VERSION = "preference-elicitation-policy-v1"

def build_thesis_artifact_provenance_context(
    run_id: str,
    *,
    metadata: Mapping[str, Any],
    evaluation_manifest: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    metadata_payload = _json_mapping(metadata)
    evaluation_manifest_payload = _json_mapping(evaluation_manifest)
    lane_id = _first_nonempty_text(evaluation_suite.get("role"), "thesis_evaluation") or "thesis_evaluation"
    git_commit_hash = _resolve_git_commit_hash()
    environment_lockfile_hash, environment_lockfile_path = _resolve_environment_lockfile_hash()
```

The provenance payload records identity and policy hashes:

    "run_id": run_id,

    "preference_model_version": ROUTE_PREFERENCE_MODEL_VERSION,

The external-data section can then be direct. OpenStreetMap is an essential geospatial dependency and must be cited with its attribution/legal surface [OpenStreetMap copyright](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright/en) and VGI quality literature [Goodchild 2007](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10708-007-9111-y), [Haklay 2010](https://doi.org/10.1068/b35097). DfT road traffic counts, GOV.UK conversion factors, and Open-Meteo are input evidence sources with explicit provenance boundaries [DfT road traffic counts](https://www.data.gov.uk/dataset/208c0e7b-353f-4e2d-8b7a-1a7118467acc/gb-road-traffic-counts), [GOV.UK conversion factors](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/government-conversion-factors-for-company-reporting), [Open-Meteo docs](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs). The repo is better than a project that simply consumes these sources because it records provenance, freshness, support, policy identity, and failure modes.

### AX67. The Paper-Claim Spine Needs To Be Stated As An Evidence-Bounded Design-Science Contribution

The actual published paper should not start from the implementation menu, because that would make the system sound like a feature collection. The spine is sharper: the project implements a prototype treatment of making freight-route recommendation auditable under incomplete route search, uncertain evidence, and incomplete preference knowledge. The hard part is that each uncertainty type can break the recommendation in a different way. Search uncertainty means a hidden challenger may exist. Evidence uncertainty means the current cost, delay, toll, terrain, emissions, or weather state may be weakly supported. Preference uncertainty means the user-facing top route may not remain top after the user clarifies trade-offs. Ordinary route planners tend to collapse these into a single path or score; this repo keeps them separated until the terminal decision.

This is a design-science paper rather than a pure algorithm paper. Hevner et al. define the design-science contribution around a purposeful artifact, rigorous evaluation, and a relevant problem [Hevner et al. 2004](https://doi.org/10.2307/25148625). Wieringa's design-science cycle explains why problem investigation, treatment design, and treatment validation should be explicit [Wieringa 2014](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-43839-8). The repo satisfies that pattern because it contains a treatment artifact, evidence lanes, failure atlases, checked claim maps, and code-level terminal semantics. It is better than a route-planning demo for the paper's purpose because the artifact exposes its own uncertainty and refusal logic instead of presenting a polished route even when the assumptions are weak.

The paper's central answer can be written directly:

The project designed a selective freight-route decision engine that turns candidate paths into certified decision packages. Its novelty is the integration of search criticality, evidence support, preference compatibility, robust/tail-risk scoring, provenance, and typed abstention into one auditable decision contract. The output is a terminal state saying whether route A is certified, whether a set of routes is certified, or whether the system refuses singleton certification because search, evidence, preference, budget, world-model support, or model assumptions remain unresolved.

The terminal output model is what makes the claim defensible:

```python
# backend/app/certification_models.py
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DecisionPackage(SerializableRecord):
    recommended_route: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    certified_set: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    frontier_summary: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    certificate_summary: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    stability_summary: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    preference_summary: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    support_summary: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    abstention_summary: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    action_trace_summary: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    witness_summary: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    artifact_pointers: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    selected_certificate_basis: str | None = None
    terminal_type: str = "singleton"
    certification_state: CertificationState | None = None
    abstention_record: AbstentionRecord | None = None
```

The exact class fields matter for thesis writing. A conventional router can return geometry, distance, duration, and maybe alternatives. A conventional MCDA tool can return a rank after weights are supplied. This project returns a decision package in which route geometry is only one part of the evidence. The `terminal_type` records whether the terminal surface is a singleton, certified set, or abstention-style state. `certificate_summary`, `frontier_summary`, `stability_summary`, `preference_summary`, and `support_summary` separate proof-like route support, frontier structure, local stability, preference ambiguity, and support evidence from the route itself. `abstention_summary` and `abstention_record` record why the system refuses to overclaim. `action_trace_summary`, `witness_summary`, and `artifact_pointers` then connect the terminal decision to rerunnable evidence. That is why the design is stronger for a paper than a normal dashboard: the artifacts can be audited independently of the visual interface.

### AX68. Threats To Validity Must Be A First-Class Section, Not A Defensive Appendix

The paper needs a strong threats-to-validity section because this system is empirical, live-source-dependent, UK-scoped, and artifact-heavy. Shadish, Cook, and Campbell's validity taxonomy is useful for structuring this section into internal, construct, external, and statistical-conclusion validity [Shadish et al. 2002](https://psycnet.apa.org/record/2002-17373-000). Wohlin et al. give the software-engineering analogue for experiment planning and reporting [Wohlin et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-29044-2). Demsar is relevant because the thesis compares methods across route cases and must avoid casual rank-significance claims [Demsar 2006](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v7/demsar06a.html).

Internal validity threats are mainly route-engine state, cache state, live-source freshness, seed choice, and strict-mode availability. The project mitigates these by recording run identity, policy hashes, route-graph state, manifests, fixed seeds, and strict preflight gates. It does not pretend those threats vanish. That is better than hiding them because a reviewer can see whether the evidence world changed.

Construct validity threats are mainly metric translation. Duration, monetary cost, emissions, CVaR, preference compatibility, certificate lower bounds, and candidate criticality are proxies for operational freight quality. The report should explicitly say that these are inspectable decision metrics, not the whole of fleet operations. The code supports this distinction by validating route weights and accepting legacy aliases without letting bad numeric inputs silently distort the score:

```python
# backend/app/models.py
class Weights(BaseModel):
    """User preference weights. Backend normalises to avoid UI mistakes."""

    time: float = Field(..., ge=0)
    money: float = Field(..., ge=0)
    co2: float = Field(..., ge=0)

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def accept_legacy_aliases(cls, value: object) -> object:
        if not isinstance(value, dict):
            return value
        data = dict(value)
        if "money" not in data:
            for key in ("cost", "monetary_cost"):
                if key in data:
                    data["money"] = data[key]
                    break
        if "co2" not in data:
            for key in ("emissions", "emissions_kg", "co2e"):
                if key in data:
                    data["co2"] = data[key]
                    break
        return data

    @field_validator("time", "money", "co2")
    @classmethod
    def finite(cls, v: float) -> float:
        if v != v or v in (float("inf"), float("-inf")):
            raise ValueError("weight must be finite")
        return v
```

External validity is deliberately limited. The current artifact is UK-focused, road-freight-focused, calibrated around repo-local UK assets, and dependent on available routing/evidence sources. The paper should not claim general global freight superiority. It should claim a transferable architecture: separate search, evidence, preference, support, certification, and abstention surfaces so another region can be integrated without changing the scientific logic. This is stronger than overclaiming transfer because it gives reviewers a clear boundary: the method is portable; the current evidence is UK-scoped.

Publication citation bridge: add dataset-shift taxonomy rather than treating transfer as one undifferentiated risk. Moreno-Torres et al. organise dataset shift into mechanisms such as covariate, prior, and concept shift [Moreno-Torres et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patcog.2011.06.019). That helps the paper say why corridor-family and weather-regime holdouts are diagnostic stress surfaces: they test specified observable shifts, not every latent freight-market, routing-engine, or regional deployment shift.

Conclusion validity is limited by claim scope. The maintained evidence says the suite is publishable on current applied evidence, while deployment-grade certification remains future work. This is not a weakness to hide. Ioannidis and Fanelli are useful citations because negative and incomplete evidence are part of scientific honesty, not just failed engineering [Ioannidis 2005](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.0020124), [Fanelli 2012](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11192-011-0494-7). The repo is better than a one-off result table because it carries claim boundaries into checked docs rather than burying them.

### AX69. DCCS Is Not A Standard K-Shortest-Path Wrapper; It Is A Candidate-Evidence Triage Layer

The paper should explicitly distinguish three layers that reviewers may otherwise conflate. The routing layer produces feasible path geometry. The candidate-generation layer creates a set of alternatives. The DCCS layer decides which candidates deserve refinement and which candidates are not decision-critical under the current evidence. That is not the same as Yen's K-shortest-path algorithm [Yen 1971](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.17.11.712), Eppstein's K-shortest-path algorithm [Eppstein 1998](https://doi.org/10.1137/S0097539795290477), or a limited-overlap route-set method [Chondrogiannis et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00778-020-00604-x). Those methods answer "which paths should be generated?" DCCS asks "which generated path is decision-critical enough to spend refinement, evidence, or preference budget on?"

The DCCS configuration exposes the design choice rather than burying it:

```python
# backend/app/decision_critical.py
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DCCSConfig:
    mode: str = "bootstrap"
    pipeline_variant: str = "dccs"
    search_budget: int = 3
    bootstrap_seed_size: int = 2
    refinement_cost_floor: float = 1.0
    near_duplicate_threshold: float = 0.82
    objective_gap_weight: float = 1.0
    mechanism_gap_weight: float = 0.45
    overlap_penalty_weight: float = 1.25
    stretch_penalty_weight: float = 0.5
    flip_bias: float = -0.35
    flip_logistic_scale: float = 2.35
    challenger_search_completeness_weight: float = 0.18
    challenger_hidden_challenger_weight: float = 0.12
```

The dataclass defaults are conservative standalone defaults, not the full live-route runtime configuration. In live `/route`, `_dccs_runtime_config` passes the effective request/settings search budget, currently `ROUTE_PIPELINE_SEARCH_BUDGET=6` by default, and sets `bootstrap_seed_size=max(1, ROUTE_DCCS_BOOTSTRAP_COUNT)`, currently `3` by default. `near_duplicate_threshold=0.82` still makes corridor duplication explicit, which is important because route alternatives that share most of their edges do not give strong evidence about operational choice. The gap, hidden-challenger, and search-completeness terms encode the thesis claim that unresolved search mass is itself decision evidence, not an inconvenience. The paper should describe DCCS as an instrumented candidate-evidence triage policy rather than proof of optimal candidate selection.

The project-specific calculation is clearer in `candidate_criticality.py`:

```python
# backend/app/candidate_criticality.py
support_mass = candidate_envelope.support_mass if candidate_envelope is not None else 0.0
winner_lcb_lift = max(0.0, 0.45 * objective_gap + 0.15 * (1.0 - support_mass))
pairwise_gap_lcb_lift = max(0.0, 0.35 * mechanism_gap + 0.10 * (1.0 - overlap))
flip_radius_lift = max(0.0, 0.50 * flip_probability + 0.05 * max(0.0, stretch - 1.0))
unresolved_winner_mass = max(0.0, 1.0 - objective_gap)
preference_relevance = _clamp_unit(
    0.40 * mechanism_gap + 0.30 * time_regret_gap + 0.20 * (1.0 - overlap)
)
search_deficiency_risk = _clamp_unit(
    0.45 * (1.0 - objective_gap) + 0.25 * overlap + 0.30 * float(near_duplicate)
)
action_cost = max(0.0, _as_float(predicted_refine_cost))
denominator = max(1.0, action_cost)
criticality_score = (
    winner_lcb_lift
    + pairwise_gap_lcb_lift
    + flip_radius_lift
    + unresolved_winner_mass
    + preference_relevance
    + search_deficiency_risk
) / denominator
```

The contribution is that candidate triage is not only distance or route diversity. It estimates whether a candidate can lift winner lower bounds, close pairwise gaps, improve flip-radius evidence, resolve possible-winner mass, matter to preference elicitation, or reveal a search deficiency. Other systems often rank alternatives by length, time, overlap, or a scalar generalized cost. This system is better for certification because it ranks candidates by expected contribution to a decision proof boundary.

The observed-refinement code also matters because it turns DCCS into a measurable component rather than a storytelling layer:

```python
# backend/app/decision_critical.py
def record_refine_outcome(
    record: DCCSCandidateRecord,
    *,
    observed_refine_cost: float | None,
    frontier_added: bool = False,
    decision_flip: bool = False,
    dominated_but_close: bool = False,
    redundant: bool = False,
) -> DCCSCandidateRecord:
    if frontier_added:
        label = "frontier_addition"
    elif decision_flip:
        label = "decision_flip"
    elif dominated_but_close:
        label = "challenger_but_not_added"
    elif redundant:
        label = "non_challenger_redundant"
    else:
        label = record.decision_reason
    delta = observed_refine_cost - record.predicted_refine_cost
    ratio = observed_refine_cost / max(1e-9, record.predicted_refine_cost)
```

This should be highlighted in the paper because it answers a natural reviewer question: how do we know DCCS is doing anything useful? The project records observed frontier additions, decision flips, challenger hit rates, redundant refinements, predicted-vs-observed refine-cost error, and cost ratios. That is better than a heuristic K-path selector because it makes candidate triage falsifiable.

### AX70. VOI Turns The System From A Static Ranker Into A Bounded Metareasoner

Value-of-information framing should be central in the paper. Howard's classic value-of-information framing says information matters when it can change a decision [Howard 1966](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1966.300074). Russell and Wefald show why computation itself should be controlled as a resource [Russell and Wefald 1991](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(91)90015-C). WhatIf Freight Router adapts those ideas to route recommendation: the controller chooses between search actions, evidence actions, preference actions, and stopping, under finite budgets.

The controller's parameters are deliberately small and interpretable:

```python
# backend/app/voi_controller.py
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class VOIConfig:
    certificate_threshold: float = 0.67
    stop_threshold: float = 0.02
    search_budget: int = 3
    evidence_budget: int = 2
    max_iterations: int = 8
    top_k_refine: int = 2
    resample_increment: int = 25
    lambda_certificate: float = 0.60
    lambda_margin: float = 0.25
    lambda_frontier: float = 0.15
    lambda_radius_or_flip_budget: float = 0.02
    lambda_unresolved_mass: float = 0.02
    lambda_preference_ambiguity: float = 0.02
    near_tie_threshold: float = 0.03
    search_completeness_threshold: float = 0.84
    search_completeness_action_bonus: float = 0.22
    evidence_uncertainty_threshold: float = 0.08
```

The weighting tells the thesis story. Certificate gain is the dominant term because the goal is not route entertainment; it is certified recommendation. Margin and frontier terms come next because closing a pairwise gap or boundary can change whether the system can stop. Radius, unresolved mass, and preference ambiguity have small but nonzero weights because they should influence action choice without overwhelming the certificate objective. The near-tie and search-completeness thresholds make the controller conservative around ambiguous decisions.

The action-scoring equation is implemented as value-per-cost:

```python
# backend/app/voi_controller.py
q_score = (
    (cfg.lambda_certificate * predicted_winner_lcb_gain(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_margin * predicted_gap_lcb_gain(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_frontier * predicted_boundary_contraction(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_radius_or_flip_budget * predicted_radius_or_flip_budget_gain(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_unresolved_mass * predicted_unresolved_mass_reduction(scored_action))
    + (
        cfg.lambda_preference_ambiguity
        * predicted_preference_ambiguity_reduction(scored_action)
    )
) / (cost + cfg.epsilon)
```

This is not a claim of globally optimal metareasoning. It is a bounded engineering surrogate. The controller is better than static scoring because it can justify why the next action is route search, evidence refresh, preference query, or stopping. It is weaker than a formal optimal policy over the full belief-state MDP. The contribution is the auditable controller trace and stop certificate, not a universal VOI optimality theorem.

### AX71. Typed Abstention Is The Human-Automation Safety Boundary

Human-automation and situation-awareness literature belongs in the paper because a route recommendation system can easily become over-automation. Parasuraman, Sheridan, and Wickens classify automation by stages and levels of human interaction [Parasuraman et al. 2000](https://doi.org/10.1109/3468.844354). Endsley explains why situation awareness matters in dynamic systems [Endsley 1995](https://doi.org/10.1518/001872095779049543). WhatIf Freight Router is designed as decision support, not full automation: it recommends, certifies, refuses, and explains the next human action.

The abstention mapping is the clearest code evidence:

```python
# backend/app/abstention.py
@property
def recommended_action(self) -> str:
    action = self.detail.get("recommended_action")
    if action:
        return str(action)
    return {
        "typed_abstention_recommended": "expand_worlds",
        "uncertified_due_to_search": "expand_search",
        "uncertified_due_to_evidence": "refresh_evidence",
        "uncertified_due_to_preference": "ask_preference",
        "uncertified_due_to_out_of_support_world_model": "expand_world_model",
        "uncertified_due_to_budget": "increase_budget",
        "uncertified_due_to_model_assumption": "review_model_assumptions",
    }[self.reason_code]
```

The classifier is intentionally conservative:

```python
# backend/app/abstention.py
if budget_text or _contains_any(stop_text, ("budget", "exhausted", "quota")):
    return "uncertified_due_to_budget"

if support_flag is False or _contains_any(
    support_text,
    ("out_of_support", "unsupported", "outside_support", "out of support"),
):
    return "uncertified_due_to_out_of_support_world_model"

if credible_search_uncertainty is True or _contains_any(
    stop_text,
    ("search_incomplete", "no_action_worth_it", "search_uncertain", "insufficient_search"),
) or (search_completeness_score is not None and search_completeness_score < 0.5):
    return "uncertified_due_to_search"
```

This is better than a confidence badge because it distinguishes what failed. A low-confidence route badge may tell a user to be cautious, but it does not say what action would improve the decision. Here, an unsupported world model points to expanding the world model, a search deficiency points to expanding candidate search, preference ambiguity points to asking the user, and budget exhaustion points to increasing budget or narrowing the claim. That is the paper's human-automation safety boundary.

### AX72. Proxy Evidence Needs Causal-Style Support Logic, Not Just More Data

The proxy-audit subsystem is connected to causal-inference and sample-support literature. Propensity scores are classically used to balance observed covariates [Rosenbaum and Rubin 1983](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/70.1.41). Doubly robust estimation combines outcome and propensity models under assumptions [Bang and Robins 2005](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1541-0420.2005.00377.x). Hernan and Robins give a broader causal-inference framing for why identification assumptions matter [Hernan and Robins](https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/miguel-hernan/causal-inference-book/). The repo is not claiming full causal identification; it borrows the discipline that proxy evidence must record support, overlap, leakage safety, and audit coverage before it can be used for certification.

The positivity diagnostic is the exact code hook:

```python
# backend/app/support_model.py
def build_positivity_diagnostics(
    *,
    audited_route_pair_count: int,
    candidate_route_pair_count: int | None = None,
    propensity_scores: list[float] | None = None,
    support_state: Any | None = None,
    min_propensity: float = 0.05,
    min_audit_coverage_ratio: float = 0.1,
    provenance: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> PositivityDiagnostics:
    coverage_ratio = 0.0 if candidate_count <= 0 else audited_count / candidate_count
    minimum_propensity = min(propensities) if propensities else 0.0
    positivity_ok = (
        audited_count > 0
        and coverage_ratio >= _clamp01(min_audit_coverage_ratio)
        and minimum_propensity >= _clamp01(min_propensity)
    )
    weak_overlap_detected = audited_count > 0 and minimum_propensity < _clamp01(min_propensity)
```

The recommendation logic is also thesis-relevant:

```python
# backend/app/support_model.py
if audited_count <= 0:
    recommendation = "collect_initial_audits"
elif coverage_ratio < _clamp01(min_audit_coverage_ratio):
    recommendation = "increase_audit_coverage"
elif weak_overlap_detected:
    recommendation = "widen_support_before_proxy_certification"
else:
    recommendation = "ready_for_support_aware_correction"
```

This is better than a proxy-only route model because it does not treat more predictions as more truth. A proxy model can be systematically wrong in exactly the regions where route decisions are hard. The repo therefore records audit coverage, propensity minima, support bins, correction metadata, leakage-safe training flags, and proxy-only fractions. The paper framing is support-aware evidence governance: proxy evidence can assist decisions, but weak overlap or missing audit coverage can trigger abstention or claim narrowing.

The proxy-audit record makes the residual correction inspectable:

```python
# backend/app/audit_correction.py
residual = audited - proxy
correction_factor = audited / proxy if proxy not in (0.0, -0.0) else 1.0
resolved_correction_applied = abs(residual) > 0.0
resolved_audit_probability = _clamp01(audit_probability)
resolved_propensity_score = _clamp01(propensity_score)
```

The wording for the published paper is precise: this is not a causal proof of unbiased freight evidence. It is better than naive proxy evaluation because it forces every proxy-corrected claim to expose residual bias, correction path, propensity metadata, support state, and audit coverage.

### AX73. Green-Freight Claims Must Be Carbon-Scope-Aware Rather Than Marketing-Style

The emissions contribution is written against green road freight and emissions-accounting literature. The Pollution-Routing Problem connects cost, emissions, speed, and routing [Bektas and Laporte 2011](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trb.2011.02.004). Demir, Bektas, and Laporte review green road-freight research and show why fuel, routing, and operational choices cannot be treated as a single constant factor [Demir et al. 2014](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2013.12.033). For accounting boundaries, the paper cites ISO 14083 [ISO 14083](https://www.iso.org/standard/78864.html), the GLEC Framework [Smart Freight Centre 2025, GLEC Framework v3.2](https://smart-freight-centre-media.s3.amazonaws.com/documents/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3.2_21_10_25_1.pdf), and established emissions-model families such as HBEFA, COPERT, and MOVES [HBEFA](https://www.hbefa.net/), [COPERT](https://www.emisia.com/utilities/copert/), [MOVES](https://www.epa.gov/moves).

The repo's design is better than a constant kg-CO2e-per-km multiplier because fuel and carbon are modeled as scoped evidence with provenance and uncertainty. The fuel-energy model keeps fuel, energy, emissions, price, uncertainty, and source metadata together:

```python
# backend/app/fuel_energy_model.py
FUEL_EMISSIONS_KG_PER_L = {
    "diesel": 2.68,
    "petrol": 2.31,
    "lng": 1.51,
}

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SegmentEnergyResult:
    fuel_liters: float
    fuel_liters_p10: float
    fuel_liters_p50: float
    fuel_liters_p90: float
    energy_kwh: float
    emissions_kg: float
    fuel_cost_gbp: float
    fuel_cost_uncertainty_low_gbp: float
    fuel_cost_uncertainty_high_gbp: float
    emissions_uncertainty_low_kg: float
    emissions_uncertainty_high_kg: float
    source: str
    price_source: str | None = None
    consumption_model_version: str | None = None
```

The carbon-pricing layer refuses weak provenance in strict mode:

```python
# backend/app/carbon_model.py
_PROVENANCE_DISALLOWED_TERMS = (
    "synthetic",
    "heuristic",
    "legacy",
    "interpolated",
    "simulated",
    "wobble",
)

def _reject_non_empirical_payload(
    payload: dict[str, object],
    *,
    reason_code: str,
    source_label: str,
) -> None:
    strict, _require_live_url, _allow_fallback, _pytest_bypass_enabled = _strict_live_carbon_policy()
    if not strict:
        return
    basis = str(payload.get("calibration_basis", payload.get("basis", ""))).strip().lower()
    if any(term in basis for term in _PROVENANCE_DISALLOWED_TERMS):
        raise ModelDataError(
            reason_code=reason_code,
            message="Carbon payload provenance is not empirical enough for strict runtime policy.",
            details={"source": source_label, "calibration_basis": basis},
        )
```

The paper states that this system is not a certified emissions-accounting product and does not replace ISO/GLEC reporting. Its advantage for research is different: it makes emissions a route-decision criterion with uncertainty, provenance, and strict failure modes. Other systems may provide stronger regulatory accounting or fleet-scale carbon reporting. WhatIf Freight Router is better for the thesis problem because emissions are co-optimised with time, money, risk, evidence support, and preference ambiguity instead of being a post-hoc label.

### AX74. Geospatial Data Quality, Map Matching, And Route-Graph Identity Are Core Limitations

Geospatial-data quality is a first-order limitation. OpenStreetMap is powerful but variable; Goodchild's volunteered geographic information framing and Haklay's OSM completeness analysis explain why coverage and quality need explicit treatment [Goodchild 2007](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10708-007-9111-y), [Haklay 2010](https://doi.org/10.1068/b35097). Map-matching literature such as Newson and Krumm's HMM method shows that connecting observed positions to road links is a nontrivial inference problem [Newson and Krumm 2009](https://doi.org/10.1145/1653771.1653818). This repo does not solve general map matching. It instead records route-graph identity, candidate diagnostics, source state, and support status so the route evidence can be audited.

Publication citation bridge: OD ambiguity should also cite address-geocoding and transport map-matching uncertainty. Zandbergen compares address point, parcel, and street geocoding and shows that the chosen geocoding reference affects positional accuracy [Zandbergen 2008](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compenvurbsys.2007.11.006). Quddus, Ochieng, and Noland survey map-matching constraints for transport applications [Quddus et al. 2007](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.trc.2007.05.002). This supports the report's claim that OD support ledgers and route-graph identity are evidence-quality controls, not guarantees of true physical origin/destination identity.

The route-graph diagnostics are small but important:

```python
# backend/app/routing_graph.py
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GraphCandidateDiagnostics:
    explored_states: int
    generated_paths: int
    emitted_paths: int
    candidate_budget: int
    effective_max_hops: int = 0
    effective_hops_floor: int = 0
    effective_state_budget_initial: int = 0
    effective_state_budget: int = 0
    no_path_reason: str = ""
    no_path_detail: str = ""
```

This is better than simply saying "no route found" because the failure carries search evidence. A route may fail because the graph is fragmented, the candidate budget was too small, the hop floor was too strict, a component mismatch exists, or the state budget was exhausted. Those are different scientific meanings. Route-graph failure is not a generic runtime failure; it is evidence about the support of the candidate-generation process.

### AX75. Reproducibility Is Strongest When Negative Results And Workflows Are Artifacted

Computational reproducibility literature supports the artifact-evidence design. Peng argues that reproducible computational science requires enough detail for others to inspect the computation [Peng 2011](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1213847). Sandve et al. provide practical reproducibility rules for computational research [Sandve et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285). FAIR and PROV explain why metadata, identity, and provenance matter [Wilkinson et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18), [W3C PROV-DM](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/). ACM artifact review gives the publication lens [ACM artifact review](https://www.acm.org/publications/policies/artifact-review-and-badging-current).

The evaluator is built as a reproducibility surface, not just a script:

```python
# backend/scripts/run_thesis_evaluation.py
parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20260320)
parser.add_argument(
    "--seed-repeat-count",
    type=int,
    default=1,
    help="Configured seed-repeat plan for lane metadata. This annotates reporting surfaces and does not rerun the evaluator by itself.",
)
parser.add_argument("--search-budget", type=int, default=4)
parser.add_argument("--evidence-budget", type=int, default=2)
parser.add_argument("--world-count", type=int, default=64)
parser.add_argument("--certificate-threshold", type=float, default=0.80)
parser.add_argument("--tau-stop", type=float, default=0.02)
parser.add_argument("--cache-mode", choices=THESIS_CACHE_MODES, default="preserve")
parser.add_argument("--baseline-refinement-policy", choices=("first_n", "random_n", "corridor_uniform"), default="corridor_uniform")
```

The defaults are paper-relevant. `seed=20260320` makes deterministic reruns comparable. `search-budget=4` and `evidence-budget=2` bound the controller so improvements cannot be explained only by unlimited computation. `world-count=64` and `certificate-threshold=0.80` define the certification world and threshold used by the evaluation surface. `tau-stop=0.02` sets a small stop tolerance so the controller does not continue chasing negligible predicted gains. `baseline-refinement-policy="corridor_uniform"` gives the baseline a route-diversity-aware refinement policy rather than an artificially weak first-N baseline.

Reproducibility includes negative and bounded evidence. The maintained checked suite currently records an applied-evidence green verdict rather than declaring theorem-grade or deployment victory. That is better than a greenwashed artifact because artifact review depends on being able to reproduce both successes and limitations. The paper can therefore state that the project demonstrates a reproducible evidence architecture; it cannot state that the system is deployment-ready or theorem-complete.

### AX76. Likely Reviewer Questions And Direct Paper-Ready Answers

A reviewer may ask whether this is just OSRM plus a dashboard. The answer is no: OSRM or ORS can provide routing substrate evidence, but the paper contribution is the decision layer above routing. The system records candidate search, support, preference ambiguity, certificate state, risk, provenance, and abstention. It does not compete with CH/CRP/MLD routers on raw query speed; it uses routing as one input to a decision contract.

A reviewer may ask whether DCCS is just K-shortest paths with a different name. The answer is no: K-shortest-path algorithms generate ranked paths by path cost or constrained variants. DCCS ranks candidates by decision criticality: winner lower-bound lift, pairwise gap lift, flip-radius lift, unresolved winner mass, preference relevance, search-deficiency risk, and action cost. That makes it a certification-aware triage layer, not a path generator.

A reviewer may ask whether the preference model is just weighted-sum MCDA. The answer is no: the weighted sum is only one scoring surface. The repo also models compatible weight sets, possible-best and necessary-best routes, preference shrinkage, stop hints, and typed abstention when preference ambiguity prevents singleton certification. Weighted sums, TOPSIS, AHP, ELECTRE, PROMETHEE, SMAA, and robust ordinal regression are useful comparators, but the project is better for this thesis problem because it joins preference uncertainty to route evidence and terminal certification.

A reviewer may ask whether the system overstates emissions precision. The answer is no if the paper keeps the current wording: emissions are model-conditioned and provenance-scoped. The system co-optimises emissions with freight decisions, but it does not replace ISO 14083, GLEC, HBEFA, COPERT, MOVES, or regulated fleet accounting. That limitation is a strength because it prevents carbon marketing claims from replacing scientific evidence.

A reviewer may ask whether the evaluation establishes universal superiority. The answer is no. The evaluation supports lane-specific, artifact-specific, UK-scoped claims under named settings and evidence policies. The strongest publishable contribution is the architecture and evidence discipline, plus measured lane behavior where checked artifacts support the claim. Remaining limitations are research boundaries and future-work constraints, not missing polish.

The final paper therefore uses this hierarchy of claims. The safest high-level claim is that the project designs and implements an auditable selective route-decision architecture. The next claim is that the implementation exposes concrete evidence surfaces for search, evidence, preference, risk, support, provenance, and refusal. The empirical claim is limited to generated checked artifacts and current gate status. The limitation claim is explicit: the current evidence does not prove global deployment readiness, legal truck compliance, complete carbon accounting, conformal validity, or formal VOI optimality.

### AX77. Artifact Packaging, Current Verdict, And Self-Containment Closure

The report also needs one final artifact-packaging statement because a published paper reviewer will ask where the evidence root is. The evidence root is not the rendered PDF or SVG alone. Rendered figures and tables are presentation surfaces. The evidence roots are populated CSV/JSON metric sources, provenance companions, lane manifests, checked bundle indexes, verdict JSON files, and `source_files` references that generated those presentation surfaces. Rendered SVG/PDF/HTML files and empty co-packaged figure source JSONs are presentation/export companions, not metric roots. This is aligned with FAIR and PROV framing: the important publication object is not just a pretty result; it is an inspectable chain from source data and settings to an artifact identity [Wilkinson et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18), [W3C PROV-DM](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/).

The root reviewer package index is `paper_artifact_index.json`, with `schema_version="paper_artifact_index.v1"` and `status="current_checked_local_slice"`. Its notes state that it is conservative and only lists checked local artifact files that exist in the repository workspace. That matters because it prevents the paper from citing aspirational outputs. The index distinguishes reviewer-facing headline paper surfaces, supporting non-headline paper surfaces, and reviewer-package companion bundles. It also records the critical limitation that some older focused-VOI sidecars still point at a single-seed family; repeated-seed preference-burden evidence lives separately in the newer focused-VOI proof bundle and seed companions. That distinction belongs in the paper because it prevents a reader from treating every staged table as repeated-seed proof.

### AX78. Published-Paper Completeness Ledger: What The Paper Must Say And Where The Evidence Lives

The next paper should not be written as a tour of the repository. It should be written as a design-science and applied-algorithm paper whose artifact is a freight-route decision-support system with auditable evidence boundaries. That framing is supported by Hevner, March, Park, and Ram's design-science account of IT artifacts as research contributions when they are rigorously built and evaluated [Hevner et al. 2004](https://doi.org/10.2307/25148625), Wieringa's design-science methodology for information systems and software engineering [Wieringa 2014](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-662-43839-8), and ACM artifact-review practice, which treats code/data artifacts as inspectable evidence rather than private implementation detail [ACM artifact review](https://www.acm.org/publications/policies/artifact-review-and-badging-current).

The core paper question is not "can a shortest path be found?" because Dijkstra, A*, CH/CRP/MLD, OSRM, ORS, PTV, Mapbox, and commercial logistics optimizers already cover large parts of that space. The core paper question is: can a freight-route system make a recommendation only when the recommendation is backed by route evidence, preference evidence, uncertainty evidence, support evidence, and reproducible artifact evidence, and otherwise refuse with a useful next action? That is the problem addressed and implemented by the codebase, with current empirical support anchored in the applied-evidence green checked verdict and in the detailed DCCS, refine-cost, and VOI lane artifacts. It is hard because it joins four hard subproblems that are usually separated: road-network routing, alternative/choice-set generation, multi-criteria preference uncertainty, and evidence-bounded certification under live and proxy data.

The paper should make the following claims explicitly, in this order:

| Paper claim | Why it belongs in the paper | Local evidence | External framing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The problem is freight-route decision support, not generic shortest-path routing. | A reviewer will otherwise compare only raw routing speed. | `backend/app/routing_osrm.py`, `backend/app/routing_ors.py`, `backend/app/voi_controller.py`, `backend/app/certification_models.py` | Route-planning surveys such as [Delling et al. 2009](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-02094-0_7) and [Bast et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-49487-6_2) |
| Candidate adequacy is decision-critical, not just K-shortest enumeration. | A large set of alternatives is useless if it does not change certification or preference ambiguity. | `backend/app/candidate_criticality.py`, `backend/app/decision_critical.py`, `backend/app/voi_dccs_cache.py` | Route-choice and choice-set literature: [Prato 2009](https://doi.org/10.1016/S1755-5345(13)70005-8), [Bovy 2009](https://doi.org/10.1080/01441640802078673), [Ben-Akiva and Bierlaire 1999](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4615-5203-1_2) |
| MCDA is necessary but insufficient by itself. | Weighted scores can hide unsupported or preference-ambiguous choices. | `backend/app/objectives_selection.py`, `backend/app/preference_state.py`, `backend/app/preference_update.py` | MCDA and robust ordinal regression sources already cited in AX43-AX61 |
| Selective abstention is a positive design feature. | A system that always returns one route can be unsafe or misleading when evidence is weak. | `backend/app/abstention.py`, `backend/app/certified_set.py`, `backend/app/confidence_sequences.py` | Reject-option and selective-classification literature: [Chow 1970](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406), [El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/el-yaniv10a.html) |
| Tail risk is a bounded route-decision penalty, not a universal robust optimum. | A paper needs to explain why downside route worlds affect decisions without overclaiming distributional robustness. | `backend/app/risk_model.py`, `backend/app/uncertainty_model.py`, `backend/app/confidence_sequences.py`, risk fields in route/evaluation artifacts | Coherent risk and CVaR sources: [Artzner et al. 1999](https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9965.00068), [Rockafellar and Uryasev 2000](https://doi.org/10.21314/JOR.2000.038) |
