The artifact writer then normalises JSON, writes a summary companion, and refreshes the bundle index:

```python
# backend/app/run_store.py
def write_json_artifact(run_id: str, artifact_name: str, payload: dict[str, Any] | list[Any]) -> Path:
    path = artifact_path_for_name(run_id, artifact_name)
    normalized = jsonable_encoder(payload)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(normalized, indent=2, default=str), encoding="utf-8")
    _write_json_summary_companion(run_id, artifact_name, normalized)
    _refresh_route_bundle_index_if_ready(run_id, artifact_name=artifact_name)
    return path
```

The method section should state that this is the repository's answer to "how did you evaluate it?" The evaluation combines aggregate metrics with the ability to replay or inspect requests, selected candidates, warning lists, candidate diagnostics, certificates, VOI stop summaries, sampled-world manifests, support summaries, route traces, provenance events, metadata, and artifact indexes. This aligns with reproducibility and artifact-review expectations, but remains bounded: the current checked suite supports an applied-evidence paper while the report still preserves deployment and theorem limits. That is a stronger design/evidence architecture claim than a route demo because a reviewer can inspect what was supported, what was narrowed, and what remains future validation.

The paper should use the following claim/evidence mapping to avoid leaving important items implicit:

| Paper claim | External basis | Repo evidence to cite | Safe wording |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Route recommendation under uncertainty should allow refusal. | Reject-option classification [Chow 1970](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406), selective classification [El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/el-yaniv10a.html). | `backend/app/abstention.py`, decision package, certificate summaries, failure atlas. | The system emits typed abstention when support is insufficient; it does not prove real-world optimality. |
| Candidate alternatives must be evidence objects. | K-shortest and alternative-route literature [Yen 1971](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.17.11.712), [Eppstein 1998](https://doi.org/10.1137/S0097539795290477), [Abraham et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.1145/2444016.2444019). | DCCS candidate ledgers, search budgets, hidden-challenger/search-deficiency fields. | DCCS ranks decision-critical candidates and exposes search-evidence state; exhaustive-search proof remains outside the current evidence. |
| Robust route evidence needs bounded worlds and support metadata. | Robust optimisation and CVaR literature [Ben-Tal and Nemirovski 2002](https://doi.org/10.1007/s101070100286), [Rockafellar and Uryasev 2000](https://doi.org/10.21314/JOR.2000.038), [Filippi et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cor.2025.107096). | `sampled_world_manifest.json`, `world_support_summary.json`, certificate summaries, fragility maps. | The repo certifies within sampled evidence worlds and support assumptions, not over all possible futures. |
| Preference uncertainty should remain visible. | Preference elicitation and MCDA/ROR/SMAA literature [Boutilier et al. 2006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2006.02.003), [Lahdelma et al. 1998](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(97)00163-X), [Greco et al. 2008](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2007.08.013). | `PreferenceState`, compatible-set summaries, preference query traces. | The repo uses finite compatible-set evidence and typed queries; it does not learn a user's true utility function. |
| More computation should be justified by decision value. | VOI and bounded-rational metareasoning [Howard 1966](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1966.300074), [Russell and Wefald 1991](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(91)90015-C). | `voi_controller.py`, `voi_action_trace.json`, `voi_action_scores.csv`, `voi_stop_certificate.json`. | VOI is a deterministic surrogate controller with traces, not a Bayes-optimal policy. |
| Research software must expose artifacts and provenance. | FAIR [Wilkinson et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18), W3C PROV, ACM artifact review, REST/API design [Fielding 2000](https://www.ics.uci.edu/~fielding/pubs/dissertation/top.htm). | run bundles, `metadata.json`, `provenance`, signatures, docs checks. | The system is artifacted and inspectable; some generated evidence remains local-only or bounded to the checked reviewer package. |

The equations in the final paper should be written as adapted decision contracts, not as unmodified textbook algorithms. The canonical scalar route choice is:

```text
r* = argmin_r E[C(r)]
```

The repo's decision object is closer to:

```text
d* in {certified_singleton(r), certified_set(R), abstain(reason)}

subject to candidate support, evidence support, preference support,
budget support, and model-assumption support.
```

That change is the core originality. It replaces a path-only minimizer with a terminal decision family. It is not mathematically stronger than every robust shortest-path formulation, but it is more appropriate for the applied paper because it exposes the practical reasons a route recommendation should or should not be made.

The canonical CVaR expression is:

```text
CVaR_alpha(L) = min_eta eta + (1 / (1 - alpha)) * E[max(L - eta, 0)]
```

The repo should not claim that every risk term is a full formal CVaR optimisation. Its risk-family code deliberately labels `cvar_excess` as the default tail-excess penalty and treats entropic/downside variants as thesis-specific penalties on CVaR excess. The paper should say that the route selector borrows from tail-risk reasoning while keeping the implementation boundary explicit.

The canonical VOI expression compares expected utility before and after buying information:

```text
VOI = E[max_a U(a | new information)] - max_a E[U(a | current information)] - cost
```

The repo's VOI surrogate instead uses certificate lift, margin/frontier adequacy, search deficiency, preference ambiguity, and action cost. That is a deliberate engineering modification. It makes the controller auditable and cheap enough for route-level interaction, while preserving the limitation that the scoring is not a proof of optimal metareasoning.

The paper's limitations paragraph should be blunt. Scientific limits are UK-scoped evidence, route-level rather than fleet-level optimisation, no theorem-backed end-to-end optimality, no conformal distribution-free coverage claim, finite compatible-set preference approximation, and route-level emissions evidence rather than formal regulated inventory accounting. Deployment limits are legal HGV restriction completeness, bridge/height/weight enforcement, dangerous-goods compliance, validated dispatcher trust calibration, production security/privacy/data-retention review, and enterprise integration. The right conclusion is not "the system is finished." The right conclusion is "the system demonstrates a concrete, inspectable architecture for evidence-bounded freight-route decision support, with clear boundaries that define the next research cycle."

The paper should also identify the next research cycle as a direct consequence of the current boundaries: broaden DCCS frontier-coverage evidence; deepen refine-cost calibration; evaluate VOI behavior across more operating regimes; run a human-subjects or expert-dispatcher study for calibrated reliance; broaden support beyond the current UK evidence slice; and add a frozen external artifact release if publication requires independent artifact review. This turns the current boundaries into a research agenda rather than a weakness hidden in an appendix.

### AX93. Publication-Ready Claim Catalogue, Literature Anchors, Algorithm Box, And Code Evidence

This section is the paper-writing bank. It identifies the statements the actual published paper is likely to need, gives the safest wording, cites the external literature, and points to exact code evidence. It is deliberately written as prose and code evidence rather than as a checklist, because the aim of this report is to let the thesis writer lift complete arguments into the paper without re-reading the whole repository.

The central contribution should be described as follows: WhatIf Freight Router implements an evidence-bounded freight-route decision architecture. It does not replace road-routing engines, fleet optimisers, emissions-accounting standards, or legal HGV compliance systems. It uses routing engines and route candidates as inputs, then asks whether the evidence justifies a terminal decision. That is a stronger and narrower claim than "better routing." It is better for a publishable applied thesis when the objective is inspectable decision support because the output can say: this route is certified, this set is certified, more search is needed, more evidence is needed, a preference question is needed, the world model is out of support, the budget is exhausted, or the assumptions are too weak.

The paper should include the following method box as "Algorithm 1." It is the simplest way to prevent reviewers from seeing the project as a loose collection of features.

```text
Algorithm 1: Evidence-bounded freight-route decision package

Input:
  OD request, vehicle/scenario/cost settings, preference state,
  route-search budget B_s, evidence budget B_e, world count W,
  certification threshold tau, VOI stop threshold tau_stop.

1. Run strict request/readiness checks.
2. Generate raw graph candidates K_raw under bounded search.
3. Build a DCCS ledger for every candidate:
     objective proxy, mechanism descriptor, overlap, stretch,
     hidden-challenger/search-deficiency signals, predicted refine cost.
4. Select a bounded candidate subset for refinement:
     if no strict frontier exists, bootstrap diverse evidence candidates;
     otherwise reserve anti-collapse candidates and rank by decision-critical evidence:
     objective/mechanism gaps, overlap, stretch, flip pressure, preference sensitivity,
     expected proxy/audit value, search completeness, hidden-challenger risk, and cost.
5. Refine selected candidates through the routing provider into R.
6. Compute freight objectives, support/provenance features, and the strict frontier F.
7. Run Route-Evidence Frontier Certification (REFC) when pipeline_mode is dccs_refc or voi:
     sample bounded evidence worlds, compute winner/family support,
     pairwise gaps, fragility, value-of-refresh, and certified-set state.
8. Run VOI-AD2R when pipeline_mode is voi:
     score search/evidence/preference actions by predicted decision gain per cost;
     stop when certificate and search/support conditions are adequate or no action is worth its cost.
9. Emit one terminal DecisionPackage:
     certified_singleton(route), certified_set(routes), or typed_abstention(reason, remedy).
10. Persist manifest, decision_package.json, certificate/VOI/support artifacts, provenance, and summaries.
```

The first important code anchor is DCCS selection. Source: `backend/app/decision_critical.py`.

```python
def select_candidates(candidates, *, frontier=(), refined=(), config=None):
    cfg = config or DCCSConfig()
    ledger = build_candidate_ledger(candidates, frontier=frontier, refined=refined, config=cfg)
    selected, skipped = [], []
    budget = max(0, int(cfg.search_budget))

    if cfg.mode == "bootstrap":
        remaining = list(ledger)
        while remaining and len(selected) < budget:
            ranked = sorted(
                remaining,
                key=lambda record: (
                    -_bootstrap_score(record, selected=selected, candidate_pool=ledger, config=cfg),
                    record.near_duplicate,
                    record.candidate_id,
                ),
            )
            record = ranked[0]
            reason = "selected_by_bootstrap"
            if record.graph_path in {item.graph_path for item in selected}:
                reason = "duplicate_signature"
            elif any(item.corridor_signature == record.corridor_signature for item in selected[: max(1, cfg.bootstrap_seed_size - 1)]):
                reason = "duplicate_corridor_bootstrap"
            chosen = replace(
                record,
                decision="refine" if reason == "selected_by_bootstrap" else "skip",
                decision_reason=reason,
                selection_rank=len(selected) if reason == "selected_by_bootstrap" else None,
            )
            selected.append(chosen) if chosen.decision == "refine" else skipped.append(chosen)
            remaining = [item for item in remaining if item.candidate_id != record.candidate_id]
    else:
        reserved_records = _reserve_anti_collapse_records(ledger, config=cfg)
        effective_budget = max(budget, len(reserved_records))
        ...
```

This snippet matters because it shows a candidate policy with more structure than "take the first k paths." Bootstrap mode explicitly rejects duplicate signatures and early duplicate corridors; challenger mode reserves anti-collapse records before spending the remaining budget by decision-critical score. That design is justified by alternative-route literature, which shows that route alternatives must be diverse and meaningful rather than merely next-shortest [Akgun et al. 2000](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(99)00214-3), [Abraham et al. 2010](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-13193-6_3), [Chondrogiannis et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00778-020-00604-x). What the repo changes is the scoring target: an alternative is valuable when it can change the decision evidence, alongside being short or non-overlapping.

The second code anchor is the public decision family. Source: `backend/app/main.py`.

```python
if abstention is not None:
    terminal_type = "typed_abstention"
    public_selected = None
    public_recommended = None
    public_certified_set = []
elif len(raw_certified_set) > 1:
    terminal_type = "certified_set"
    public_selected = None
    public_recommended = None
    public_certified_set = raw_certified_set
else:
    terminal_type = "certified_singleton"
    public_selected = selected
    public_recommended = selected
    public_certified_set = []
```

That code is the compact answer to "what problem was solved?" The project implements a route API where the terminal response is not forced to be a route. It can be a singleton, a set, or a refusal. This is the route-decision adaptation of selective prediction and reject-option reasoning [Chow 1970](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406), [El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/el-yaniv10a.html), while keeping the certification wording closer to assurance-case practice than to legal approval [Kelly 2004](https://doi.org/10.4271/2004-01-1779), [Habli and Kelly 2013](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ssci.2013.04.007).

The public response model makes that contract explicit. Source: `backend/app/models.py`.

```python
class DecisionPackage(BaseModel):
    terminal_type: Literal["certified_singleton", "certified_set", "typed_abstention"] = "certified_singleton"
    selected: RouteOption | None = None
    candidates: list[RouteOption] = Field(default_factory=list)
    recommended_route: RouteOption | None = None
    certified_set: list[RouteOption] = Field(default_factory=list)
    abstention: AbstentionRecord | None = None
    selected_certificate: RouteCertificationSummary | None = None
    winner_confidence_state: WinnerConfidenceState | dict[str, Any] | None = None
    pairwise_gap_states: list[PairwiseGapState | dict[str, Any]] = Field(default_factory=list)
    preference_state: PreferenceState = Field(default_factory=PreferenceState)
    support_summary: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    world_support_summary: dict[str, Any] | DecisionWorldSupportSummary = Field(default_factory=dict)
    abstention_summary: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    certified_set_summary: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    artifact_pointers: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
```

The paper should say that this response is stronger than a conventional route JSON for auditability because it puts the route, alternatives, certificate state, confidence state, pairwise gaps, preference state, support state, abstention state, and artifact pointers in the same typed object. It should not say this proves operational superiority over Google Routes, HERE, PTV, ORTEC, Descartes, Transporeon, OSRM, openrouteservice, or GraphHopper. Those systems remain stronger for production map coverage, fleet planning, or logistics integration. The superiority claim is only for the research objective: inspectable route-decision evidence.

The third code anchor is certified-set safety. Source: `backend/app/certified_set.py`.

```python
@property
def safe(self) -> bool:
    return bool(self.certified and self.support_flag)

certified = bool(
    support_flag
    and decision_certified
    and winner_score >= threshold_value
    and excluded
)
exclusion_basis = [
    "confidence_state_threshold",
    "decision_region_certified" if decision_certified else "decision_region_not_certified",
    "winner_threshold_met" if winner_score >= threshold_value else "winner_threshold_not_met",
]
if not support_flag:
    exclusion_basis.append("support_flag_false")
```

The important point is that `safe` is not a synonym for "winner has a high empirical score." It requires certification and support. The winner threshold is only one term. The decision-region certificate, challenger exclusion, and support flag also matter. This is how the repo avoids the common applied-systems error of presenting a high score as proof. The paper should connect this to robust and stochastic routing literature by saying that the repo does not solve every uncertainty model; it exposes the support state of the bounded evidence model it actually used [Fan et al. 2005](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.camwa.2004.07.028), [Dokka and Goerigk 2017](https://doi.org/10.4230/OASIcs.ATMOS.2017.16), [Chassein et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2018.10.006).

The fourth code anchor is typed abstention. Source: `backend/app/abstention.py`.

```python
def recommended_action(self) -> str:
    action = self.detail.get("recommended_action")
    if action:
        return str(action)
    return {
        "typed_abstention_recommended": "expand_worlds",
        "uncertified_due_to_search": "expand_search",
        "uncertified_due_to_evidence": "refresh_evidence",
        "uncertified_due_to_preference": "ask_preference",
        "uncertified_due_to_out_of_support_world_model": "expand_world_model",
        "uncertified_due_to_budget": "increase_budget",
        "uncertified_due_to_model_assumption": "review_model_assumptions",
    }[self.reason_code]
```

This is better than a generic "unable to certify" response because each refusal is actionable. Search failure asks for more search. Evidence failure asks for refresh. Preference failure asks for elicitation. Out-of-support failure asks for an expanded world model. Budget failure asks for more budget. Model-assumption failure asks for assumption review. The external literature gives the legitimacy of refusal; the repo adds domain-specific diagnosis and remedy.

The fifth code anchor is conservative reason classification. Source: `backend/app/abstention.py`.

```python
if budget_text or _contains_any(stop_text, ("budget", "exhausted", "quota")):
    return "uncertified_due_to_budget"

if support_flag is False or _contains_any(
    support_text,
    ("out_of_support", "unsupported", "outside_support", "out of support"),
):
    return "uncertified_due_to_out_of_support_world_model"

if credible_search_uncertainty is True or _contains_any(
    stop_text,
    ("search_incomplete", "no_action_worth_it", "search_uncertain", "insufficient_search"),
) or (search_completeness_score is not None and search_completeness_score < 0.5) or (
    search_completeness_gap is not None and search_completeness_gap > 0.0
):
    return "uncertified_due_to_search"
```

This ordering should be justified in the paper. Budget and support failures are handled first because they invalidate stronger claims regardless of preference or score. Search failure is next because hidden challengers can break the recommendation even if the current top route looks good. Evidence and preference failures follow because they require different remedies. The fallback to model-assumption abstention is conservative: when the system cannot name a more specific evidence problem, it refuses the strongest claim rather than overfitting a reason.

The exact mathematical deviation from common academic norms can be stated as five equations.

```text
Classical route output:
  r* = argmin_r sum_{e in r} c_e

This repo's terminal object:
  d* in {certified_singleton(r), certified_set(S), typed_abstention(reason)}

DCCS candidate value:
  criticality(c) =
    [winner_lcb_lift + pairwise_gap_lcb_lift + flip_radius_lift
     + unresolved_winner_mass + preference_relevance + search_deficiency_risk]
    / max(1, predicted_refine_cost)

REFC safety:
  safe(S) = certified(S) and support_flag(S)

VOI action score:
  Q(a) = predicted_decision_gain(a) / (action_cost(a) + epsilon)
```

Those equations explain why the project is not just MCDA. A weighted sum, VIKOR score, or Tchebycheff scalarizer chooses within the current candidate set [Marler and Arora 2010](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00158-009-0460-7), [Opricovic and Tzeng 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(03)00020-1). The repo keeps scalar ranking but wraps it in candidate adequacy, support, bounded evidence worlds, preference-state shrinkage, VOI, and refusal. That is why the modified scalarizer should be framed as an engineering selector rather than the main theoretical invention.

The UK applied context should be stated with current public evidence. Department for Transport statistics report that domestic freight in the UK moved `206` billion tonne-kilometres in 2024 and that the majority, `82%`, was moved by road [DfT Transport Statistics Great Britain 2024 freight](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/transport-statistics-great-britain-2025/transport-statistics-great-britain-2024-freight). DfT road-freight statistics separately report `168` billion tonne-kilometres moved by GB-registered HGVs in 2024 [DfT Road freight statistics 2024](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/road-freight-statistics-2024). The UK Future of Freight plan names data and technology, net zero, people and skills, planning, and the National Freight Network as policy priorities [Future of Freight plan](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/future-of-freight-plan). The paper can use those facts to justify why UK road freight is a meaningful applied domain, but it must also say the repo is not a full legal compliance engine. Drivers' hours [GOV.UK drivers' hours](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/drivers-hours-goods-vehicles), maximum HGV weights [GOV.UK HGV maximum weights](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/hgv-maximum-weights/hgv-maximum-weights), Clean Air Zones [GOV.UK Clean Air Zones](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/driving-in-a-clean-air-zone), dangerous-goods rules, and bridge/height/weight constraints require data and checks that are not proved complete by this repository.

The strongest "why mine is better" paragraph should be bounded and specific:

Compared with a routing engine, this project is better for a research paper about auditable freight-route decisions because it preserves the decision evidence after a path is found. Compared with a VRP/TMS optimizer, it is better for explaining one route recommendation because it exposes certification, support, preference ambiguity, and refusal rather than only a dispatch plan. Compared with plain MCDA, it is better because the score is not the final authority; support, candidate adequacy, preference ambiguity, and typed abstention can still block the route. Compared with robust optimisation, it is better for this prototype when uncertainty sets are not fully validated because it states the bounded evidence-world assumptions and can refuse out-of-support cases. Compared with emissions standards, it is not better for official carbon accounting; it is better for route-decision transparency because route-level emissions assumptions are visible alongside cost, time, risk, and evidence state.

The final paper should be explicit about what would falsify stronger future claims. A future deployment-grade DCCS claim would need broader hidden-challenger, pruning, and certificate-critical evidence. A future VOI claim would need stronger evidence that refinement actions are useful across operating regimes and that realized certificate movement is robust. A future preference claim would need compatible-set shrinkage to reduce decision ambiguity without contradiction. A future certification claim would need strong support flags, wide enough world manifests, and stable optional-stopping/perturbation behavior. A future reproducibility claim is falsified if artifacts cannot be located, manifests are stale, docs checks fail, or the published bundle cannot be independently inspected.

### AX94. Thesis Title, Chapter Spine, Mathematical Claim Ledger, And Publishability Critique

This section exists to connect the proposed thesis table of contents to the master evidence base. It should be treated as the bridge from this report to the final paper or dissertation draft. The goal is not to create a new plan that points away from the codebase; the goal is to make sure each planned thesis section has enough technical substance, citations, equations, code evidence, and limitation wording to be defensible without changing the implementation.

The best title should avoid overclaiming legal certification, global freight optimisation, or deployment readiness. The strongest title is:

```text
Evidence-Bounded Freight Route Decision Support
```

The strongest subtitle is:

```text
Route-Evidence Certification, Value-of-Information Control, and Typed Abstention for UK Road Freight
```

The full recommended title is therefore:

```text
Evidence-Bounded Freight Route Decision Support:
Route-Evidence Certification, Value-of-Information Control, and Typed Abstention for UK Road Freight
```

This title is stronger than "WhatIf Freight Router" alone because it names the research contribution rather than the product name. It is stronger than "Certified Freight Routing" because it avoids implying regulatory certification. It is stronger than "A Better Freight Router" because the current evidence does not support universal route-quality superiority. It is also stronger than "Multiobjective Freight Routing" because multiobjective routing is not the full novelty; the novelty is the evidence-bounded terminal decision family.

Acceptable alternatives, in descending order, are:

| Candidate title | Strength | Weakness |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Evidence-Bounded Freight Route Decision Support: Route-Evidence Certification, Value-of-Information Control, and Typed Abstention for UK Road Freight` | Most accurate. Names the core contribution and the UK applied boundary without implying regulatory certification. | Long, but appropriate for a thesis. |
| `From Shortest Paths to Auditable Freight Route Decisions: Evidence-Bounded Certification and Abstention for UK Road Freight` | Very readable and directly connects the thesis journey. | Slightly less specific about VOI. |
| `Auditable Freight Routing Under Search, Evidence, and Preference Uncertainty` | Elegant and broad. | Does not mention the concrete terminal outputs. |
| `Selective Route Certification for Evidence-Aware Freight Decision Support` | Compact and paper-like. | Could be mistaken for formal safety/regulatory certification unless the subtitle is careful. |
| `WhatIf Freight Router: An Evidence-Bounded Decision Architecture for UK Road Freight` | Keeps the system name. | Better as a project artifact title than as the academic title. |

The proposed thesis outline is workable, but it should be rewritten around an argument rather than a code tour. Mary Shaw's advice on software-engineering papers is relevant here: a good software-engineering research paper must make the research question, contribution type, and validation approach clear rather than only describe a system [Shaw 2003](https://doi.org/10.1109/ICSE.2003.1201262). Design-science research gives the right methodological frame because this is an implemented artifact evaluated against a practical problem [Hevner et al. 2004](https://doi.org/10.2307/25148625), [Peffers et al. 2007](https://doi.org/10.2753/MIS0742-1222240302). The evaluation chapter should be framed using design-science evaluation and empirical software-engineering practice rather than as a loose demo [Venable et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1057/ejis.2014.36), [Runeson and Host 2009](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10664-008-9102-8), [Wohlin et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-29044-2).

The chapter text should then be written as an argument, not as a list of files. The introduction should begin with the operational fact that a freight route recommendation is a decision made under incomplete search, conflicting objectives, uncertain evidence, and incomplete user preference information. A shortest-path engine can answer "which path is cheapest under this cost function"; this thesis asks a more constrained and more publishable question: when is the available evidence strong enough to recommend, when should the system return a set, and when should it abstain with a typed reason? That wording gives the thesis a serious applied-computing problem while keeping legal, commercial, and logistical deployment validation as separate evidence layers.

Chapter 1 should present the three-modification framework as the thesis' main intellectual move. The first modification is DCCS: candidate generation is redirected from "more alternatives" to "decision-critical alternatives." The second modification is REFC: route choice is not accepted unless the evidence world and challenger set support the claim. The third modification is VOI-AD2R: extra computation is treated as a budgeted action with inspectable value rather than as an unlimited hidden loop. These are stronger than a conventional application build because each modification changes the decision contract. They are weaker than a new theoretical routing algorithm because they do not replace Dijkstra, A*, contraction hierarchies, Yen, Eppstein, or route-engine internals. The thesis should be proud of the integration, but it should not claim a new shortest-path algorithm.

Chapter 2 should make the related-work comparison explicit. Road-network routing is mature: Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm [Dijkstra 1959](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01386390), A* [Hart, Nilsson, and Raphael 1968](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1968.300136), contraction hierarchies [Geisberger et al. 2008](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68552-4_24), and route-planning surveys [Bast et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-49487-6_2) explain why fast road routing itself is not the novel claim. K-shortest and alternative-route work [Yen 1971](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.17.11.712), [Eppstein 1998](https://doi.org/10.1137/S0097539795290477), [Akgun, Erkut, and Batta 2000](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(99)00214-3), [Abraham et al. 2010](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-13193-6_3), and [Chondrogiannis et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00778-020-00604-x) explains why returning more alternatives is also not enough. The thesis contribution starts after these methods have produced route evidence: it decides whether the evidence justifies a terminal decision.

Commercial and open-source route engines should be described as essential baselines, not as straw men. OSRM and OpenStreetMap-backed routing are mature enough that this thesis should not claim superiority over them at low-level graph search [Huber and Rust 2016](https://doi.org/10.1177/1536867X1601600209), and the OSRM backend itself is an established open-source routing-engine family [Project OSRM](https://github.com/Project-OSRM/osrm-backend). The thesis is better for auditable freight decision support because it preserves the route evidence, certificate state, abstention reason, provenance, and artifacts around the route. That is a different benchmark from raw routing speed or map coverage. A fair sentence for the paper is: "The system uses route engines as evidence suppliers and contributes the decision-evidence layer above them."

Vehicle-routing and transport-management optimisation should also be treated carefully. The vehicle routing problem and its variants focus on fleet-level assignment, capacity, time windows, depots, and multi-stop route plans [Toth and Vigo 2002](https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9780898718515.ch1). Green vehicle routing extends this to energy and emissions objectives [Lin et al. 2014](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2013.07.107). Those papers are not "worse" than this project; they solve a different optimisation scale. My solution is better only for the narrower thesis problem of explaining and certifying a route-decision recommendation for a single requested routing context. It is not better for full fleet dispatch, depot scheduling, vehicle loading, or multi-day logistics planning.

Emissions-accounting standards should be used as boundaries. ISO 14083 provides a transport-chain GHG quantification and reporting methodology [ISO 14083:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/78864.html), the GLEC Framework provides logistics-emissions accounting guidance [Smart Freight Centre GLEC Framework](https://www.smartfreightcentre.org/documents/328/GLEC_FRAMEWORK_v3_UPDATED_02_04_24.pdf), and the GHG Protocol Product Standard covers product life-cycle GHG reporting [GHG Protocol Product Standard](https://ghgprotocol.org/product-standard). This project is not better than those standards for official emissions reporting. It is better for decision transparency inside the prototype because emissions assumptions appear beside time, money, support, provenance, and certification state. The paper should therefore say "model-conditioned CO2e decision evidence," not "certified emissions accounting."

MCDA should be described as a foundation rather than an opponent. Weighted sums, TOPSIS, VIKOR, Tchebycheff scalarisation, and multiobjective methods provide accepted ways to compare conflicting criteria [Hwang and Yoon 1981](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-48318-9), [Belton and Stewart 2002](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4615-1495-4), [Opricovic and Tzeng 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(03)00020-1), [Marler and Arora 2010](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00158-009-0460-7). The project differs because MCDA rank is not the final authority. A route can rank well and still be blocked by support failure, challenger evidence, preference ambiguity, budget exhaustion, or out-of-support assumptions. That is the correct "why mine is better" claim: better for preventing unsupported recommendations, not universally better at scalar ranking.

Robust and stochastic routing should be treated as the main mathematical alternative to REFC. Robust optimisation chooses decisions that perform acceptably under defined uncertainty sets [Ben-Tal and Nemirovski 1998](https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.23.4.769), [Bertsimas and Sim 2004](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.1030.0065). Stochastic and robust shortest-path variants model uncertain travel times or costs [Fan, Kalaba, and Moore 2005](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.camwa.2004.07.028), [Dokka and Goerigk 2017](https://doi.org/10.4230/OASIcs.ATMOS.2017.16). The project differs by refusing to imply that its uncertainty set is complete. REFC certifies within named evidence worlds and can abstain outside them. That is better when the available data is incomplete, because the system does not silently turn missing world coverage into false robustness.

VOI and metareasoning should justify the controller. Classical value of information asks whether new information is worth its cost [Howard 1966](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1966.300074), bounded-rational metareasoning treats computation itself as an action [Russell and Wefald 1991](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(91)90015-C), and knowledge-gradient methods provide a principled one-step optimal-learning comparison [Frazier, Powell, and Dayanik 2009](https://doi.org/10.1287/ijoc.1080.0314). VOI-AD2R is not a full Bayesian optimal-sampling policy. It is a deterministic, auditable, myopic value-per-cost controller. That makes it weaker theoretically but better for this implementation because each chosen or rejected action can be inspected in route artifacts.

Selective prediction and assurance-case literature should justify typed abstention. Selective classification studies when a predictor should abstain instead of returning an unsafe label [El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/el-yaniv10a.html), [Geifman and El-Yaniv 2019](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/geifman19a.html). Conformal prediction is a useful comparator for statistically valid prediction sets [Vovk, Gammerman, and Shafer 2022](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-06649-8); conformal validity would require a separate conformal calibration layer beyond the current implementation. Assurance-case work explains why explicit evidence, claims, and structured justification matter in safety-adjacent systems [Kelly 2004](https://doi.org/10.4271/2004-01-1779). The project is stronger than a generic reject option because it identifies whether the failure is search, evidence, preference, support, budget, or model assumption.

Reproducibility should be a first-class related-work topic because it is one of the strongest publishability assets. FAIR principles [Wilkinson et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18), W3C PROV-O [W3C PROV-O](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/), empirical software-engineering methodology [Runeson and Host 2009](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10664-008-9102-8), and controlled experiment guidance [Wohlin et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-29044-2) support the claim that artifacts, manifests, logs, and negative results matter. The codebase's advantage is not that every result is green; it is that the result state is preserved and reviewable.

Chapter 3 should be mathematical but not inflated. It should explicitly state that the graph-search layer is inherited from standard routing algorithms and that the thesis modifies the decision layer. The relevant mathematical contribution is the terminal decision family, candidate criticality score, support-aware certification predicate, myopic VOI action score, finite preference ambiguity model, and risk-aware utility terms. The thesis should say how each variable was chosen: high weights on winner support and flip pressure protect the selected decision; denominator normalisation penalises expensive refinement; support gates prevent out-of-world certification; entropy and knee terms prevent scalarisation collapse; stop thresholds prevent unbounded compute. These are design choices, not fitted universal laws.

Chapter 4 should then turn those equations into algorithms. The algorithmic story is: produce raw route candidates; normalise and identify decision-critical candidate evidence; refine only where expected decision value justifies it; form a strict frontier; attempt REFC certification; run VOI only in the VOI mode; and return a terminal decision package. The reason this is better than simply generating many K-shortest paths is that each extra candidate must have a decision-evidence role as well as a geometric route identity.

Chapter 5 should state the evaluation design with the same discipline as the code. The evaluation is not a generic demo; it is claim-gated. Green surfaces support architecture, provenance, docs consistency, and artifact inspection. Deployment and theorem boundaries constrain the strongest claims. The publishability verdict must be quoted honestly: the current checked bundle supports the applied-evidence paper framing, but not deployment readiness. That makes the thesis stronger, not weaker, if the discussion frames those boundaries as evidence about the limits of the current artifact.

Chapter 6 should use source snippets as proof that the design is implemented. The central type-level claim is visible in `backend/app/models.py`:

This snippet should be used to state that REFC and VOI are live but mode-gated. A publishable paper should not imply the most expensive evidence loop is always executed. The better claim is that the architecture supports progressive evidence modes and records which mode was used.

Chapter 7 should not try to convert applied evidence into deployment evidence. The strongest discussion is: the architecture worked as an evidence-preserving decision system; the current artifact supports an applied publishability/adoption framing; and deployment/theorem-grade validation identifies the next research cycle. This is publishable as an applied artifact or design-science paper if the evaluation is positioned around "what the artifact demonstrates and falsifies." It is not yet publishable as a claim that freight operators should deploy the system unchanged.

The mathematical spine of the thesis should be made explicit at the start of Chapter 3. A path-only router solves:

```text
r* = argmin_r sum_{e in r} c_e
```

That equation belongs to the shortest-path and road-routing lineage [Dijkstra 1959](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01386390), [Hart, Nilsson, and Raphael 1968](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1968.300136), [Bast et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-49487-6_2). The implementation treats paths as evidence candidates and lifts the decision to:

```text
d* in {certified_singleton(r), certified_set(S), typed_abstention(k)}
```

with `k` drawn from search, evidence, preference, support, budget, and model-assumption failure classes. That terminal-family equation is the central mathematical reframing. It is better than a path-only output for this thesis because it can represent justified refusal. It is worse than a full deployment guarantee if the reader expects legal route approval, so the thesis must keep the bounded wording.

The route candidate should be defined as a vector, not as geometry alone:

```text
x_r = (
  time_r,
  money_r,
  co2_r,
  distance_r,
  toll_r,
  terrain_r,
  q95_r,
  cvar_r,
  support_r,
  provenance_r,
  preference_state_r
)
```

This is how the thesis should explain the jump from road routing to freight decision support. Road-routing literature explains how to find routes; MCDA and multiobjective optimisation explain why a scalar winner is not automatic once criteria conflict [Belton and Stewart 2002](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4615-1495-4), [Marler and Arora 2010](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00158-009-0460-7). Freight route-choice and value-of-time literature justify why time, money, and route characteristics must remain visible rather than hidden [Knorring, He, and Kornhauser 2005](https://doi.org/10.1177/0361198105192300106), [Zamparini and Reggiani 2007](https://doi.org/10.1080/01441640701322834), [Sun et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.3141/2354-12).

The selector equation should be presented as a transparent engineering scalarizer:

```text
score_r =
  VIKOR_Q_r
  + lambda_balance * balance_penalty_r
  + lambda_distance * normalized_distance_r
  + lambda_eta_distance * eta_distance_penalty_r
  + lambda_knee * knee_penalty_r
  - lambda_entropy * entropy_reward_r
  + time_preservation_penalty_r
```

Source: `backend/app/main.py`.

```python
elif math_profile == "modified_vikor_distance":
    score = (
        vikor_q
        + (balance_weight * balance_penalty)
        + (distance_weight * n_distance)
        + (eta_distance_weight * eta_distance_penalty)
        + (knee_weight * knee_penalty)
        - (entropy_weight * entropy_reward)
        + time_preservation_penalty
    )
```

The academic norm here is a weighted sum, Tchebycheff compromise, TOPSIS, VIKOR, or another MCDA ranking rule [Hwang and Yoon 1981](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-48318-9), [Opricovic and Tzeng 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(03)00020-1), [Steuer and Choo 1983](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02591870). The project changes the norm by adding freight-specific penalties and rewards around distance, ETA-distance coupling, compromise-knee behaviour, entropy spread, and time preservation. This is better for the thesis because the score can be explained term by term. It is not a new theorem and should not be sold as one. The thought process to write in the thesis is: first preserve recognisable MCDA structure, then add only those route-specific guard terms that prevent implausible freight recommendations from winning merely because a scalar normalisation made them look attractive.

The VIKOR machinery should also be shown, because it is the clearest way to demonstrate that the modification is controlled rather than arbitrary:

```text
n_j(r) = (x_j(r) - min_R x_j) / max(max_R x_j - min_R x_j, floor_j)
S_r = sum_j w_j n_j(r)
R_r = max_j w_j n_j(r)
Q_r = v * (S_r - S*) / (S- - S*) + (1 - v) * (R_r - R*) / (R- - R*)

modified_score_r =
  Q_r
  + lambda_balance * balance_r
  + lambda_distance * n_distance_r
  + lambda_eta * sqrt(n_time_r * n_distance_r)
  + lambda_knee * knee_r
  - lambda_entropy * entropy_r
  + time_preservation_penalty_r
```

Source: `backend/app/main.py`.

```python
weighted_sum_rows = [
    (wt * n_time) + (wm * n_money) + (we * n_co2)
    for n_time, n_money, n_co2, _ in norm_rows
]
weighted_regret_rows = [
    max(wt * n_time, wm * n_money, we * n_co2)
    for n_time, n_money, n_co2, _ in norm_rows
]
vikor_q = (vikor_v * _safe_scale(weighted_sum, vikor_s_min, vikor_s_max)) + (
    (1.0 - vikor_v) * _safe_scale(weighted_regret, vikor_r_min, vikor_r_max)
)
```

The thesis should state that the modification is not "I changed VIKOR until it looked good." It is a staged design: preserve VIKOR's group-utility/regret compromise, then add route-specific terms for freight plausibility. The `sqrt(n_time * n_distance)` term makes a long-distance/long-ETA route pay a coupled penalty; the entropy reward favours routes that improve more than one objective at once; the knee term discourages extreme single-objective winners when a balanced compromise is available. The resulting score is more explainable for freight routing than a black-box learned ranker, but it remains an engineering scalarizer rather than a new MCDA theorem.

DCCS should be defined as a value-of-refinement score over candidates:

```text
criticality(c) =
  (
    winner_lcb_lift_c
    + pairwise_gap_lcb_lift_c
    + flip_radius_lift_c
    + unresolved_winner_mass_c
    + preference_relevance_c
    + search_deficiency_risk_c
  ) / max(1, predicted_refine_cost_c)
```

Source: `backend/app/candidate_criticality.py`.

```python
winner_lcb_lift = max(0.0, 0.45 * objective_gap + 0.15 * (1.0 - support_mass))
pairwise_gap_lcb_lift = max(0.0, 0.35 * mechanism_gap + 0.10 * (1.0 - overlap))
flip_radius_lift = max(0.0, 0.50 * flip_probability + 0.05 * max(0.0, stretch - 1.0))
unresolved_winner_mass = max(0.0, 1.0 - objective_gap)
preference_relevance = _clamp_unit(
    0.40 * mechanism_gap + 0.30 * time_regret_gap + 0.20 * (1.0 - overlap)
)
search_deficiency_risk = _clamp_unit(
    0.45 * (1.0 - objective_gap) + 0.25 * overlap + 0.30 * float(near_duplicate)
)
denominator = max(1.0, action_cost)
criticality_score = (
    winner_lcb_lift
    + pairwise_gap_lcb_lift
    + flip_radius_lift
    + unresolved_winner_mass
    + preference_relevance
    + search_deficiency_risk
) / denominator
```

This is one of the most original implementation-level calculations. Alternative-route algorithms usually focus on short, diverse, or low-overlap paths [Akgun, Erkut, and Batta 2000](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(99)00214-3), [Abraham et al. 2010](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-13193-6_3), [Chondrogiannis et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00778-020-00604-x). DCCS instead asks whether a candidate is likely to change certification evidence. The weights are not learned universal constants; they are transparent design priorities. Winner support and flip pressure are weighted strongly because they directly threaten the terminal route decision. Preference relevance is included because a route can be decision-critical even if its current objective score is not best. The denominator prevents expensive refinement from dominating unless it has commensurate expected value. The thesis should describe this as a principled engineering adaptation of alternative-route generation toward decision-critical evidence acquisition.

The selection story should be written as two linked scores: a bootstrap score that prevents candidate collapse and a challenger score that chooses which remaining evidence is worth refining:

```text
score_boot(c | S) = benefit_boot(c, S) / max(1, cost_boot(c, S))
score_chal(c) = gain_chal(c) / max(1, penalty_chal(c))
```

The important difference from K-shortest ranking is that `gain_chal(c)` is not only route length or route cost. It combines objective closeness, mechanism diversity, flip probability, preference sensitivity, search-completeness pressure, hidden-challenger risk, overlap, stretch, and predicted refine cost. This is why DCCS can treat a candidate as important even when it is not currently the cheapest candidate: it may still be the candidate that decides whether the winner is certifiable. Diversity methods such as NSGA-II are relevant comparators because they preserve non-dominated alternatives [Deb et al. 2002](https://doi.org/10.1109/4235.996017), but DCCS is narrower: it preserves candidates that matter to certification.

REFC should be written as support-aware certification rather than raw winner frequency:

```text
certified(S) =
  support_flag(S)
  and decision_region_certified(S)
  and winner_score(S) >= tau
  and active_challengers_excluded(S)

safe(S) = certified(S) and support_flag(S)
```

The implementation also supports a confidence-state reading. The thesis should write the empirical winner certificate as:

```text
p_hat_r = (1 / |W|) * sum_{w in W} 1[r = argmin_{r'} score_w(r')]
LCB_r = anytime_hoeffding_lower_bound(success_r, |W|, delta)
singleton_safe(r) =
  support_flag
  and LCB_r >= tau
  and active_challenger_gaps_nonnegative
  and no_blockers
```

Source: `backend/app/evidence_certification.py` and `backend/app/confidence_sequences.py`.

```python
lower_bound, upper_bound = anytime_hoeffding_interval(
    success_count,
    sample_count,
    delta=delta,
)
```

This should be described as a bounded empirical certificate, not as a full conformal or distributionally robust guarantee. The reason it is better for the current codebase than claiming a complete uncertainty model is that it can name its sample count, delta source, support flag, and stopping-valid trace state.

This is different from classic robust shortest path:

```text
min_r max_{u in U} f(r, u)
```

Robust and stochastic routing literature optimises against uncertainty models, distributions, or uncertainty sets [Ben-Tal and Nemirovski 1998](https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.23.4.769), [Bertsimas and Sim 2004](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.1030.0065), [Fan, Kalaba, and Moore 2005](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.camwa.2004.07.028), [Dokka and Goerigk 2017](https://doi.org/10.4230/OASIcs.ATMOS.2017.16). The repo's design is better for this codebase because it does not pretend to know a complete true uncertainty set. It certifies within the evidence world it can name, and it refuses when support is weak. The limitation is that it is not full distributionally robust optimisation.

VOI should be stated as a bounded myopic metareasoning surrogate, and the equation should match the implemented action score:

```text
Q(a) =
  (
    lambda_certificate * predicted_winner_lcb_gain_a
    + lambda_margin * predicted_gap_lcb_gain_a
    + lambda_frontier * predicted_boundary_contraction_a
    + lambda_radius * predicted_radius_or_flip_budget_gain_a
    + lambda_unresolved * predicted_unresolved_mass_reduction_a
    + lambda_preference * predicted_preference_ambiguity_reduction_a
  ) / (cost_search_a + cost_evidence_a + epsilon)

stop if max_a Q(a) < tau_stop
```

Source: `backend/app/voi_controller.py`.

```python
q_score = (
    (cfg.lambda_certificate * predicted_winner_lcb_gain(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_margin * predicted_gap_lcb_gain(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_frontier * predicted_boundary_contraction(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_radius_or_flip_budget * predicted_radius_or_flip_budget_gain(scored_action))
    + (cfg.lambda_unresolved_mass * predicted_unresolved_mass_reduction(scored_action))
    + (
        cfg.lambda_preference_ambiguity
        * predicted_preference_ambiguity_reduction(scored_action)
    )
) / (cost + cfg.epsilon)
```

The classical value-of-information comparison is:

```text
VOI = E[max_a U(a | new information)] - max_a E[U(a | current information)] - cost
```

Howard gives the value-of-information decision-theory origin [Howard 1966](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1966.300074), Russell and Wefald give the bounded-rational computation-as-action frame [Russell and Wefald 1991](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(91)90015-C), and knowledge-gradient work is a useful comparator for optimal learning [Frazier, Powell, and Dayanik 2009](https://doi.org/10.1287/ijoc.1080.0314). The repo's version is better for the thesis artifact because every action score is inspectable and cheap enough for route-level use. It is weaker than full Bayesian optimal sampling and must be described as a deterministic value-per-cost controller rather than an optimal sampling proof.

Tail risk should be introduced with the canonical CVaR formula and then narrowed to the implementation:

```text
CVaR_alpha(L) = min_eta eta + (1 / (1 - alpha)) * E[max(L - eta, 0)]
```

Source: `backend/app/main.py`.

```python
def _option_joint_robust_utility(option: RouteOption, *, risk_aversion: float) -> float:
    utility_mean, utility_cvar95 = _option_joint_utility_stats(option)
    return robust_objective(
        mean_value=utility_mean,
        cvar_value=utility_cvar95,
        risk_aversion=risk_aversion,
        risk_family=settings.risk_family,
```

Coherent risk measures and CVaR are standard [Artzner et al. 1999](https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9965.00068), [Rockafellar and Uryasev 2000](https://doi.org/10.21314/JOR.2000.038). The project adapts them into a route-decision penalty family rather than making a full stochastic-programming claim. That is better than hiding "risk" inside one vague coefficient, because the thesis can name the tail-risk quantity and the family used. It is weaker than a fully calibrated traffic-distribution model, so the evidence bank must keep the model-conditioned wording.

The implemented empirical tail calculation is more specific than the textbook formula. It uses the Hyndman-Fan type-7 quantile convention [Hyndman and Fan 1996](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.1996.10473566) and integrates the empirical tail quantile in `backend/app/risk_model.py`:

```python
def cvar(values: Iterable[float], *, alpha: float = 0.95) -> float:
    ordered = sorted(float(v) for v in values)
    ...
    tail_integral = 0.0
    for start, end in zip(knots, knots[1:], strict=False):
        q_start = quantile(ordered, start)
        q_end = quantile(ordered, end)
        tail_integral += 0.5 * (q_start + q_end) * (end - start)
    result = tail_integral / max(1e-12, 1.0 - alpha_clamped)
    threshold = quantile(ordered, alpha_clamped)
    return max(result, threshold)
```

The paper should explicitly say that the `entropic` and `downside_semivariance` options in `backend/app/risk_model.py` are thesis-specific tail penalties, not canonical full-distribution risk measures. That wording prevents a reviewer from rejecting the method for overclaiming a standard it does not implement.

Preference ambiguity should be formalised as a shrinking compatible set:

```text
C_t = {w in W : w satisfies all pairwise, threshold, ratio, veto, and time-guard constraints observed by time t}

necessary_best(r) = true if r is best for every w in C_t
possible_best(r) = true if r is best for at least one w in C_t
```

This connects to utility elicitation and minimax-regret preference reasoning [Boutilier et al. 2006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2006.02.003), SMAA [Lahdelma, Hokkanen, and Salminen 1998](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(97)00163-X), and robust ordinal regression [Greco, Mousseau, and Slowinski 2008](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2007.08.013). The implementation is a finite approximation, so the thesis should say it preserves and narrows preference ambiguity; it should not say it learns the user's true utility function.

The final terminal-decision rule should be stated plainly:

```text
d* =
  certified_singleton(r) if singleton_safe(r)
  certified_set(S) if set_safe(S)
  typed_abstention(reason, remedy) otherwise

reason precedence:
  budget -> out_of_support -> search -> evidence -> preference -> model_assumption
```

Source: `backend/app/abstention.py`.

if budget_text or _contains_any(stop_text, ("budget", "exhausted", "quota")):
    return "uncertified_due_to_budget"
...
if credible_search_uncertainty is True or _contains_any(
    stop_text,
    ("search_incomplete", "no_action_worth_it", "search_uncertain", "insufficient_search"),
