#### AX95.6 Literature Positioning For EB-RDC

EB-RDC is positioned against five mature families.

First, shortest-path and road-network routing literature explains the substrate. Dijkstra [Dijkstra 1959](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01386390), A* [Hart, Nilsson, and Raphael 1968](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1968.300136), Yen [Yen 1971](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.17.11.712), Eppstein [Eppstein 1998](https://doi.org/10.1137/S0097539795290477), contraction hierarchies [Geisberger et al. 2008](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68552-4_24), customizable route planning [Delling et al. 2015](https://doi.org/10.1287/trsc.2014.0579), and route-planning surveys [Bast et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-49487-6_2) show that fast route computation is mature. EB-RDC does not compete with that literature on raw query speed. It uses route computation as the evidence substrate.

Second, alternative-route and choice-set literature explains why multiple candidates matter. K-shortest and alternative-route methods can produce several plausible paths, but EB-RDC asks which candidates are decision-critical for certification. That is why DCCS is more than route diversity: it scores hidden-challenger risk, certificate-criticality, overlap, flip probability, mechanism gap, and search-completeness contribution.

Third, MCDA and robust/stochastic routing explain conflicting objectives and uncertainty. Weighted sums, VIKOR, Tchebycheff scalarization, Pareto methods, robust optimization, stochastic shortest paths, and CVaR provide valid foundations. EB-RDC differs by making the score non-final: a high-ranked route can still be uncertified if support, preference, search, or evidence conditions are insufficient.

Fourth, VOI and metareasoning justify the action controller. EB-RDC does not refine every candidate or ask unlimited preference questions. It buys more route/evidence/preference information only when the predicted decision value justifies the cost.

Fifth, selective prediction and assurance-case literature justify abstention and evidence objects. EB-RDC adapts reject-option logic from prediction to freight routing. It records whether the issue is search, evidence, preference, support, budget, or model assumption, and it stores the evidence chain in artifacts.

The publication-safe novelty sentence is:

```text
EB-RDC is a route-decision certification algorithm: it composes mature route computation, candidate triage, bounded evidence-world certification, preference-state preservation, value-of-information action control, and typed abstention into one auditable terminal decision contract for freight routing.
```

That sentence is strong enough for a distinction-level thesis framing while remaining honest about the implemented evidence boundary.

### AX96. Publication-Readiness Quality Audit: How To Position The Work

In this evidence bank, top-tier means academically defensible rather than rhetorically inflated. A top thesis or later applied-systems paper becomes stronger by naming the precise contribution, tying every claim to code/tests/artifacts, explaining why alternative designs were weaker for this research objective, and making the remaining evidence conditions visible. The right standard is design-science rigor: the work contributes an artifact and evaluates it in context, but the artifact must still be connected to a problem, design rationale, evaluation method, and threat model [Hevner et al. 2004](https://doi.org/10.2307/25148625), [Peffers et al. 2007](https://doi.org/10.2753/MIS0742-1222240302), [Gregor and Hevner 2013](https://doi.org/10.25300/MISQ/2013/37.2.01), [Wieringa 2014](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-43839-8). On that standard, the project is strong as an applied artifact and particularly strong where the claim is about evidence-bounded route-decision software.

The key evidence conditions that determine the strongest publication claim are the following.

| Issue | Why it matters academically | Current evidence strength | Thesis-safe interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Contribution identity can still blur between routing, certification, and evaluation artifact. | Road-network shortest-path routing is a mature literature; a thesis that sounds like only "I built a route planner" is easy to dismiss against Dijkstra, A*, contraction hierarchies, customizable routing, OSRM, and ORS [Dijkstra 1959](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01386390), [Hart et al. 1968](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1968.300136), [Geisberger et al. 2008](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68552-4_24), [Bast et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-49487-6_2). | Strong for EB-RDC as an evidence-bounded route-decision architecture whose substrate is mature routing. | The thesis states that route engines generate evidence, while EB-RDC certifies, sets, refines, or abstains over bounded evidence. |
| The theorem package is partial by design. | The report contains implementation-grounded propositions; theorem-level originality needs complete assumptions, proof obligations, and counterexample boundaries. | Good for assumption-limited propositions and implementation-contract claims. | The paper uses these as implementation-contract and bounded-scope propositions. |
| Evaluation is artifact-rich and locally reproducible. | Design-science evaluation must show utility in context; empirical software-engineering reports must expose case-study scope, construct validity, internal validity, and external validity [Runeson and Höst 2009](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10664-008-9102-8). | Strong local tests, generated bundles, strict docs checks, and artifact provenance. | Claim research-grade artifact evaluation with recorded external-validity boundaries. |
| User/operator trust is currently argued through inspection surfaces. | A decision-support thesis can show inspectable evidence; a human-factors claim would additionally need user studies, reliance measures, or operator-task experiments. | Strong UI and artifact inspection surfaces. | Say the system supports auditability and prepares the ground for later operator studies. |
| Robust/stochastic claims require precise wording. | Robust optimization, stochastic routing, min-max regret, and CVaR have precise mathematical meanings [Ben-Tal and Nemirovski 1998](https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.23.4.769), [Bertsimas and Sim 2004](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.1030.0065), [Rockafellar and Uryasev 2000](https://doi.org/10.21314/JOR.2000.038), [Aissi et al. 2009](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejor.2008.06.012). | Strong for bounded evidence-world summaries. | Describe REFC as bounded-world evidence certification. |
| Preference reasoning is strong as ambiguity preservation. | MCDA, SMAA, and regret-based elicitation already address uncertain or incomplete preferences [Hwang and Yoon 1981](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-48318-9), [Opricovic and Tzeng 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(03)00020-1), [Lahdelma and Salminen 2001](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.49.3.444.11220), [Boutilier et al. 2006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2006.02.003). | Strong as preference-state preservation and query trace. | Claim ambiguity preservation and auditable preference-state updates. |
| VOI is an auditable controller. | VOI/metareasoning theory asks when information or computation changes decision utility [Howard 1966](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1966.300074), [Russell and Wefald 1991](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(91)90015-C), [Horvitz 1987](https://erichorvitz.com/u87.htm). | Strong as deterministic value-per-cost action control. | Say VOI-AD2R is an auditable route-specific metareasoning controller. |
| Abstention is diagnostic route-decision semantics. | Selective prediction and reject-option work define coverage/risk trade-offs and, in conformal prediction, formal validity conditions [Chow 1970](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406), [El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/el-yaniv10a.html), [Geifman and El-Yaniv 2017](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/7073-selective-classification-for-deep-neural-networks), [Vovk et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-06649-8). | Strong typed abstention semantics. | Claim diagnostic refusal by reason family with bounded evidence scope. |
| Reproducibility is strong locally and artifact-led. | Reproducible computational research requires exact scripts, data, environment, and artifacts; ACM artifact badging separates available, functional, reusable, reproduced, and replicated artifacts [Sandve et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285), [ACM Artifact Review and Badging 2020](https://www.acm.org/publications/policies/artifact-review-and-badging-current). | Strong local artifacts and docs checker. | Claim artifacted reproducibility discipline with independent replication as later evidence. |
| Literature review breadth is broad but must avoid becoming a source dump. | A systematic software-engineering literature review requires an explicit protocol; a thesis evidence bank can be broader but must still synthesize, not only list [Kitchenham and Charters 2007](https://www.cin.ufpe.br/~in1037/leitura/kitchenham2007guidelines.pdf). | Strong quantity of citations; synthesis quality must be maintained. | Use citations to explain precise boundaries and design choices, not to decorate claims. |

#### AX96.1 The Actual Critique In Thesis Prose

The thesis is strongest when it is framed as a design-science and applied-systems contribution. It identifies a real problem: freight route engines can return plausible paths without exposing enough evidence to decide whether the route should be trusted. The implementation then contributes a named artifact, EB-RDC, which connects candidate generation, decision-critical candidate screening, bounded evidence-world certification, preference-state preservation, VOI action control, typed abstention, and replayable artifacts. That is a coherent artifact contribution under the design-science model: the artifact changes the decision contract, and the evaluation inspects whether the implemented artifact behaves according to its contract [Hevner et al. 2004](https://doi.org/10.2307/25148625), [Peffers et al. 2007](https://doi.org/10.2753/MIS0742-1222240302), [Venable et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1057/ejis.2014.36), [Wieringa 2014](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-43839-8). Gregor and Hevner's design-science positioning is especially useful because it separates situated artifact contribution from mature general design theory [Gregor and Hevner 2013](https://doi.org/10.25300/MISQ/2013/37.2.01). EB-RDC currently belongs in the strong artifact/nascent design-theory category, not in the mature universal-theory category.

The thesis becomes easiest to defend when it is positioned above the mature shortest-path substrate. Fast road-network routing is already well served by shortest-path and preprocessing methods. Dijkstra's algorithm formalised the shortest-path problem for weighted graphs [Dijkstra 1959](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01386390). A* formalised heuristic search under explicit admissibility assumptions [Hart et al. 1968](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1968.300136). Contraction hierarchies and customizable route planning address the practical problem of very fast road-network queries after preprocessing [Geisberger et al. 2008](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68552-4_24), [Delling et al. 2015](https://doi.org/10.1287/trsc.2014.0579). Route-planning surveys show how mature this field already is [Bast et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-49487-6_2). EB-RDC therefore asks the next applied-systems question: once candidate routes exist, which decision state is certifiable under bounded route, evidence, preference, support, and budget assumptions?

The thesis is also strongest when it treats failures and abstentions as evidence rather than embarrassment. Reject-option and selective-classification literature explains why refusing to decide can be rational when uncertainty is too high [Chow 1970](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406), [El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/el-yaniv10a.html). EB-RDC adapts that principle to route decisions by using typed abstention reasons such as search, evidence, preference, support, budget, and model-assumption insufficiency. The route-specific contribution is diagnostic refusal: the system reports why a route decision is uncertified, which remedy family is relevant, and which artifacted assumptions define the refusal.

#### AX96.2 Why The Proofs Are Useful But Not Yet Complete

The proof material is valuable because it lifts the thesis beyond a software demo. The propositions in AX95 tie terminal states, abstention families, certificate scope, support flags, and VOI termination to implementation objects. This gives the final thesis mathematical shape. A theory-first paper would need all assumptions formalised, every helper invariant named, edge cases covered, and a clear proof that the implementation satisfies the formal model. The current theorem package is best described as a partial-proof and implementation-contract layer.

That scope is acceptable for an applied-systems thesis. In applied software and information-systems research, a rigorously evaluated artifact can be a legitimate contribution without becoming a pure theorem paper [Hevner et al. 2004](https://doi.org/10.2307/25148625). The correct paper language is:

```text
The proof contribution is assumption-bounded. The propositions show that the implemented decision contract has exclusive terminal semantics, finite controller execution under configured budgets, typed abstention classification, and certificate scope tied to recorded evidence worlds. The proof scope is the implemented decision contract rather than a universal model of all road-network, real-world traffic, or information-acquisition behaviour.
```

This is much stronger than leaving the proof material as "sketches". It tells the reader exactly what is proven, why it matters, and what is not proven.

#### AX96.3 Why The Evaluation Is Strong For A Thesis And Still Limited For Publication

The evaluation is unusually strong for a BSc or MSc-style codebase thesis because it is not just screenshots or anecdotal examples. The repository has tests, generated artifacts, route bundles, theorem maps, claim matrices, negative-result ledgers, local docs consistency checks, endpoint parity checks, and provenance/index files. That is a major strength. It aligns with reproducible computational research principles: preserve exact commands, inputs, outputs, and intermediate evidence so another reader can inspect the analysis chain [Peng 2011](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1213847), [Sandve et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285), [Collberg and Proebsting 2016](https://doi.org/10.1145/2812803). It also moves toward artifact-review expectations, where availability, functionality, reusability, reproduced, and replicated status are separate claims [ACM Artifact Review and Badging 2020](https://www.acm.org/publications/policies/artifact-review-and-badging-current), and toward FAIR-style data/metadata discipline where findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability must be designed rather than assumed [Wilkinson et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18). The National Academies' distinction between reproducibility and replicability is also important: the current bundle is strong on local reproducibility discipline, while independent replication remains future evidence [National Academies 2019](https://doi.org/10.17226/25303).

The evaluation should be presented as research-grade artifact evidence with external-validity boundaries. A publication reviewer can ask whether the same evidence discipline holds on unseen regions, new data providers, real dispatcher workflows, legal HGV restrictions, and independently reproduced environments. The current repository answers many local-replay questions and defines the next validation layers clearly. Empirical software-engineering case-study guidance expects the report to make context, data collection, analysis procedures, and validity threats explicit [Runeson and Höst 2009](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10664-008-9102-8). The report therefore states:

```text
The evaluation demonstrates implementation fidelity and local artifacted behavior. Field deployment, independent replication, operator reliance measurement, and legal/commercial route certification are separate validation layers beyond the current artifact evidence.
```

That sentence protects the thesis. It turns an examiner's strongest objection into a documented threat-to-validity boundary.

#### AX96.4 The Exact Difference Between "Strong BSc Thesis" And "Publishable Research Paper"

For a BSc end-of-year thesis, the project is very strong because it has a real software artifact, a non-trivial backend, a frontend, multiple algorithms, data/model assets, tests, generated results, documentation discipline, and a coherent research framing. Most BSc projects do not reach this level of evidence integration. A BSc examiner can reasonably reward the work for system design, implementation complexity, evaluation discipline, and reflective limitation handling.

For a publishable applied paper, the bar changes. A paper must convince reviewers that the contribution is novel relative to existing work, that the evaluation answers the claim, and that limitations are not hidden. The current codebase supports a promising applied-systems paper if the claim is:

```text
EB-RDC is an implemented evidence-bounded route-decision contract that composes mature route computation, candidate triage, bounded evidence-world certification, preference-state preservation, VOI-style action control, and typed abstention into replayable freight-route decision artifacts.
```

The current codebase is therefore best served by avoiding a claim like:

```text
This system is a deployment-ready freight router that outperforms commercial routing systems and provides theorem-backed optimal robust routing.
```

That comparison target is the wrong scholarly target because commercial products have different map coverage, live-data contracts, legal-routing integrations, fleet workflows, and operational reliability objectives, while robust-optimization and routing theory have stronger global mathematical guarantees under their own assumptions [Ben-Tal and Nemirovski 1998](https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.23.4.769), [Bertsimas and Sim 2004](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.1030.0065), [Bast et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-49487-6_2).

#### AX96.5 The Literature Review Must Make The Design Choices Look Inevitable

The literature review shows why EB-RDC combines Dijkstra, A*, VIKOR, CVaR, VOI, and selective prediction lineages. The chain is:

1. Shortest-path and routing engines solve path generation efficiently, so the thesis uses them rather than competes with them [Dijkstra 1959](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01386390), [Hart et al. 1968](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1968.300136), [Geisberger et al. 2008](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68552-4_24).
2. Alternative-route and K-route methods create candidate sets, but they do not by themselves certify that a candidate is decision-safe.
3. MCDA explains multiattribute scoring, but scalar scores can hide preference ambiguity [Ehrgott 2005](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-27659-9), [Hwang and Yoon 1981](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-48318-9), [Opricovic and Tzeng 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(03)00020-1), [Marler and Arora 2010](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00158-009-0460-7).
4. SMAA and minimax-regret elicitation show why uncertain preferences are represented as regions or regret, not silently collapsed into one hidden weight vector [Lahdelma and Salminen 2001](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.49.3.444.11220), [Boutilier et al. 2006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2006.02.003).
5. Robust and stochastic optimization explain uncertainty, but global robust optimality can be too strong or too conservative for a bounded implemented artifact [Ben-Tal and Nemirovski 1998](https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.23.4.769), [Bertsimas and Sim 2004](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.1030.0065), [Rockafellar and Uryasev 2000](https://doi.org/10.21314/JOR.2000.038).
6. VOI/metareasoning explains why further search, evidence refresh, sampling, or preference questions should be budgeted actions rather than unlimited computation [Howard 1966](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1966.300074), [Horvitz 1987](https://erichorvitz.com/u87.htm), [Russell and Wefald 1991](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(91)90015-C), [Frazier et al. 2009](https://doi.org/10.1287/ijoc.1080.0314).
7. Selective prediction explains why refusal can be rational, while EB-RDC adapts refusal into typed route-decision abstention [Chow 1970](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406), [El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/el-yaniv10a.html), [Cortes et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-46379-7_5), [Geifman and El-Yaniv 2017](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.08500).

Written this way, the literature review makes the architecture feel necessary. Each field solves part of the problem. EB-RDC is the composition that makes those pieces operational in a route-decision artifact.

#### AX96.6 What Is Actually Excellent

The codebase foregrounds several genuine positives.

First, the project has a defensible problem statement: make route decisions inspectable, certifiable, set-valued, or abstaining under bounded evidence. That is more precise than a vague "make routing better" objective.

Second, the implementation changes the API contract. A conventional route service returns geometry and metrics. This system returns route evidence, certificate state, preference state, support summaries, artifacts, and abstention semantics. That is a meaningful systems contribution.

Third, the repository shows unusual evidence discipline. Claim matrices, theorem maps, negative-result files, docs checks, endpoint parity checks, generated artifacts, and provenance records make the thesis auditable. This is exactly the kind of engineering maturity that turns a project from a demo into a serious applied artifact.

Fourth, the scope conditions are intellectually useful. Typed abstention, bounded evidence worlds, and artifacted negative results show that the system has a principled terminal state when certainty is unsupported. That is stronger academically than forcing every route into a winner.

Fifth, EB-RDC is a good named algorithmic contribution because it does not compete with the wrong literature. It respects mature route computation and contributes a decision layer above it.

#### AX96.7 Scope Conditions For The Final Paper

The final thesis or paper states the following scope conditions explicitly:

- EB-RDC is positioned as the decision layer above mature route-computation substrates.
- Raw route-query latency remains the domain of OSRM, ORS, CH-style routing, CRP/MLD, hub labels, and related path-serving techniques.
- REFC certificates are bounded by generated candidates, sampled worlds, support assumptions, thresholds, and model state.
- VOI-AD2R is an auditable route-specific metareasoning controller whose decisions are recorded in traces and stop certificates.
- Typed abstention is diagnostic route-decision semantics with reason families and remedy families.
- Preference state preserves compatible preferences and exposes ambiguity rather than claiming to recover the user's private utility exactly.
- Generated artifacts provide local reproducibility evidence and prepare the work for later independent replication.
- UI auditability is an inspection and communication contribution that can support later dispatcher-reliance studies.
- UK-focused evidence improves local specificity but limits geographic generalisation.
- Legal HGV, bridge, dangerous-goods, driver-hours, and clean-air compliance require their own data contracts and tests when they are promoted from context into certified constraints.

These scope conditions strengthen the project because they make the claim survivable. Metascience work on publication bias and overclaiming explains why transparent negative and bounded results matter [Ioannidis 2005](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.0020124), [Fanelli 2012](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11192-011-0494-7). For this project, calibrated claim discipline is a strength because the contribution is selective certification. A system that knows when to abstain should also produce a thesis that knows the support conditions under which its claims hold.

#### AX96.8 Final Critique Verdict

The project is already strong enough for a high-mark BSc thesis if the final write-up is disciplined. It has a serious artifact, a credible problem, code depth, evaluation artifacts, and a mature claim boundary. It can plausibly be framed as distinction-level because the system goes beyond a CRUD app, beyond a simple route API wrapper, and beyond a notebook-only experiment.

The route from current evidence to a top PhD-style or mature publication claim is clear: complete theorem closure, independent external replication, field/user validation, full legal/commercial compliance validation where claimed, and a clean separation between local artifact success and general deployment success. Those are the natural next validation layers for the same architecture.

The strongest framing from the current codebase is:

```text
This thesis contributes EB-RDC, an implemented evidence-bounded route-decision certification architecture for freight routing. It demonstrates how mature route computation can be lifted into an auditable decision contract that returns certified singleton routes, certified sets, or typed abstentions under bounded candidate, evidence, preference, support, budget, and model assumptions. The contribution is strongest as an applied design-science artifact with rigorous local evidence, and its remaining limitations define a clear path to later publication rather than invalidating the thesis.
```

That is the strongest honest version of the work. It is ambitious, defensible, and much harder to attack than an overclaim.

#### AX96.9 Evaluation Critique Details: Baselines, Ablations, Failure Examples, And Runtime Cost

The baseline story is a matched-comparison protocol rather than a loose superiority claim. Baseline comparisons are meaningful only under matched OD pairs, departure assumptions, vehicle/scenario settings, provider identity, graph identity, strictness policy, feasibility filters, and objective interpretation. If EB-RDC is evaluated against OSRM or ORS, the paper says whether the baseline is being judged on route speed, route cost, evidence completeness, decision certification, or abstention behavior. Otherwise the comparison can become invalid because the systems optimize different targets. This is a construct-validity issue in the sense of empirical software-engineering evaluation: the metric must measure the claim being made [Runeson and Höst 2009](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10664-008-9102-8), [Wohlin et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-29044-2), [ACM SIGSOFT Empirical Standards](https://www2.sigsoft.org/EmpiricalStandards/).

The ablation ladder is explained causally. The variants are best read as a layered design argument: `V0` establishes path-return or baseline behavior, `A` adds DCCS candidate evidence, `B` adds REFC certification, and `C` adds VOI control. Any performance or quality claim says which layer caused the observed change and which confounders remain. For example, a gain after adding REFC is evidence that bounded-world certification changed the terminal decision contract; it is not automatically evidence that route travel times improved. A gain after adding VOI is evidence that the action controller changed refinement/evidence behavior; it is not automatically evidence that the controller is Bayes-optimal.

The failure atlas is narrative evidence. It contributes three worked example patterns: one support downgrade, one typed abstention, and one case where EB-RDC refuses a tempting singleton. These examples show why refusal is a scientific output rather than a failed route request. This is the practical route-decision analogue of selective prediction: the important result is whether the system can answer and whether it can identify when an answer lacks justification [Chow 1970](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406), [El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/el-yaniv10a.html).

The runtime story is an engineering tradeoff. EB-RDC improves auditability by adding candidate ledgers, evidence worlds, certification summaries, VOI traces, and provenance, but that auditability has runtime, storage, and maintenance cost. The paper reports the tradeoff directly: EB-RDC deliberately spends computation and documentation effort to make decisions inspectable. That is a good design choice for a thesis about auditability, while low-latency route serving remains a different optimisation objective.

Finally, the current "green" evidence must stay scoped. The checked suite supports an applied-evidence thesis/paper framing over implementation fidelity, local artifacts, generated reviewer bundles, and bounded decision semantics. Field deployment, external replication, legal routing correctness, commercial-map benchmarking, and validated dispatcher reliance are separate validation layers. Naming those layers makes the thesis claim credible.

### AX97. Detailed Abstract Support, Literature Expansion, Chapter Signposting, And Source Attribution

This appendix exists because the final thesis abstract and opening chapters need to do more than name features. They need to explain what a better route-decision solution means, why the chapter order is logical, how software design carries the research contribution, where the literature sits, and how standard algorithms are attributed. The thesis should treat EB-RDC as an applied design-science artifact: the contribution is the implemented decision architecture, terminal decision contract, evidence discipline, and route-specific composition of known algorithmic families.

#### AX97.1 What A Better Solution Means

In this project, "better" should be defined by decision quality rather than raw path speed alone. A route answer is better when it is inspectable, evidence-bounded, preference-aware, and capable of refusing overconfident answers. This is a stronger and more accurate definition than a leaderboard claim because freight routing is a multiobjective operational decision. Truck route-choice studies show that drivers and operators trade off time, distance, reliability, tolls, and other attributes rather than following a single universal metric [Knorring, He, and Kornhauser 2005](https://doi.org/10.1177/0361198105192300106), [Sun et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.3141/2354-12), [Wang and Goodchild 2014](https://doi.org/10.3141/2411-14). Freight value-of-time evidence also shows heterogeneity, so a fixed global time-money conversion is a weak model of the user's actual decision [Zamparini and Reggiani 2007](https://doi.org/10.1080/01441640701322834), [Binsuwadan et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tra.2020.06.002).

The thesis therefore defines a better solution as a route-decision system with the following properties:

- **Candidate evidence awareness.** The system records which routes were generated, which candidates were refined, which were filtered, and which hidden-challenger risks remain.
- **Evidence-world awareness.** The system evaluates route choices across bounded stress worlds for evidence families such as scenario, toll, terrain, fuel, carbon, weather, stochastic uncertainty, support, and freshness.
- **Preference-state awareness.** The system preserves compatible preference states and possible-best/necessary-best structure instead of forcing every user into one unexamined weight vector.
- **Action-cost awareness.** The system treats more search, more evidence, more samples, and more preference questions as finite-budget actions whose expected decision value must justify their cost.
- **Terminal-state honesty.** The system returns a certified singleton, a certified set, or a typed abstention, so uncertainty changes the decision output rather than being buried in prose.
- **Artifact auditability.** The system emits manifests, traces, certificates, support summaries, and provenance records so the result can be checked after the request.

This definition of "better" links directly to design implications. A path-only API can be excellent at returning a route but weak at explaining whether the route decision is justified. EB-RDC improves the decision contract by making support, uncertainty, preference ambiguity, and abstention part of the software output. That is why the project is best presented as a route-decision architecture rather than a lower-level shortest-path replacement.

#### AX97.2 Chapter Organisation And Why It Is Organised That Way

The chapter order should be defended explicitly because it mirrors the artifact dependency graph. The thesis reads best as a chain of claims in which each chapter makes the next chapter possible.

| Thesis chapter | Purpose in the argument | Why this order is justified | Design implication carried forward |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Introduction | State the freight route-decision problem, motivation, research questions, and contributions. | The reader first needs to know that the target is auditable decision support under uncertainty. | Sets the terminal decision contract as the thesis spine. |
| Background, related work, and mathematical preliminaries | Place the work against routing, alternative routes, MCDA, robust/stochastic decision making, VOI, selective prediction, assurance, and reproducibility. | The gap only becomes visible after showing that each mature literature solves part of the problem. | Justifies composition instead of isolated algorithm invention. |
| Mathematical formulation and model extensions | Define route candidates, objective vectors, strict frontiers, bounded evidence worlds, preference states, certificates, action costs, and terminal states. | Algorithms cannot be evaluated until the objects and invariants are defined. | Converts software behaviour into thesis-readable mathematical objects. |
| Algorithms and solution methods | Present EB-RDC, DCCS, REFC, preference preservation, VOI-AD2R, and typed abstention as one named method. | Once the objects exist, the method can be stated as a procedure with inputs, outputs, budgets, and terminal semantics. | Shows exactly how mature routing substrates are lifted into route-decision certification. |
| Requirements and experimental design | Translate research claims into tests, baselines, ablations, metrics, artifacts, and validity threats. | Evaluation should measure the claim being made, so requirements must come before results. | Prevents route-speed, route-quality, certificate-quality, and artifact-quality claims from being conflated. |
| System architecture and implementation | Explain the FastAPI backend, Next.js frontend, OSRM/ORS/graph routing layer, strict assets, caches, artifacts, and provenance. | The algorithm is only publishable as an applied artifact if the software design actually realizes it. | Makes software design a research contribution, not implementation afterthought. |
| Evaluation, results, and discussion | Interpret test results, generated bundles, ablations, abstentions, runtime cost, limitations, and future validation layers. | Results are meaningful only after the design and experimental contract are known. | Shows which claims are supported, scoped, empirical, or left as future validation. |

This structure also gives signposting language for the final thesis. The introduction should tell the reader that the project proceeds from problem and literature to mathematics, then to algorithms, then to software design, then to evaluation. The architecture chapter should refer back to design implications from the literature: fail-closed readiness follows evidence-bounded certification; endpoint terminal types follow selective decision making; route substrate abstraction follows mature route-planning literature; provenance follows reproducible computational research; UI inspection panels follow the need for auditability in decision support.

#### AX97.3 Literature Review Expansion With Direct Source Links

The literature review should synthesize rather than list. The following source map gives the strongest literature route through the thesis.

**Design science and software design.** Hevner, March, Park, and Ram define design-science research in information systems as artifact creation and evaluation in response to relevant problems [Hevner et al. 2004](https://doi.org/10.2307/25148625). Peffers et al. give a design-science methodology with problem identification, objectives, design/development, demonstration, evaluation, and communication [Peffers et al. 2007](https://doi.org/10.2753/MIS0742-1222240302). Gregor and Hevner explain how to position design-science knowledge contributions for maximum impact [Gregor and Hevner 2013](https://doi.org/10.25300/MISQ/2013/37.2.01), and Wieringa frames design-science methodology for software and information systems [Wieringa 2014](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-662-43839-8). The project uses this tradition because its research contribution is a working artifact whose design choices are evaluated through source, tests, and generated evidence.

**Software architecture and stakeholder-facing design.** The architecture should be written as a set of views: functional route computation, information/provenance, development/module structure, deployment/runtime services, operational strictness, and evaluation artifacts. Viewpoint-based architecture documentation by Rozanski and Woods is useful because it treats architecture as stakeholder-specific views and cross-cutting perspectives [Rozanski and Woods, Software Systems Architecture](https://www.informit.com/articles/article.aspx?p=1766161). Bass, Clements, and Kazman's software-architecture tradition is also useful for explaining quality attributes such as modifiability, reliability, observability, and performance [Software Architecture in Practice](https://cs.gmu.edu/~rpettit/files/lectures/443L07.pdf). EB-RDC's software architecture is therefore part of the thesis: route decisions are only auditable because the backend, frontend, artifact store, strict preflight checks, and provenance surfaces were designed together.

**Road-network routing substrate.** Dijkstra supplies the classical nonnegative shortest-path baseline [Dijkstra 1959](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01386390). A* supplies heuristic search under lower-bound assumptions [Hart, Nilsson, and Raphael 1968](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1968.300136). Yen and Eppstein provide core K-shortest-path foundations [Yen 1971](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.17.11.712), [Eppstein 1998](https://doi.org/10.1137/S0097539795290477). Contraction hierarchies and customizable route planning explain why modern routing engines can serve road-network queries quickly [Geisberger et al. 2008](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68552-4_24), [Delling et al. 2015](https://doi.org/10.1287/trsc.2014.0579). Bast et al.'s survey is the best high-level source for modern transportation-network route planning [Bast et al. 2016](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.05140). This literature justifies using OSRM, ORS, and local graph search as substrate evidence rather than claiming the substrate itself as the novelty.

**Open route engines and map data.** OSRM's official documentation describes it as a high-performance routing engine for OpenStreetMap data [OSRM API documentation](https://project-osrm.org/docs/v26.4.0/), and the OSRM backend repository documents the MLD/CH preprocessing options and routing service [Project-OSRM/osrm-backend](https://github.com/Project-OSRM/osrm-backend). OpenRouteService documents directions/routing, extra information, and geospatial API surfaces [openrouteservice Directions Service](https://giscience.github.io/openrouteservice/api-reference/endpoints/directions/). OpenStreetMap is a community-built editable map and data source [OpenStreetMap About](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/About_OpenStreetMap). These sources are important because the thesis can cite the engines and data substrate directly while keeping EB-RDC's claim at the decision layer.

**Alternative routes, overlap, and choice sets.** K-shortest paths alone can produce near-duplicate routes. Alternative-route literature studies overlap, stretch, local optimality, and route-set quality [Akgun et al. 2000](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(99)00214-3), [Abraham et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.1145/2444016.2444019), [Bader et al. 2011](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-19754-3_5). EB-RDC's DCCS layer is better for this thesis objective because it asks which candidates are decision-critical as well as geometrically distinct. Overlap, mechanism disagreement, hidden-challenger risk, and certificate-criticality are decision evidence in addition to diversity heuristics.

**Freight route choice and operational trade-offs.** Long-haul truck route choice studies show that time and distance matter in observed behaviour [Knorring et al. 2005](https://doi.org/10.1177/0361198105192300106). Truck-route-choice work identifies route characteristics and information sources as decision factors [Sun et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.3141/2354-12). Tolling changes truck speed and routing decisions, and toll rate, travel time, and reliability can all be influential [Wang and Goodchild 2014](https://doi.org/10.3141/2411-14). Freight value-of-time studies show that time valuation varies by context and measurement method [Zamparini and Reggiani 2007](https://doi.org/10.1080/01441640701322834), [Binsuwadan et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tra.2020.06.002). These papers justify the thesis choice to expose time, money, CO2, toll, scenario, and reliability-style evidence rather than optimizing one hidden scalar.

**Multicriteria decision analysis and preference ambiguity.** Pareto reasoning and multicriteria optimization provide the language of nondominance, scalarisation, and trade-offs [Ehrgott 2005](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-27659-9), [Marler and Arora 2004](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00158-003-0368-6). VIKOR and TOPSIS-style compromise ranking explain one family of multicriteria route ranking [Opricovic and Tzeng 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(03)00020-1). SMAA is especially relevant because it studies uncertain or incomplete preferences by exploring weight spaces and acceptability [Lahdelma and Salminen 2001](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.49.3.444.11220). Minimax-regret elicitation explains why preference questions should be chosen to reduce decision regret rather than to collect every preference [Boutilier et al. 2006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2006.02.003). EB-RDC improves on a fixed weighted-sum design for this thesis because it preserves preference ambiguity and can return a certified set or preference abstention when a unique route is not justified.

**Robustness, stochastic routing, and tail risk.** Robust optimization supplies a formal language for uncertainty sets and conservative decisions [Ben-Tal and Nemirovski 1998](https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.23.4.769), [Bertsimas and Sim 2004](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.1030.0065). Stochastic programming and sample-average approximation explain why sampled worlds can support bounded empirical decisions [Shapiro, Dentcheva, and Ruszczynski](https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9780898718751). CVaR gives a standard tail-risk measure [Rockafellar and Uryasev 2000](https://doi.org/10.21314/JOR.2000.038), and risk-averse shortest-path studies show how CVaR and entropic risk appear in uncertain arc-length routing [Chicoisne, Ordonez, and Espinoza 2018](https://doi.org/10.1287/ijoc.2017.0795). EB-RDC's REFC layer is better for the current artifact because it keeps the evidence-world manifest explicit and replayable instead of making a broad uninspectable robust-optimization claim.

**Value of information, metareasoning, and algorithm selection.** Howard's information value theory explains why information should be valued by its decision impact [Howard 1966](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1966.300074). Russell and Wefald's decision-theoretic control of computation explains why computation itself can be selected as an action under resource limits [Russell and Wefald 1991](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(91)90015-C). Horvitz's bounded rationality/metareasoning work is relevant to deciding when to compute or stop [Horvitz 1987](https://erichorvitz.com/u87.htm), and Frazier et al.'s knowledge-gradient work is useful context for one-step information-value policies [Frazier et al. 2009](https://doi.org/10.1287/ijoc.1080.0314). EB-RDC's VOI-AD2R controller adapts this literature into a deterministic, auditable route-specific controller; the important design gain is that search, evidence, preference, resampling, stopping, and abstention are all explicit actions.

**Selective prediction, abstention, and confidence sets.** Chow's reject-option work establishes that refusal can be optimal under uncertainty [Chow 1970](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406). Selective classification develops risk-coverage reasoning for models that can abstain [El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/el-yaniv10a.html), [Geifman and El-Yaniv 2017](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/7073-selective-classification-for-deep-neural-networks), [SelectiveNet, Geifman and El-Yaniv 2019](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/geifman19a.html). Conformal prediction supplies calibrated prediction sets under exchangeability assumptions [Shafer and Vovk 2008](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/beta/papers/v9/shafer08a.html), [Angelopoulos and Bates 2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.07511). EB-RDC's route abstention is better for the present software artifact because it is typed by operational reason family and tied to evidence artifacts, support state, and remedy actions.

**Reproducibility, artifacts, and evidence discipline.** Peng argues for reproducible computational science [Peng 2011](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1213847), and Sandve et al. provide practical rules for reproducible computational research [Sandve et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285). The FAIR principles define findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability as data-management goals [Wilkinson et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18). ACM artifact badging separates available, functional, reusable, reproduced, and replicated artifacts [ACM Artifact Review and Badging](https://www.acm.org/publications/policies/artifact-review-and-badging-current). This literature justifies the repository's unusually heavy emphasis on manifests, run bundles, theorem maps, claim matrices, docs checks, and generated reviewer packages.

#### AX97.4 Algorithm And Code Source Attribution Audit

The final thesis should be explicit about method provenance. The standard algorithms and mathematical ideas below should be cited whenever they appear in the thesis. The original claim should be worded as adaptation, composition, constraint design, artifact design, or route-specific decision-contract design, with the standard algorithm families presented as cited foundations.

| Local surface | Standard source family to cite | What is adapted in this repository | Safe thesis wording |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `_dijkstra_shortest_path` and optional `heuristic_fn` in `backend/app/k_shortest.py` | Dijkstra shortest paths [Dijkstra 1959](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01386390), A* [Hart et al. 1968](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1968.300136) | Adds route-specific bounded state, deadlines, max hops, transition-state constraints, repeat limits, banned nodes/edges, and a local admissibility warning. | "The project implements Dijkstra/A*-style bounded candidate search as a route-evidence generator." |
| `yen_k_shortest_paths_with_stats` in `backend/app/k_shortest.py` | Yen K-shortest loopless paths [Yen 1971](https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.17.11.712); Eppstein as related K-shortest literature [Eppstein 1998](https://doi.org/10.1137/S0097539795290477) | Adds detour caps, candidate pool limits, state budgets, deadlines, termination diagnostics, and edge-cost caching for route evidence. | "The project adapts Yen-style K-shortest generation for bounded route-candidate evidence." |
| DCCS objective/diversity terms | Multiobjective diversification and crowding [Deb et al. 2002](https://doi.org/10.1109/4235.996017), alternative-route overlap/stretch literature [Akgun et al. 2000](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(99)00214-3), [Abraham et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.1145/2444016.2444019) | Changes the selection question from "which paths are diverse" to "which candidates are decision-critical for certification." | "DCCS is a thesis-specific decision-critical candidate screening heuristic built from cited route-diversity and multicriteria ideas." |
| Weighted sums, Tchebycheff/VIKOR, Pareto and epsilon filtering | Multicriteria optimization [Ehrgott 2005](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-27659-9), VIKOR/TOPSIS [Opricovic and Tzeng 2004](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(03)00020-1), epsilon-constraint [Haimes et al. 1971](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSMC.1971.4308298) | Uses these methods as transparent route-ranking/frontier tools, then passes the result to certification rather than treating score as final truth. | "The project uses standard MCDA methods as interpretable scoring/frontier components." |
| REFC sampled evidence worlds | Stochastic programming/SAA [Shapiro et al.](https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9780898718751), global sensitivity/stress testing [Saltelli et al. 2008](https://doi.org/10.1002/9780470725184), confidence sequences [Howard et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1214/20-AOS1991) | Builds route-specific bounded worlds, support metadata, fragility maps, sampled-world manifests, and certificate summaries. | "REFC is a bounded evidence-world certification layer over generated route frontiers." |
| CVaR and entropic/tail-risk summaries | CVaR [Rockafellar and Uryasev 2000](https://doi.org/10.21314/JOR.2000.038), risk-averse shortest paths [Chicoisne et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1287/ijoc.2017.0795) | Computes empirical tail-risk summaries for generated candidates and uses them as route-decision evidence. | "The project uses standard tail-risk concepts as measured route-evidence features." |
| Preference state, possible-best/necessary-best, preference queries | SMAA [Lahdelma and Salminen 2001](https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.49.3.444.11220), minimax regret elicitation [Boutilier et al. 2006](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2006.02.003) | Preserves compatible preference regions and query traces in the route-decision package. | "Preference logic adapts incomplete-preference reasoning to freight route certification." |
| VOI-AD2R | Value of information [Howard 1966](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1966.300074), metareasoning [Russell and Wefald 1991](https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(91)90015-C), knowledge-gradient context [Frazier et al. 2009](https://doi.org/10.1287/ijoc.1080.0314) | Uses a deterministic value-per-cost surrogate to select search/evidence/preference/resampling/stop actions. | "VOI-AD2R is an auditable route-specific metareasoning controller." |
| Typed abstention | Reject option [Chow 1970](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406), selective classification [El-Yaniv and Wiener 2010](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/el-yaniv10a.html), SelectiveNet [Geifman and El-Yaniv 2019](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/geifman19a.html) | Converts refusal into operational route-decision reason families and remedy actions. | "Typed abstention adapts selective-decision ideas to route recommendations." |
| Artifact/provenance/evaluation bundles | Reproducible research [Peng 2011](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1213847), [Sandve et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285), FAIR [Wilkinson et al. 2016](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18), ACM artifacts [ACM Artifact Review and Badging](https://www.acm.org/publications/policies/artifact-review-and-badging-current) | Treats evidence, manifests, sidecars, and claim ledgers as first-class research outputs. | "The evaluation is artifact-led and locally reproducible under recorded assumptions." |

The method-audit conclusion is: the thesis should cite standard methods generously and claim originality in the route-specific composition, bounded software contract, implementation choices, evidence artifacts, and terminal semantics. That is more impressive than claiming ownership of known algorithms because it shows scholarship and protects the paper from an obvious reviewer objection.

#### AX97.5 Code Snippets That Show The Source Attribution Boundary

The route-candidate generator explicitly implements Dijkstra/A*-style search with local constraints. The code comment already cites A* and states the admissibility condition, which is exactly the right thesis posture:

```python
# backend/app/k_shortest.py
def _dijkstra_shortest_path(..., heuristic_fn: HeuristicFn | None = None, ...):
    # When `heuristic_fn` is provided, this becomes an A* search over the
    # augmented state space. Optimality still relies on the heuristic being
    # admissible / consistent:
    # Hart, Nilsson, Raphael (1968) https://doi.org/10.1109/TSSC.1968.300136
    initial_h = max(0.0, float(heuristic_fn(start))) if heuristic_fn is not None else 0.0
```

This snippet should be discussed as an implementation of cited shortest-path search. The thesis-specific part is the bounded augmented state space: `max_hops`, `max_state_budget`, `max_repeat_per_node`, `max_cost_limit`, `transition_state_fn`, `deadline_monotonic_s`, and termination diagnostics. Those additions make graph search serve EB-RDC's evidence contract.

The K-shortest layer similarly cites Yen and then adds route-evidence diagnostics:

```python
# backend/app/k_shortest.py
# Yen's loop repeatedly evaluates root-path costs for many spur branches.
# Cache edge costs once so root-prefix costs are O(1) per spur index instead
# of repeatedly scanning adjacency lists.
#
# Reference (original K-shortest loopless paths algorithm):
# Yen (1971), Management Science 17(11), 712-716
# https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.17.11.712
edge_cost_lookup: dict[tuple[str, str], float] = {}
```

The contribution is that the repository wraps Yen-style spur generation with deadlines, detour caps, state budgets, no-path reasons, and candidate-pool controls so K-shortest paths become controlled evidence for downstream certification.

DCCS is thesis-specific, but the code is explicit that it borrows from multiobjective diversity ideas:

```python
# backend/app/decision_critical.py
# DCCS is thesis-specific, but its objective-space coverage and diversity terms
# borrow from standard multi-objective search ideas such as normalized
# nearest-neighbour spacing and crowding/diversification; see Deb et al.,
# "A fast and elitist multiobjective genetic algorithm: NSGA-II",
# https://doi.org/10.1109/4235.996017 .
```

The DCCS flip transform is an auditable deterministic surrogate rather than a learned probability model. That is a key originality boundary:

```python
# backend/app/decision_critical.py
raw = (
    (config.flip_objective_weight * objective_gap)
    + (config.flip_mechanism_weight * mechanism_gap)
    + (config.flip_overlap_weight * (1.0 - overlap))
    + (config.flip_stretch_weight * max(0.0, stretch - 1.0))
    + (config.flip_confidence_weight * confidence)
    + viability
)
raw = config.flip_bias + raw
return 1.0 / (1.0 + math.exp(-config.flip_logistic_scale * raw))
```

This is better than a hidden ranking model for the thesis because every term has a route-decision interpretation. `objective_gap` measures whether a challenger can improve objectives; `mechanism_gap` measures whether the candidate comes from a different evidence mechanism; `1.0 - overlap` rewards non-duplicate route shape; `stretch - 1.0` lets detour contribute without making every detour attractive; confidence prevents unsupported proxies from dominating; and `viability` penalizes non-improving challengers. The logistic link turns those terms into a bounded priority score for budget allocation.

The DCCS configuration shows how the variables were tuned to reflect the thesis objective:

```python
# backend/app/decision_critical.py
near_duplicate_threshold: float = 0.82
objective_gap_weight: float = 1.0
mechanism_gap_weight: float = 0.45
overlap_penalty_weight: float = 1.25
stretch_penalty_weight: float = 0.5
flip_bias: float = -0.35
flip_logistic_scale: float = 2.35
flip_objective_weight: float = 1.25
flip_mechanism_weight: float = 0.85
flip_overlap_weight: float = 0.70
flip_stretch_weight: float = 0.35
flip_confidence_weight: float = 0.55
flip_viable_bonus: float = 0.30
flip_nonimprovement_penalty: float = 1.10
```

The important explanation is that the largest flip weight is on objective gap because close objective competition is the strongest reason to refine a challenger. Mechanism gap receives a large but smaller weight because different generation mechanisms can reveal hidden decision evidence. Overlap matters because near-duplicates are less informative. Stretch matters less because detours can be useful but should not dominate by being merely different. The negative bias and non-improvement penalty prevent every candidate from being treated as critical. This is better than a naive "refine the shortest K" design because it spends route computation where the decision may change.

REFC is also source-aware in code. It positions evidence worlds as bounded stress testing and sample-average style evidence:

```python
# backend/app/evidence_certification.py
# REFC uses bounded stress-world analysis rather than an unconstrained noise
# model. The construction is closer to global sensitivity analysis and explicit
# stress testing than to learned simulation; see Saltelli et al.
#
# The route certificate itself is an empirical winner-frequency estimate over
# those worlds, following the sample-average-approximation perspective used in
# stochastic programming.
```

The state and family effects are explicit rather than hidden:

```python
# backend/app/evidence_certification.py
DEFAULT_STATE_EFFECTS: dict[str, tuple[float, float, float]] = {
    "nominal": (0.00, 0.00, 0.00),
    "mildly_stale": (0.040, 0.030, 0.032),
    "low_confidence": (0.078, 0.062, 0.056),
    "proxy": (0.185, 0.152, 0.132),
    "refreshed": (-0.038, -0.030, -0.024),
}
DEFAULT_FAMILY_SENSITIVITY: dict[str, tuple[float, float, float]] = {
    "scenario": (0.82, 0.34, 0.24),
    "toll": (0.05, 1.00, 0.12),
    "terrain": (0.18, 0.22, 0.82),
}
```

This is better than a single undifferentiated noise parameter because it lets the thesis explain how evidence state changes time, money, and CO2 differently by family. A stale traffic/scenario source should not perturb the same objectives as a toll tariff or terrain/emissions source. The implementation makes that modelling choice inspectable.

VOI-AD2R cites metareasoning and then implements finite route-decision budgets:

```python
# backend/app/voi_controller.py
# VOI-AD2R uses a deterministic myopic value-per-cost controller. The design is
# inspired by decision-theoretic control of computation and one-step
# value-of-information policies rather than by learned RL.

class VOIConfig:
    certificate_threshold: float = 0.67
    stop_threshold: float = 0.02
    search_budget: int = 3
    evidence_budget: int = 2
    max_iterations: int = 8
    top_k_refine: int = 2
    resample_increment: int = 25
    lambda_certificate: float = 0.60
    lambda_margin: float = 0.25
    lambda_frontier: float = 0.15
```

The thesis should explain these constants as a budgeted decision policy. `certificate_threshold` defines the empirical support level used by the controller. `stop_threshold` prevents wasting computation on negligible expected gain. `search_budget`, `evidence_budget`, `max_iterations`, `top_k_refine`, and `resample_increment` make cost visible and bounded. `lambda_certificate`, `lambda_margin`, and `lambda_frontier` weight the controller toward certificate improvement while still valuing margin improvement and frontier discovery. This is better than exhaustive refinement because it makes the trade-off between decision value and computation measurable.

Typed abstention is another source-attribution point: the idea inherits from reject-option decision making, but the route-specific reason vocabulary is implemented here:

```python
# backend/app/abstention.py
ABSTENTION_REASON_CODES = (
    "typed_abstention_recommended",
    "uncertified_due_to_search",
    "uncertified_due_to_evidence",
    "uncertified_due_to_preference",
    "uncertified_due_to_out_of_support_world_model",
    "uncertified_due_to_budget",
    "uncertified_due_to_model_assumption",
)
```

This is better than a generic error because each reason maps to a different remedy family. Search abstention suggests widening or refining candidate search; evidence abstention suggests refreshing or auditing evidence; preference abstention suggests eliciting preferences; support-world abstention suggests expanding the support model; budget abstention suggests budget review; model-assumption abstention suggests assumption review. That is the route-decision adaptation of selective refusal.

#### AX97.6 How EB-RDC Changes Standard Equations

The standard shortest-path equation is:

```text
p* = argmin_p sum_{e in p} c_e
```

A standard weighted route scorer is:

```text
r* = argmin_r  w_time * time(r) + w_money * money(r) + w_co2 * co2(r)
```

EB-RDC changes the output object:

```text
T(q) = certify_or_abstain(K_raw, F, W, P, E, B, Theta)
T(q) in { certified_singleton(r*), certified_set(C), typed_abstention(k) }
```

This is the central mathematical shift. The project still uses paths, objective vectors, scalar scores, and Pareto/frontier concepts, but it makes them intermediate evidence rather than the final answer. The final answer depends on candidate evidence `K_raw`, refined frontier `F`, bounded evidence worlds `W`, preference state `P`, evidence/support state `E`, finite budgets `B`, and thresholds `Theta`. This change is better for the thesis objective because it represents the decision process that a freight operator actually needs: the route, the evidence supporting it, the remaining ambiguity, and the reason a route may be uncertified.

DCCS can be described as a candidate-value surrogate:

```text
flip_score(c) = sigma(alpha_0
    + alpha_1 objective_gap(c)
    + alpha_2 mechanism_gap(c)
    + alpha_3 (1 - overlap(c))
    + alpha_4 max(0, stretch(c) - 1)
    + alpha_5 confidence(c)
    + viability(c))
```

The mathematical change from a standard K-shortest list is that DCCS prioritizes *decision impact*. A candidate is valuable when it can change the certificate, expose a hidden challenger, improve frontier recall, or shrink preference ambiguity. That is why DCCS is better than blindly refining the shortest or most geometrically different routes.

REFC can be written as a bounded-world winner-support estimate:

```text
support(r) = (1 / |W|) * sum_{w in W} 1[r wins under world w]
certificate(r*) = support(r*) >= tau_cert
```

The thesis-specific change is that `W` is a replayable manifest of evidence states, family sensitivities, support conditions, and route exposures. That makes the certificate auditable and bounded.

VOI-AD2R can be written as a myopic action-value rule:

```text
a_t = argmax_a  predicted_decision_gain(a | state_t) / (cost(a) + epsilon)
stop when max_a value_per_cost(a) < tau_stop or budgets are exhausted
```

The thesis-specific change is that the action set is route-decision native: refine DCCS candidates, refresh evidence, increase stochastic samples, ask preference questions, stop, or abstain. This is a better applied design than always refining everything because it makes decision effort part of the method.

#### AX97.7 Direct Abstract Text To Reuse In The Thesis

The abstract in the opening of this report is the master abstract, but the following shorter version can be reused in a submitted thesis:

```text
This thesis presents WhatIf Freight Router, an auditable freight-route decision system that turns route recommendation from a path-return task into an evidence-bounded decision problem. The project contributes Evidence-Bounded Route-Decision Certification (EB-RDC), an implemented architecture that composes mature routing substrates with decision-critical candidate screening, bounded evidence-world certification, preference-state preservation, value-of-information action control, and typed abstention. The system is implemented as a Python/FastAPI backend, a Next.js frontend, OSRM/ORS-backed routing services, strict UK-focused model assets, and artifact/provenance stores that expose route candidates, certificates, sampled-world manifests, support summaries, VOI traces, and terminal reason codes. The thesis is organised from problem and literature to mathematics, algorithms, requirements, architecture, and evaluation because each layer defines the objects needed to evaluate the next. Evaluation uses tests, endpoint parity checks, docs consistency checks, generated reviewer bundles, theorem maps, claim matrices, and checked lane artifacts. The contribution is strongest as an applied design-science artifact: it demonstrates how route engines can be lifted into a decision contract that returns certified singleton routes, certified sets, or typed abstentions under recorded candidate, evidence, preference, support, budget, and model assumptions.
```

This abstract gives enough signposting to satisfy the professor's feedback: it says what problem is solved, why software design matters, what EB-RDC designs, how chapters are organised, how evaluation works, and what "better" means in the thesis.
